Seccomp default graduates to GA for improved container security, and pod scheduling readiness provides better control over when pods are ready to schedule. Key features include freeze on k8s.gcr.io, multiple service CIDRs, and parallel image pulls.

actionRequired.description:
Give terminal phase correctly to all pods that will not be restarted. 

In particular, assign Failed phase to pods which are deleted while pending. Also, assign a terminal 
phase (Succeeded or Failed, depending on the exit statuses of the pod containers) to pods which
are deleted while running.

This fixes the issue for jobs using pod failure policy (with JobPodFailurePolicy and PodDisruptionConditions 
feature gates enabled) that their pods could get stuck in the pending phase when deleted.

Users who maintain controllers which relied on the fact that pods with RestartPolicy=Always
never enter the Succeeded phase may need to adapt their controllers. This is because as a consequence of 
the change pods which use RestartPolicy=Always may end up in the Succeeded phase in two scenarios: pod 
deletion and graceful node shutdown.
actionRequired.author: mimowo

enrichment.title: Assign correct terminal phase to deleted pods
enrichment.summary: Pods that are deleted without restart now receive a proper terminal phase (Failed for pending deletions, Succeeded or Failed for running deletions) based on container exit status.
enrichment.action: Update any controllers or custom logic that assume RestartPolicy=Always pods never reach the Succeeded phase; handle possible Succeeded status on pod deletion or graceful node shutdown.

where BUILTIN\Users may be able to read container logs and NT

securityInformation.title: Bypassing mountable secrets policy imposed by the ServiceAccount admission plugin
securityInformation.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where users may be able to launch containers that bypass the mountable secrets policy enforced by the ServiceAccount admission plugin when using containers, init containers, and ephemeral containers with the envFrom field populated.

securityInformation.title: Insufficient input sanitization in in-tree storage plugin leads to privilege escalation on Windows nodes
securityInformation.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a user that can create pods and persistent volumes on Windows nodes may be able to escalate to admin privileges on those nodes. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they are using an in-tree storage plugin for Windows nodes.

securityInformation.title: Insufficient input sanitization on Windows nodes leads to privilege escalation
securityInformation.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a user that can create pods on Windows nodes may be able to escalate to admin privileges on those nodes. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they include Windows nodes.

securityInformation.title: Insufficient input sanitization on Windows nodes leads to privilege escalation
securityInformation.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where a user that can create pods on Windows nodes may be able to escalate to admin privileges on those nodes. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if they include Windows nodes.

securityInformation.title: Bypassing enforce mountable secrets policy imposed by the ServiceAccount admission plugin
securityInformation.description:
A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where users may be able to launch containers that bypass the mountable secrets policy enforced by the ServiceAccount admission plugin when using ephemeral containers. The policy ensures pods running with a service account may only reference secrets specified in the service account's secrets field. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if the ServiceAccount admission plugin and the `kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets` annotation are used together with ephemeral containers.

**Note**: This only impacts the cluster if the ServiceAccount admission plugin is used (most cluster should have this on by default as recommended in https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/admission-controllers/#serviceaccount), the `kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets` annotation is used by a service account (this annotation is not added by default), and Pods are using ephemeral containers.

apiChange.description:
`PodSpec.Container.Resources` became mutable for CPU and memory resource types.
- `PodSpec.Container.ResizePolicy` (new object) gives users control over how their containers are resized.
- `PodStatus.Resize` status describes the state of a requested Pod resize.
- `PodStatus.ResourcesAllocated` describes node resources allocated to Pod.
- `PodStatus.Resources` describes node resources applied to running containers by CRI.
- `UpdateContainerResources` CRI API now supports both Linux and Windows.
apiChange.author: vinaykul
apiChange.userFacingChange:
In-place resize feature for Kubernetes Pods
  - Changed the Pod API so that the `resources` defined for containers are mutable for `cpu` and `memory` resource types.
  - Added `resizePolicy` for containers in a pod to allow users control over how their containers are resized.
  - Added `allocatedResources` field to container status in pod status that describes the node resources allocated to a pod.
  - Added `resources` field to container status that reports actual resources applied to running containers.
  - Added `resize` field to pod status that describes the state of a requested pod resize.

  For details, see KEPs below. ([#102884](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/102884), [@vinaykul](https://github.com/vinaykul)) [SIG API Machinery, Apps, Instrumentation, Node, Scheduling and Testing]

enrichment.problem: Container resource requests and limits for CPU and memory were immutable, forcing users to delete and recreate Pods to change sizes, which caused downtime and complex rollout procedures.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that needs to adjust CPU or memory of running containers—e.g., stateful services, batch jobs, or autoscaling use cases—can now resize pods in place instead of recreating them.
enrichment.fix: Made `PodSpec.Container.Resources` mutable for CPU and memory, introduced `PodSpec.Container.ResizePolicy` to control resize behavior, added status fields (`Resize`, `ResourcesAllocated`, `Resources`) to expose resize progress and actual allocated resources, and extended the CRI `UpdateContainerResources` API to support in‑place updates on both Linux and Windows nodes.
enrichment.impact: Enables live, in‑place scaling of Pods without disruption, simplifying operations, reducing downtime, and allowing more responsive resource management for both Linux and Windows workloads.

apiChange.description:
Introduces new alpha functionality to the reflector, allowing user to enable API streaming.

To activate this feature, users can set the `ENABLE_CLIENT_GO_WATCH_LIST_ALPHA` environmental variable.
It is important to note that the server must support streaming for this feature to function properly.
If streaming is not supported by the server, the reflector will revert to the previous method
of obtaining data through LIST/WATCH semantics.
apiChange.author: p0lyn0mial
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Introduces new alpha functionality to the reflector, allowing user to enable API streaming.

To activate this feature, users can set the `ENABLE_CLIENT_GO_WATCH_LIST_ALPHA` environmental variable.
It is important to note that the server must support streaming for this feature to function properly.
If streaming is not supported by the server, the reflector will revert to the previous method
of obtaining data through LIST/WATCH semantics.

enrichment.problem: Client-go reflectors could only retrieve data via LIST/WATCH semantics; there was no way to use the newer API streaming watch-list feature, limiting efficiency and latency for controllers and other watchers.
enrichment.affected: Clients using client-go reflectors (e.g., controllers, operators) that enable the env var; requires apiserver support for streaming watch-list.
enrichment.fix: Adds an alpha feature that enables API streaming for the reflector. Users can turn it on by setting the ENABLE_CLIENT_GO_WATCH_LIST_ALPHA environment variable. When enabled, the reflector will use the streaming watch-list API if the apiserver supports it, otherwise it gracefully falls back to the traditional LIST/WATCH path.
enrichment.impact: Controllers and other components that rely on client-go watches can benefit from lower latency and reduced load when streaming is available, while maintaining compatibility with servers that do not yet support the streaming endpoint.

apiChange.description:
Implemented API streaming for the `watch-cache`

When `sendInitialEvents` `ListOption` is set together with `watch=true`, it begins the watch stream with synthetic init events followed by a synthetic "Bookmark" after which the server continues streaming events.
apiChange.author: p0lyn0mial
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Implements API for streaming for the watch-cache

When sendInitialEvents ListOption is set together with watch=true, it begins the watch stream with synthetic init events followed by a synthetic "Bookmark" after which the server continues streaming events.

enrichment.problem: When a client requested a watch with the `sendInitialEvents` list option, the watch-cache could not stream the initial synthetic events followed by a bookmark, forcing clients to handle inconsistent initial state or miss the bookmark semantics.
enrichment.affected: Any workload or tool that watches resources using the watch‑cache with `sendInitialEvents`, including controllers and kubectl.
enrichment.fix: Added API streaming support for the watch‑cache. When `sendInitialEvents` is set together with `watch=true`, the server now starts the watch stream with synthetic init events, emits a synthetic "Bookmark" event, and then continues streaming live events.
enrichment.impact: Clients that use `watch=true` with `sendInitialEvents` (e.g., controllers, kubectl, custom operators) now receive a complete initial snapshot and a bookmark, improving watch reliability, reducing extra list calls, and enabling more efficient event processing.

apiChange.description:
`kubelet`: migrated `--container-runtime-endpoint` and `--image-service-endpoint`
to kubelet config
apiChange.author: pacoxu
apiChange.userFacingChange: kubelet: migrate "--container-runtime-endpoint" and "--image-service-endpoint" to kubelet config

enrichment.problem: The kubelet command-line flags `--container-runtime-endpoint` and `--image-service-endpoint` were removed and are now only configurable via the kubelet config file, which can break clusters that still set these flags directly.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where kubelet is started with `--container-runtime-endpoint` or `--image-service-endpoint` flags; those scripts will fail or the flags will be ignored after the change.
enrichment.fix: The two flags have been migrated to the kubelet configuration API. Users must now specify `containerRuntime.endpoint` and `imageService.endpoint` fields in the kubelet config file instead of using the CLI flags.
enrichment.impact: Administrators need to update their kubelet startup scripts or provisioning tools to use the config file. This unifies node configuration, improves configurability, and prevents hidden flag usage, but may require a one‑time migration for existing deployments.

apiChange.description: `cacheSize` field in `EncryptionConfiguration` is not supported for KMSv2 provider
apiChange.author: aramase
apiChange.userFacingChange: cacheSize field in EncryptionConfiguration is not supported for KMSv2 provider

issueContext.title: [KMSv2] Use expiring cache
issueContext.body:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d581cc90adba6c84919738841fe3e07302d53e33/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/value/encrypt/envelope/kmsv2/envelope.go#L95-L99

/sig auth

enrichment.problem: `cacheSize` was accepted in the EncryptionConfiguration for the KMSv2 provider even though the provider does not support a configurable cache size, leading to users configuring a field that has no effect and possible confusion about encryption performance.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that enable envelope encryption with a KMSv2 provider and set the `cacheSize` field in their EncryptionConfiguration.
enrichment.fix: Validation for EncryptionConfiguration now rejects the `cacheSize` field when the KMSv2 provider is used, removing the unsupported option and documenting that KMSv2 uses its own expiring cache.
enrichment.impact: Prevents misconfiguration of encryption at rest, clarifies expected behavior for KMSv2, and avoids users relying on a non‑functional cache setting that could have caused performance misunderstandings.

apiChange.description:
Added a new alpha API: ClusterTrustBundle (`certificates.k8s.io/v1alpha1`).
A ClusterTrustBundle may be used to distribute [X.509](https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-X.509) trust anchors to workloads within the cluster.
apiChange.author: ahmedtd
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Added a new alpha API: ClusterTrustBundle (`certificates.k8s.io/v1alpha1`).
A ClusterTrustBundle may be used to distribute [X.509](https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-X.509) trust anchors to workloads within the cluster.

enrichment.problem: Clusters had no built‑in mechanism to distribute X.509 trust anchors (certificate authority bundles) to workloads, making it hard to manage trust for internal services and third‑party components.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and any workloads that need to verify TLS connections using custom or internal CA bundles.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the alpha ClusterTrustBundle API (certificates.k8s.io/v1alpha1) that lets administrators create and manage trust‑anchor bundles as cluster‑scoped resources, which can then be consumed by workloads.
enrichment.impact: Provides a standardized way to propagate trusted root certificates across the cluster, simplifying secure communication for workloads and paving the way for future features that rely on shared trust anchors.

apiChange.description: Migrated the `DaemonSet` controller (within `kube-controller-manager`) to use [contextual logging](https://k8s.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/system-logs/#contextual-logging)
apiChange.userFacingChange: Migrated the DaemonSet controller (within `kube-controller-manager) to use [contextual logging](https://k8s.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/system-logs/#contextual-logging)

enrichment.problem: The DaemonSet controller logs lacked contextual information, making it difficult for operators to correlate log entries and debug DaemonSet behavior.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and developers who monitor or debug DaemonSet controller activity.
enrichment.fix: Migrated the DaemonSet controller (running in kube-controller-manager) to use the new contextual logging framework, adding structured fields (e.g., controller name, namespace, DaemonSet name) to its log messages.
enrichment.impact: Operators and developers can now filter and search DaemonSet controller logs more effectively, improving troubleshooting speed and overall observability of DaemonSet operations.

apiChange.description:
Added new option to the `InterPodAffinity` scheduler plugin to ignore existing
pods` preferred inter-pod affinities if the incoming pod has no preferred inter-pod
affinities. This option can be used as an optimization for higher scheduling throughput
(at the cost of an occasional pod being scheduled non-optimally/violating existing
pods preferred inter-pod affinities). To enable this scheduler option, set the
`InterPodAffinity` scheduler plugin arg `ignorePreferredTermsOfExistingPods: true`
apiChange.author: danielvegamyhre
apiChange.userFacingChange: Added new option to the InterPodAffinity scheduler plugin to ignore existing pods` preferred inter-pod affinities if the incoming pod has no preferred inter-pod affinities. This option can be used as an optimization for higher scheduling throughput (at the cost of an occasional pod being scheduled non-optimally/violating existing pods' preferred inter-pod affinities). To enable this scheduler option, set the InterPodAffinity scheduler plugin arg "ignorePreferredTermsOfExistingPods: true".

issueContext.title: An option to disable Preferred Inter-pod affinity of existing pods
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

An option in the scheduler's ComponentConfig to ignore calculating preferences of exiting pods' affinity rules for the general case, and consider them only if the incoming pod has inter pod affinities.  In most cases this is sufficient because pods set inter-pod affinity against each other.

In the past we optimized this case by tracking only pods with inter-pod affinity, but to achieve the next level of scheduling throughput, optionally disabling this feature will be useful.

Specifically, I am suggesting that [PreScore](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3e26e104bdf9d0dc3c4046d6350b93557c67f3f4/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/interpodaffinity/scoring.go#L126) exits early if this option is enabled and the pod has no inter-pod affinities.

### Why is this needed?

To optimize for higher scheduling throughput.

/sig scheduling

/cc @Huang-Wei @alculquicondor

enrichment.problem: The InterPodAffinity scheduler plugin always evaluates preferred inter‑pod affinity terms of existing pods, even when the incoming pod has no such preferences, adding unnecessary computation and limiting scheduling throughput.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that enable the new option, especially those with large numbers of pods and workloads sensitive to scheduler latency. The change only affects scheduling behavior when the flag is turned on.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new scheduler plugin argument `ignorePreferredTermsOfExistingPods: true`. When enabled, the plugin skips evaluating existing pods' preferred inter‑pod affinity terms if the pod being scheduled has no preferred affinities, reducing scoring work.
enrichment.impact: Improves scheduling throughput and reduces scheduler CPU usage for clusters with many pods, at the trade‑off that occasional pods may be placed in a way that violates other pods' preferred affinities.

apiChange.description: Added warnings about workload resources (Pods, ReplicaSets, Deployments, Jobs, CronJobs, or ReplicationControllers) whose names are not valid DNS labels.
apiChange.author: thockin

issueContext.title: StatefulSet name accepts DNS subdomain standard, but Pods controlled by StatefulSet accepts DNS label standard
issueContext.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:

Names allowed for Pods, Deployment, StatefulSet follow DNS subdomain name defined in RFC 1123. 
Pods controlled by Deployment follows DNS subdomain name standard as well. 

However, Pod controlled by StatefuSet is following DNS label standard.
StatefulSet allows names with "." , but Pods created by the StatefulSet fails with error --

```
Events:
  Type     Reason        Age                     From                    Message
  ----     ------        ----                    ----                    -------
  Warning  FailedCreate  4m23s (x17 over 9m51s)  statefulset-controller  create Pod sts1-vol.1-0 in StatefulSet sts1-vol.1 failed error: Pod "sts1-vol.1-0" is invalid: spec.hostname: Invalid value: "sts1-vol.1-0": a DNS-1123 label must consist of lower case alphanumeric characters or '-', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character (e.g. 'my-name',  or '123-abc', regex used for validation is '[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?')
```


#### What you expected to happen:

Since "." character is allowed in the StatefulSet name, Pod replicas controlled by the StatefulSet should allow "." character as well. 
If "." is not possible for Pods controlled by StatefulSet, then StatefulSet creation should fail for "." character in the name. 

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

```
$ kubectl create -f 1sts-1vol-dot.yaml -n test
persistentvolumeclaim/pvc-3 created
statefulset.apps/sts1-vol.1 created
```


YAML FILE -->
```cat 1sts-1vol-dot.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: pvc-3
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
  s

enrichment.problem: Workload resources with names that do not conform to the DNS label format could be created without clear feedback, leading to creation failures (e.g., Pods from StatefulSets) and user confusion.
enrichment.affected: Anyone creating or managing workload resources (Pods, ReplicaSets, Deployments, Jobs, CronJobs, ReplicationControllers) with names that contain characters not allowed by the DNS‑1123 label standard.
enrichment.fix: The API now emits warnings for Pods, ReplicaSets, Deployments, Jobs, CronJobs, and ReplicationControllers whose names are not valid DNS labels, alerting users to the naming issue before the resource is rejected.
enrichment.impact: Users receive early, actionable feedback when using invalid names, preventing deployment failures and reducing troubleshooting time for naming‑related errors.

apiChange.description:
Enabled usage of `kube-proxy`, `kube-scheduler` and `kubelet` HTTP APIs for changing the logging
 verbosity at runtime for JSON output.
apiChange.author: pohly
apiChange.userFacingChange: kube-proxy, kube-scheduler and kubelet have HTTP APIs for changing the logging verbosity at runtime. This now also works for JSON output.

enrichment.problem: When kube-proxy, kube-scheduler, and kubelet were configured to emit logs in JSON format, their runtime HTTP APIs could not adjust the logging verbosity, limiting dynamic observability for JSON‑based log pipelines.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running kube-proxy, kube-scheduler, or kubelet with JSON logging enabled and using the HTTP API to adjust log levels at runtime.
enrichment.fix: Extended the HTTP `/debug/pprof/...` style logging‑verbosity endpoints for kube-proxy, kube-scheduler, and kubelet to support JSON output, allowing users to raise or lower log levels at runtime without restarting the component.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now dynamically tune the detail of JSON‑formatted logs for these core components, enabling quicker troubleshooting and tighter control of log volume in environments that ship logs to centralized JSON log aggregators.

apiChange.description:
A terminating pod on a node that is not caused by preemption no longer prevents `kube-scheduler` from preempting pods on that node
- Rename `PreemptionByKubeScheduler` to `PreemptionByScheduler`
apiChange.author: Huang-Wei
apiChange.userFacingChange:
- A terminating pod on a node that is not caused by preemption won't prevent kube-scheduler from preempting pods on that node
- Rename 'PreemptionByKubeScheduler' to 'PreemptionByScheduler'

issueContext.title: revisit `PodEligibleToPreemptOthers` func from default preemption
issueContext.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:
As the comment here explained, the logic of `PodEligibleToPreemptOthers` func from default preemption is not accurate enough, the deleting pod should be a preemption victim instead of normal deleted pod.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/104030#discussion_r680138858

Quote from @Huang-Wei 

> PodEligibleToPreemptOthers currently checks if a nominated node has low-priority terminating pods, then it assumes those terminating pods are preempted by the preemptor. It's actually not that accurate - we should verify the terminating pods are exactly preemption victims; otherwise a possible case is: the victims have been physically deleted, and the terminating pods are due to regular deletion.



#### What you expected to happen:
Refine the logic to make sure the deleting pod is actually a preemption victim.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

#### Anything else we need to know?:

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:

cc @alculquicondor 

/sig scheduling

enrichment.problem: The scheduler considered any terminating pod on a node as a preemption victim. When a pod was terminating for ordinary reasons (e.g., user‑initiated delete) it blocked kube‑scheduler from preempting other pods on that node, preventing high‑priority pods from being scheduled.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where normal pod deletions occurred on nodes that also needed preemptive scheduling; any workload relying on preemption could be delayed.
enrichment.fix: The preemption logic (PodEligibleToPreemptOthers) was updated to verify that terminating pods are actual preemption victims before treating them as such. The internal enum was also renamed from PreemptionByKubeScheduler to PreemptionByScheduler.
enrichment.impact: High‑priority pods can now be preempted on nodes even if unrelated pods are terminating, improving scheduling fairness and reducing unnecessary delays in workload placement.

apiChange.description: #### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:
apiChange.author: freddie400

enrichment.problem: Users lacked documentation and guidance on the new contextual logging capabilities, making it difficult to adopt and configure structured logs across components.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes users, developers, and operators who want to enable or configure contextual logging for better monitoring and debugging.
enrichment.fix: Added comprehensive documentation, including the KEP 3077 contextual logging proposal and usage examples, to clarify how to enable and use contextual logging in the cluster.
enrichment.impact: Improves observability by helping developers and operators understand and implement contextual logging, leading to more consistent and actionable logs across Kubernetes components.

apiChange.description: `k8s.io/component-base/logs` now also supports adding command line flags to a `flag.FlagSet`.
apiChange.author: pohly
apiChange.userFacingChange: k8s.io/component-base/logs now also supports adding command line flags to a flag.FlagSet.

enrichment.problem: The component-base logs package did not provide a way to register its logging-related command-line flags with a flag.FlagSet, making it difficult for components to expose and parse those flags automatically.
enrichment.affected: Developers and any Kubernetes component that imports k8s.io/component-base/logs and uses a flag.FlagSet for CLI flags.
enrichment.fix: The logs package now includes functionality to add its command‑line flags to any provided flag.FlagSet, enabling seamless flag registration and parsing.
enrichment.impact: Developers can now expose and configure logging flags through standard flag handling without custom code, simplifying component integration and improving consistency across the code base.

apiChange.description: `/metrics/slis` is now available for control plane components allowing you to scrape health check metrics.
apiChange.author: Richabanker
apiChange.userFacingChange: `/metrics/slis` is made available for control plane components allowing you to scrape health check metrics.

enrichment.problem: Control plane components did not expose a dedicated endpoint for Service Level Indicator (SLI) health check metrics, making it difficult for operators to scrape and monitor health metrics consistently across the control plane.
enrichment.affected: All control‑plane components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, and other core control‑plane services) that now expose the `/metrics/slis` endpoint.
enrichment.fix: Adds a `/metrics/slis` endpoint to control plane components, allowing them to expose health‑check related metrics that can be scraped by monitoring systems.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now collect SLI metrics from the control plane for better observability, alerting, and SLO tracking, improving reliability and troubleshooting of the Kubernetes control plane.

apiChange.description: Updated `KMSv2` to beta
apiChange.author: aramase
apiChange.userFacingChange: Update KMSv2 to beta

issueContext.body:

- [x] Update code references to use the beta API
- [x] Update validation to allow `v2beta1`
- [x] Check how status API checks will be done with `v2beta1`?

/triage accepted
/sig auth
/assign

enrichment.problem: The KMS v2 encryption integration only had an alpha API version without protobuf definitions, proper feature gate support, and validation for the v2beta1 version, limiting users from adopting a stable API for envelope encryption.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use KMS v2 for envelope encryption – primarily API server configurations and any workloads relying on encrypted secrets.
enrichment.fix: Implemented the v2beta1 KMS API protobuf generation, added a beta feature gate, updated all code references to use the new API, and extended validation to accept v2beta1 objects, making KMS v2 officially beta.
enrichment.impact: Users can now configure and use the KMS v2 encryption provider with a stable beta API, benefiting from better validation, feature‑gate control, and future compatibility, improving security and operational confidence.

apiChange.description: Encryption of API Server at rest configuration now allows the use of wildcards in the list of resources.  For example, *.* can be used to encrypt all resources, including all current and future custom resources.
apiChange.author: nilekhc
apiChange.userFacingChange: The API server's encryption at rest configuration now allows the use of wildcards in the list of resources.  For example, '*.*' can be used to encrypt all resources, including all current and future custom resources.

enrichment.problem: The encryption-at-rest configuration for the API server required an explicit list of resources, making it difficult to encrypt all resources and future custom resources, which could leave data unencrypted.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use API server encryption at rest, especially those with custom resources or that want to encrypt all resources.
enrichment.fix: The API server now accepts wildcards in the resource list (e.g., '*.*'), allowing administrators to encrypt every resource, including any current or future Custom Resource Definitions, with a single entry.
enrichment.impact: Simplifies encryption configuration, guarantees that all resources are encrypted by default, and protects against accidental exposure of new custom resources, improving cluster security and operational ease.

apiChange.description: kubelet: a "maxParallelImagePulls" field can now be specified in the kubelet configuration file to control how many image pulls the kubelet can perform in parallel.
apiChange.author: ruiwen-zhao

enrichment.problem: Kubelet had no configuration option to limit the number of concurrent image pulls, which could lead to resource contention, network saturation, or node instability when many pods start simultaneously.
enrichment.affected: All clusters using the kubelet, particularly those that run many pods that trigger image pulls at the same time.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `maxParallelImagePulls` field in the kubelet configuration file. Users can set this integer value to control how many image pull operations the kubelet can run in parallel.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now tune image pull concurrency to match node capacity, improving stability and performance, especially in large clusters or high‑scale rollouts.

apiChange.description: Enabled the `StatefulSetStartOrdinal` feature gate in beta
apiChange.author: pwschuurman
apiChange.userFacingChange: Enable the "StatefulSetStartOrdinal" feature gate in beta

enrichment.problem: StatefulSets could only start with ordinal 0, preventing users from creating workloads that need to begin at a higher ordinal (e.g., when migrating data or adding replicas with specific ordering).
enrichment.affected: Users creating or managing StatefulSets that need a custom start ordinal; clusters where the feature gate is enabled will see the new field respected by the controller.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the StatefulSetStartOrdinal feature gate in beta, allowing the StatefulSet controller to accept a startOrdinal field so pods can begin at a user‑specified ordinal.
enrichment.impact: Enables more flexible StatefulSet deployments and migrations, reducing manual work and potential errors when a non‑zero start ordinal is required.

apiChange.description: The PodDisruptionBudget `spec.unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy` field has graduated to beta and is enabled by default. On servers with the feature enabled, this field may be set to `AlwaysAllow` to always allow unhealthy pods covered by the PodDisruptionBudget to be evicted.
apiChange.author: ravisantoshgudimetla

enrichment.problem: Prior to this change, the PodDisruptionBudget spec.unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy field was alpha and disabled by default, limiting users' ability to evict unhealthy pods covered by a PDB, which could block necessary pod removals during maintenance or scaling events.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using PodDisruptionBudgets with unhealthy pods; administrators who need to control eviction policies.
enrichment.fix: The spec.unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy field is graduated to beta and enabled by default. Administrators can now set the field to `AlwaysAllow` to permit eviction of unhealthy pods that are selected by a PDB.
enrichment.impact: Provides finer-grained control over pod eviction behavior, preventing PDBs from unintentionally blocking the removal of unhealthy pods, thus improving cluster reliability and operational flexibility during upgrades, scaling, or node maintenance.

apiChange.description: kubelet: changed `MemoryThrottlingFactor` default value to `0.9` and formulas to calculate `memory.high`
apiChange.author: pacoxu
apiChange.userFacingChange: kubelet: change MemoryThrottlingFactor default value to 0.9 and formulas to calculate memory.high

enrichment.problem: The kubelet used a default MemoryThrottlingFactor and memory.high calculation that could result in less appropriate memory throttling and QoS behavior for pods, especially for workloads relying on accurate memory.high thresholds.
enrichment.affected: All clusters running the kubelet; pod workloads that depend on memory QoS (burstable/guaranteed) will have their memory.high thresholds adjusted.
enrichment.fix: Changed the default MemoryThrottlingFactor to 0.9 and updated the formulas that compute the cgroup `memory.high` value, providing a tighter and more consistent memory throttling policy.
enrichment.impact: Nodes will enforce a stricter memory throttling limit for pods, improving memory QoS decisions and reducing the risk of pods exceeding their memory requests. Users may see different throttling behavior for existing workloads, but overall memory management becomes more predictable.

apiChange.description:
Introduced API for streaming.

Added `SendInitialEvents` field to the `ListOptions`. When the new option is set together with `watch=true`, it begins the watch stream with synthetic init events followed by a synthetic "Bookmark" after which the server continues streaming events.
apiChange.author: p0lyn0mial
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Introduce API for streaming.

Add SendInitialEvents field to the ListOptions. When the new option is set together with watch=true, it begins the watch stream with synthetic init events followed by a synthetic "Bookmark" after which the server continues streaming events.

enrichment.problem: Clients that needed the initial state of resources had to perform a separate LIST request before starting a WATCH, leading to extra latency and potential race conditions. There was no way to receive synthetic initial events directly on a watch stream.
enrichment.affected: Any client that uses the watch API (e.g., controllers, kubectl, custom operators) gains the ability to receive an initial state snapshot without a separate LIST request.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new `SendInitialEvents` flag in `ListOptions`. When set with `watch=true`, the API server streams synthetic init events representing the current state, followed by a synthetic Bookmark, before continuing with normal watch events.
enrichment.impact: Reduces the number of API calls for controllers, kubectl, and other watch‑based clients, simplifies client logic, and improves consistency by delivering an initial snapshot within the same watch stream.

apiChange.description: Updated: Redefine AppProtocol field description and add new standard values
apiChange.author: LiorLieberman

enrichment.problem: The `appProtocol` field in Service specifications had an ambiguous description and lacked a set of standard, predefined values, causing confusion and inconsistent usage across clusters.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that define Services with the `appProtocol` field, especially those using custom or undocumented values, and any tooling that reads this field (e.g., kube-proxy, ingress controllers).
enrichment.fix: The field description is rewritten for clarity and a set of canonical standard values is added to the API, providing developers with explicit options and improving validation of Service definitions.
enrichment.impact: Users can now specify the application protocol for a Service port with clear guidance and validated choices, reducing misconfiguration, improving compatibility with networking components, and simplifying automation and tooling that rely on the field.

apiChange.description:
`NodeResourceFit` and `NodeResourcesBalancedAllocation` implement the `PreScore`
extension point for a more performant calculation.
apiChange.author: tangwz
apiChange.userFacingChange: NodeResourceFit and NodeResourcesBalancedAllocation implement the PreScore extension point for a more performant calculation.

enrichment.problem: NodeResourceFit and NodeResourcesBalancedAllocation performed their calculations during the Score phase, which added extra CPU overhead and increased scheduling latency.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the default NodeResourceFit or NodeResourcesBalancedAllocation scheduler plugins (i.e., most clusters that rely on default pod placement heuristics).
enrichment.fix: Both plugins now implement the PreScore extension point, moving their heavy calculations to the PreScore phase to reduce work done in Score and improve overall scheduling performance.
enrichment.impact: Scheduling cycles become faster and consume less CPU, benefiting clusters with many pods or high scheduling throughput. Users of the default scheduler plugins see smoother pod placement without changes to their manifests.

apiChange.description:
`ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` now provides a status field that contains results of type checking the validation expression.
The type checking is fully informational, and the behavior of the policy is unchanged.
apiChange.author: jiahuif
apiChange.userFacingChange:
ValidatingAdmissionPolicy now provides a status field that contains results of type checking the validation expression.
The type checking is fully informational, and the behavior of the policy is unchanged.

enrichment.problem: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy objects did not expose the results of type checking for their CEL validation expressions, making it hard for administrators to see why an expression might be invalid or malformed.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and developers who create or manage ValidatingAdmissionPolicy objects; any workloads that rely on admission validation may benefit from clearer error reporting.
enrichment.fix: The API now includes a new `status` field on ValidatingAdmissionPolicy that reports the outcomes of type checking the validation expression. This information is purely informational and does not alter the policy's enforcement behavior.
enrichment.impact: Admins can now diagnose and correct malformed or unsafe CEL expressions more easily, improving the observability and debugging experience for admission control policies without affecting existing policy enforcement.

apiChange.description:
Graduated seccomp profile defaulting to GA.

Set the kubelet `--seccomp-default` flag or `seccompDefault` kubelet configuration field to `true` to make pods on that node default to using the `RuntimeDefault` seccomp profile.

Enabling seccomp for your workload can have a negative performance impact depending on the kernel and container runtime version in use.

Guidance for identifying and mitigating those issues is outlined in the Kubernetes [seccomp tutorial](https://k8s.io/docs/tutorials/security/seccomp).
apiChange.author: saschagrunert
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Graduated seccomp profile defaulting to GA.

Set the kubelet `--seccomp-default` flag or `seccompDefault` kubelet configuration field to `true` to make pods on that node default to using the `RuntimeDefault` seccomp profile.

Enabling seccomp for your workload can have a negative performance impact depending on the kernel and container runtime version in use.

Guidance for identifying and mitigating those issues is outlined in the Kubernetes [seccomp tutorial](https://k8s.io/docs/tutorials/security/seccomp).

enrichment.problem: Pods did not automatically receive a seccomp profile, leaving them unconfined unless the cluster admin manually applied a profile. This reduced the default security posture of workloads.
enrichment.affected: All pods scheduled to nodes where the kubelet flag/config is enabled; cluster administrators who manage kubelet settings.
enrichment.fix: Graduated the seccomp-default feature to GA. Administrators can now set the kubelet `--seccomp-default` flag or the `seccompDefault` field in the kubelet config to `true`, causing all pods on that node to default to the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile.
enrichment.impact: Pods gain a baseline security hardening without extra configuration, improving cluster security out of the box. admins must be aware of a potential performance impact on certain kernel and container‑runtime versions and may need to tune or disable the feature for sensitive workloads.

apiChange.description: The `DownwardAPIHugePages` kubelet feature graduated to stable / GA.
apiChange.author: saschagrunert

enrichment.problem: The Downward API did not provide a stable way to expose pod hugepages limits and requests to containers, as the DownwardAPIHugePages feature was only in beta/alpha.
enrichment.affected: Pods that need to consume hugepages and rely on the Downward API for resource information; developers and operators configuring such workloads.
enrichment.fix: The DownwardAPIHugePages feature has graduated to GA in the kubelet, making the hugepages fields in the Downward API stable and generally enabled by default.
enrichment.impact: Users can now reliably use the Downward API to read hugepages resource values inside containers, improving portability and simplifying configuration of workloads that depend on hugepages.

apiChange.description:
Added CEL runtime cost calculation into ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, matching the evaluation cost
restrictions that already apply to CustomResourceDefinition.
If rule evaluation uses more compute than the limit, the API server aborts the evaluation and the
admission check that was being performed is aborted; the `failurePolicy` for the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
determines the outcome.
apiChange.author: cici37
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Added CEL runtime cost calculation into ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, matching the evaluation cost
restrictions that already apply to CustomResourceDefinition.
If rule evaluation uses more compute than the limit, the API server aborts the evaluation and the
admission check that was being performed is aborted; the `failurePolicy` for the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
determines the outcome.

enrichment.problem: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (VAP) evaluations could execute arbitrarily complex CEL expressions without any runtime cost limits, risking excessive CPU consumption and potential denial‑of‑service for the API server.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use ValidatingAdmissionPolicy with CEL rules that could exceed compute limits; any pods or resources subject to those admission policies.
enrichment.fix: Introduced CEL runtime cost calculation for VAPs, mirroring the cost restrictions already enforced for CustomResourceDefinitions. When a rule’s compute cost exceeds the configured limit, the API server aborts the evaluation and the VAP’s `failurePolicy` determines the final admission outcome.
enrichment.impact: Prevents runaway CPU usage during admission checks, aligning VAP behavior with CRD safeguards and improving cluster stability and security for users that rely on VAPs with complex validation logic.

apiChange.description: Graduated `KubeletTracing` to beta, which means that the feature gate is now enabled by default.
apiChange.author: saschagrunert
apiChange.userFacingChange: Graduate `KubeletTracing` to beta, which means that the feature gate is now enabled by default.

enrichment.problem: The KubeletTracing feature was only available in alpha and disabled by default, requiring users to manually enable the feature gate to get kubelet-level tracing.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running the kubelet that needed tracing capabilities; administrators who previously had to enable the alpha feature gate manually.
enrichment.fix: Graduated KubeletTracing to beta and enabled the feature gate by default, so tracing is now active without extra configuration.
enrichment.impact: Users gain out‑of‑the‑box tracing of kubelet operations, improving observability and debugging of node‑level issues with no additional setup.

apiChange.description: `PodSchedulingReadiness` is graduated to beta.
apiChange.author: Huang-Wei
apiChange.userFacingChange: PodSchedulingReadiness is graduated to beta.

enrichment.problem: The PodSchedulingReadiness feature was only available as an alpha API, limiting its stability and production use. Users could not rely on a consistent way to gate pod scheduling based on readiness conditions.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that relies on pod readiness gating for scheduling, such as stateful applications or CI pipelines that need pods to be fully ready before being scheduled.
enrichment.fix: The feature has been graduated to beta, stabilizing the API, making it generally available, and ensuring default enablement with clearer semantics for pod scheduling readiness checks.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now safely use PodSchedulingReadiness in production workloads, improving control over when pods become eligible for scheduling based on custom readiness signals, and reducing unexpected scheduling failures.

apiChange.description: Remove deprecated `--enable-taint-manager` and `--pod-eviction-timeout` CLI
apiChange.author: atosatto

enrichment.problem: The kubelet command-line flags `--enable-taint-manager` and `--pod-eviction-timeout` were deprecated but still accepted, leading to possible confusion and the need to maintain unused code.
enrichment.affected: Any environment where kubelet is started with `--enable-taint-manager` or `--pod-eviction-timeout`. Administrators must edit their kubelet configuration or systemd units to drop these flags.
enrichment.fix: The two deprecated flags have been removed from the kubelet CLI. Users must no longer specify them; the related functionality is now always on or has a different default behavior.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that still include these flags in kubelet start‑up scripts will encounter an "unknown flag" error and fail to start until the flags are removed. This cleanup simplifies the kubelet codebase and eliminates stale configuration options.

apiChange.description: Extended the kubelet's PodResources API to include resources allocated in `ResourceClaims` via `DynamicResourceAllocation`. Additionally, added a new `Get()` method to query a specific pod for its resources.
apiChange.author: moshe010

enrichment.problem: The kubelet PodResources API did not expose resources that are allocated through Dynamic Resource Allocation (ResourceClaims), making it impossible for consumers (e.g., device plugins, monitoring tools) to see the full set of resources a pod uses. There was also no way to query resources for a single pod via the API.
enrichment.affected: Users and tools that rely on the kubelet PodResources API (e.g., device plugins, monitoring agents, custom schedulers) now receive full resource information, including DynamicResourceAllocation claims.
enrichment.fix: Extended the kubelet's PodResources gRPC API to include resources allocated via ResourceClaims and added a new Get() method that allows callers to retrieve the resource list for a specific pod.
enrichment.impact: Enables clients to obtain complete resource allocation information, including dynamic claims, which improves observability, debugging, and integration with external resource managers and device plugins.

apiChange.description: Promoted `CronJobTimeZone` feature to GA
apiChange.author: soltysh
apiChange.userFacingChange: Promote CronJobTimeZone feature to GA

enrichment.problem: The CronJobTimeZone feature was only available as an Alpha/Beta feature requiring an explicit feature gate, limiting its stability and forcing users to manage the gate.
enrichment.affected: Users running CronJobs that need timezone support and cluster administrators who previously had to enable the CronJobTimeZone feature gate.
enrichment.fix: The feature is promoted to GA, meaning the feature gate is removed, the API is stable, and the behavior is enabled by default in the control plane components.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now rely on deterministic timezone handling for CronJobs without additional configuration, improving reliability of scheduled workloads that depend on specific time zones.

apiChange.description: Added `messageExpression` field to `ValidationRule`.
apiChange.author: DangerOnTheRanger
apiChange.userFacingChange: Added messageExpression field to ValidationRule. (#115969, @DangerOnTheRanger)

enrichment.problem: ValidationRule objects did not provide a way to specify a custom, dynamically generated error message, limiting the clarity of validation feedback for users.
enrichment.affected: Any workload or custom resource that relies on ValidationRule for admission validation will benefit from richer error messages.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `messageExpression` field on ValidationRule that allows users to define an expression to compute the validation error message at runtime.
enrichment.impact: Users can now surface more informative and context‑specific validation errors, improving debugging and user experience when working with custom resources and other validated objects.

apiChange.description:
Added `auditAnnotations` to `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy`, enabling CEL to be used to add audit annotations to request audit events.
Added `validationActions` to `ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding`, enabling validation failures to be handled by any combination of the warn, audit and deny enforcement actions.
apiChange.author: jpbetz
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Adds auditAnnotations to ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, enabling CEL to be used to add audit annotations to request audit events.
Adds validationActions to ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding, enabling validation failures to be handled by any combination of the warn, audit and deny enforcement actions.

enrichment.problem: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy could not add custom audit annotations and ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding only supported a single enforcement action, limiting flexibility in how validation failures are reported and enforced.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using admission control policies via ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding; administrators who need richer audit data or more granular validation handling.
enrichment.fix: Introduced an `auditAnnotations` field on ValidatingAdmissionPolicy that lets CEL expressions populate audit annotations on request audit events. Added a `validationActions` field on ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding allowing any combination of `warn`, `audit`, and `deny` enforcement actions for validation failures.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now enrich audit logs with policy‑specific context and choose how validation failures are handled (e.g., warn users while still auditing, or deny outright). This improves observability, debugging, and policy enforcement flexibility without breaking existing behavior.

apiChange.description: Graduated the container resource metrics feature on `HPA` to beta.
apiChange.author: sanposhiho
apiChange.userFacingChange: graduate the container resource metrics feature on HPA to beta.

enrichment.problem: The container resource metrics feature for HorizontalPodAutoscaler was only available in Alpha, lacking stability guarantees and broader support.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads using HPA that want to scale based on per‑container resource metrics, as well as cluster operators who enable this feature.
enrichment.fix: Graduated the container resource metrics feature to Beta, making the API version stable, improving validation, and ensuring broader compatibility across clusters.
enrichment.impact: Users can now safely use container-level CPU/memory metrics to drive HPA scaling in production workloads, benefiting from a more stable API and better support.

apiChange.description:
Added authorization check support to the CEL expressions of ValidatingAdmissionPolicy via a `authorizer`
variable with expressions. The new variable provides a builder that allows expressions such `authorizer.group('').resource('pods').check('create').allowed()`.
apiChange.author: jpbetz
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Added authorization check support to the CEL expressions of ValidatingAdmissionPolicy via a `authorizer`
variable with expressions. The new variable provides a builder that allows expressions such `authorizer.group('').resource('pods').check('create').allowed()`.

enrichment.problem: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy CEL expressions could not perform authorization checks, limiting policy expressiveness for scenarios that need to verify a user’s permission on other resources.
enrichment.affected: Cluster operators and developers writing ValidatingAdmissionPolicy rules that need to incorporate permission checks.
enrichment.fix: Introduced an `authorizer` variable in CEL for ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, providing a builder API (e.g., `authorizer.group('').resource('pods').check('create').allowed()`) that lets policies query the authorizer during evaluation.
enrichment.impact: Enables more powerful admission policies that can conditionally allow or reject requests based on whether the requester has permission to perform actions on other resources, improving security and flexibility for cluster operators.

apiChange.description: Graduated `Kubelet Topology Manager` to GA.
apiChange.author: swatisehgal
apiChange.userFacingChange: Graduate Kubelet Topology Manager to GA.

enrichment.problem: Kubelet Topology Manager was only available as an alpha/beta feature, limiting its use in production and lacking the stability guarantees of a GA feature.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that enable or plan to use the Kubelet Topology Manager for pod placement and resource allocation, especially those with NUMA-aware workloads.
enrichment.fix: The Topology Manager component in kubelet has been promoted to GA status, making it fully supported, stable, and enabled by default in production clusters.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators can now rely on topology-aware pod placement and resource allocation (e.g., NUMA alignment) in production workloads, improving performance and predictability without needing feature gates.

apiChange.description: Bump default API QPS limits for Kubelet.
apiChange.author: wojtek-t

enrichment.problem: The default API QPS limit used by the kubelet client was too low for large clusters or workloads that generate many API requests, causing the kubelet to be throttled and potentially delaying node health checks and pod operations.
enrichment.affected: All kubelet instances, particularly in clusters with many pods or high‑frequency API interactions, may experience fewer throttling issues.
enrichment.fix: Increase the default QPS (queries‑per‑second) limit in the kubelet configuration, allowing it to send more requests to the API server without being throttled under typical load.
enrichment.impact: Reduces kubelet throttling, improves node responsiveness and reliability, and prevents delays in pod lifecycle and node health reporting, especially in large or busy clusters.

apiChange.description:
`APIServerTracing` feature gate is now enabled by default. Tracing in the API
Server is still disabled by default, and requires a config file to enable.
apiChange.author: dashpole
apiChange.userFacingChange: APIServerTracing feature gate is now enabled by default. Tracing in the API Server is still disabled by default, and requires a config file to enable.

enrichment.problem: Enabling API server request tracing required two steps: manually turning on the APIServerTracing feature gate and providing a tracing configuration file. This added unnecessary complexity for users who wanted to use tracing.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run the kube-apiserver and want to use request tracing; administrators no longer need to toggle the feature gate manually.
enrichment.fix: The APIServerTracing feature gate is now enabled by default. Tracing remains disabled until a tracing configuration file is supplied, but operators no longer need to enable the feature gate explicitly.
enrichment.impact: Operators can enable API server tracing with a single configuration change, simplifying adoption and reducing the chance of misconfiguration. The change does not alter runtime behavior when no tracing config is present.

apiChange.description: The API server now re-uses data encryption keys while the kms v2 plugin key ID is stable.  Data encryption keys are still randomly generated on server start but an atomic counter is used to prevent nonce collisions.
apiChange.author: enj
apiChange.userFacingChange: The API server now re-uses data encryption keys while the kms v2 plugin's key ID is stable.  Data encryption keys are still randomly generated on server start but an atomic counter is used to prevent nonce collisions.

enrichment.problem: When using the KMS v2 provider with a stable key ID, the API server previously generated a new data encryption key for each operation, which could lead to nonce collisions and added unnecessary overhead.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that enable envelope encryption with a KMS v2 provider and use a stable key ID in their EncryptionConfiguration.
enrichment.fix: The API server now re‑uses the same data encryption key while the KMS v2 plugin's key ID remains unchanged. An atomic counter is employed to guarantee unique nonces, and keys are still freshly generated at server start.
enrichment.impact: Reduces CPU and latency overhead for clusters that encrypt etcd data with KMS v2, while eliminating the risk of nonce collisions, improving overall performance and reliability of data encryption operations.

apiChange.description: Relaxed API validation to allow pod node selector to be mutable for gated pods (additions only, no deletions or mutations).
apiChange.author: danielvegamyhre
apiChange.userFacingChange: Relax API validation to allow pod node selector to be mutable for gated pods (additions only, no deletions or mutations).

issueContext.title: Mutable pod scheduling directives
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

See [KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-scheduling/3838-pod-mutable-scheduling-directives) for context. This issue is creating to track work on the API validation changes.

### Why is this needed?

Validation relaxation of certain fields in the pod spec to allow for mutable scheduling directives.

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes API validation disallowed any changes to a pod's nodeSelector after the pod was created, even for gated pods that were intended to support mutable scheduling directives. This prevented users from adding node selectors to existing pods without recreating them.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that use gated (mutable) pods and need to add node selector entries after creation; controllers that manage such pods may also benefit.
enrichment.fix: Relax the API validation logic so that, for gated pods, additions to the pod.spec.nodeSelector are allowed. Deletions or modifications of existing keys remain prohibited.
enrichment.impact: Users can now add node selector constraints to running pods that opt‑in to mutable scheduling directives, simplifying workflows such as dynamic placement adjustments and reducing the need to delete and recreate pods.

apiChange.description:
Added the `MatchConditions` field to `ValidatingWebhookConfiguration` and `MutatingWebhookConfiguration` for the v1beta and v1 apis. 

The `AdmissionWebhookMatchConditions` featuregate is now in Alpha
apiChange.author: ivelichkovich
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Added the `MatchConditions` field to `ValidatingWebhookConfiguration` and `MutatingWebhookConfiguration` for the v1beta and v1 apis. 

The `AdmissionWebhookMatchConditions` featuregate is now in Alpha

enrichment.problem: Admission webhooks could only match incoming requests based on namespace, object, and operation, lacking support for arbitrary match conditions, forcing users to create multiple webhook configurations for complex filtering.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and developers who configure or implement validating or mutating admission webhooks.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `MatchConditions` field in `ValidatingWebhookConfiguration` and `MutatingWebhookConfiguration` for both v1beta1 and v1 APIs. The field is gated behind the `AdmissionWebhookMatchConditions` Alpha feature gate.
enrichment.impact: Enables fine‑grained, declarative matching of admission webhook requests, reducing the number of webhook configurations needed and allowing more precise control over when webhooks are invoked.

apiChange.description: Promoted `SelfSubjectReview` to Beta
apiChange.author: nabokihms

enrichment.problem: SelfSubjectReview was only available as an Alpha API, so users could not rely on it for production workloads and faced potential breaking changes when upgrading.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads, tools, or scripts that call the SelfSubjectReview API (e.g., RBAC permission checks in CI/CD pipelines, kubectl auth can-i, custom controllers).
enrichment.fix: The SelfSubjectReview resource has been promoted to Beta, providing a more stable API version with graduated validation, documentation, and client support.
enrichment.impact: Operators and developers can now use SelfSubjectReview in production to reliably query their own RBAC permissions, with reduced risk of future breaking changes and better tooling support.

apiChange.description:
`resource.k8s.io/v1alpha1` was replaced with `resource.k8s.io/v1alpha2`. Before
upgrading a cluster, all objects in resource.k8s.io/v1alpha1 (ResourceClaim, ResourceClaimTemplate,
ResourceClass, PodScheduling) must be deleted. The changes are internal, so
YAML files which create pods and resource claims don't need changes except for
the newer `apiVersion`.
apiChange.author: pohly
apiChange.userFacingChange: ACTION REQUIRED: resource.k8s.io/v1alpha1 was replaced with resource.k8s.io/v1alpha2. Before upgrading a cluster, all objects in resource.k8s.io/v1alpha1 (ResourceClaim, ResourceClaimTemplate, ResourceClass, PodScheduling) must be deleted. The changes will be internal, so YAML files which create pods and resource claims don't need changes except for the newer `apiVersion`.

enrichment.problem: The v1alpha1 version of the resource.k8s.io API group (ResourceClaim, ResourceClaimTemplate, ResourceClass, PodScheduling) was removed. If any objects of that version exist during a cluster upgrade, the upgrade will fail.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that have created ResourceClaim, ResourceClaimTemplate, ResourceClass, or PodScheduling objects using the v1alpha1 API version. Administrators performing an upgrade are affected.
enrichment.fix: Upgrade the API version to resource.k8s.io/v1alpha2. Before upgrading, delete all existing v1alpha1 objects. New YAML manifests only need to reference the newer apiVersion; no other changes are required.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators must clean up old API objects before upgrading, otherwise the upgrade process will be blocked. After cleanup, workloads continue to operate unchanged with the new API version.

apiChange.description: Introduced a breaking change to the `resource.k8s.io` API in its `AllocationResult` struct. This change allows a kubelet plugin for the `DynamicResourceAllocation` feature to service allocations from multiple resource driver controllers.
apiChange.author: klueska

issueContext.title: dynamic resource allocation: allow a kubelet-plugin to service allocations from multiple resource-driver controllers
issueContext.body: The goal is to allow one to write a custom controller such as the one below to (e.g.) co-allocate GPUs and RDMA interfaces (using a custom `ResourceClass` and associated `ClaimParameters` object), but allow the "default" kubelet-plugins for these resources to handle the actual device preparation and injection. **Note:** An older version of this description was too specific and suggested that we add an extension to the kubelet-plugin API to include an RCP called `WatchConfiguration`. Some of the comments at the beginning of this issue are in reference to that. We have since refined our thinking on how to do achieve the same goal, and those changes are reflected in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3802

enrichment.problem: The AllocationResult struct in the resource.k8s.io API was not designed to let a single kubelet plugin service allocation requests from multiple resource driver controllers, preventing co‑allocation scenarios such as combining GPUs and RDMA devices.
enrichment.affected: Users writing or using kubelet plugins for DynamicResourceAllocation and developers of resource driver controllers that rely on the AllocationResult API.
enrichment.fix: The AllocationResult struct was changed (breaking change) to include fields that allow a kubelet plugin for the DynamicResourceAllocation feature to handle allocations from multiple resource‑driver controllers, enabling a single plugin to manage several resources simultaneously.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now co‑allocate different device types using custom ResourceClasses while still using the default kubelet‑plugin implementations for device preparation, simplifying multi‑resource workloads and reducing the need for bespoke plugins.

apiChange.description: Added matchConditions field to ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and enabled support for CEL based custom match criteria.
apiChange.author: maxsmythe
apiChange.userFacingChange: Added matchConditions field to ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, enabled support for CEL based custom match criteria.

enrichment.problem: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy could not express custom matching logic beyond basic selectors, forcing users to rely on external admission webhooks for complex criteria.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using ValidatingAdmissionPolicy for admission control, especially those needing custom match logic. Policy authors gain new capabilities.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `matchConditions` field to ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, allowing users to define CEL (Common Expression Language) based match expressions for fine‑grained policy targeting.
enrichment.impact: Enables more precise, in‑cluster admission control without additional webhooks, reducing latency and operational complexity while expanding the expressive power of policies.

apiChange.description: Added `messageExpression` to `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy`, to set custom failure message via CEL expression.
apiChange.author: jiahuif

enrichment.problem: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy could only provide a static failure message, limiting the ability to convey context‑specific information when a policy rejects a request.
enrichment.affected: Users who create or rely on ValidatingAdmissionPolicy objects to enforce custom admission checks.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the `messageExpression` field on ValidatingAdmissionPolicy. The field accepts a CEL expression that is evaluated at admission time to generate a custom failure message.
enrichment.impact: Operators and developers can now surface richer, dynamic error messages directly from admission policies, making troubleshooting and policy debugging faster and more informative.

apiChange.description: `SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod` graduated to Beta.
apiChange.author: jsafrane
apiChange.userFacingChange: SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod graduated to Beta.

enrichment.problem: The SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod feature was only in alpha, requiring a feature gate and lacking full stability and documentation, making it difficult for users to rely on SELinux relabeling for ReadWriteOncePod volumes.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and developers using SELinux‑enforced clusters with pods that mount ReadWriteOncePod volumes.
enrichment.fix: The feature has graduated to Beta, making it enabled by default (or stable behind a beta feature gate), with improved testing, documentation, and guarantees about its behavior for pod volume mounts.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that enforce SELinux can now securely and reliably use ReadWriteOncePod volumes without custom work‑arounds, improving workload security and simplifying operations for administrators and developers.

apiChange.description: `StatefulSetAutoDeletePVC` feature gate promoted to beta.
apiChange.author: mattcary
apiChange.userFacingChange: StatefulSetAutoDeletePVC feature gate promoted to beta.

enrichment.problem: Automatic deletion of PersistentVolumeClaims (PVCs) for StatefulSets was only available behind the StatefulSetAutoDeletePVC feature gate, limiting users from safely cleaning up PVCs when StatefulSets are scaled down or deleted.
enrichment.affected: Users running StatefulSets with volumeClaimTemplates who want PVCs to be automatically deleted on scale‑down or StatefulSet deletion.
enrichment.fix: The StatefulSetAutoDeletePVC feature gate has been promoted to beta, making the automatic PVC deletion behavior generally available (enabled by default) for StatefulSets.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now automatically clean up PVCs associated with StatefulSets, preventing orphaned volumes, reducing manual storage management, and improving overall storage hygiene for workloads that use StatefulSets.

apiChange.description:
New `service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode` annotation has been introduced as a replacement for the `service.kubernetes.io/topology-aware-hints` annotation.
- `service.kubernetes.io/topology-aware-hints` annotation has been deprecated.
- kube-proxy now accepts any value that is not "disabled" for these annotations, enabling custom implementation-specific and/or future built-in heuristics to be used.
apiChange.author: robscott
apiChange.userFacingChange:
* New `service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode` annotation has been introduced as a replacement for the `service.kubernetes.io/topology-aware-hints` annotation.
* `service.kubernetes.io/topology-aware-hints` annotation has been deprecated.
* kube-proxy now accepts any value that is not "disabled" for these annotations, enabling custom implementation-specific and/or future built-in heuristics to be used.

enrichment.problem: The existing `service.kubernetes.io/topology-aware-hints` annotation was the only way to influence topology‑aware routing for Services, and kube‑proxy only accepted a limited set of values. This restricted extensibility and made it hard to evolve the feature.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using Services with the `topology-aware-hints` annotation, and any custom networking solutions that rely on kube‑proxy's topology‑aware routing logic.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode` annotation as the replacement. The old `service.kubernetes.io/topology-aware-hints` annotation is now deprecated. kube‑proxy has been updated to treat any non‑"disabled" value for these annotations as enabling topology‑aware routing, allowing custom or future built‑in heuristics.
enrichment.impact: Users can now adopt the new annotation and benefit from more flexible, implementation‑specific topology routing without breaking existing clusters. Future networking implementations can introduce new modes without needing additional code changes in kube‑proxy.

apiChange.description: Removed support for the `v1alpha1` kubeletplugin API of `DynamicResourceManagement`. All plugins must be updated to `v1alpha2` in order to function properly.
apiChange.author: klueska
apiChange.userFacingChange: ACTION REQUIRED: We have removed support for the v1alpha1 kubeletplugin API of DynamicResourceManagement. All plugins must update to v1alpha2 in order to function properly going forward.

enrichment.problem: Support for the v1alpha1 kubeletplugin API used by DynamicResourceManagement was removed, causing any plugins that still target this version to fail.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running custom or built‑in kubelet plugins that target the v1alpha1 DynamicResourceManagement API.
enrichment.fix: All kubelet plugins must be updated to use the v1alpha2 version of the DynamicResourceManagement API to restore functionality.
enrichment.impact: Plugins that have not been migrated will stop working, which can break custom resource allocation or other node‑level extensions that relied on the older API. Updating to v1alpha2 restores normal operation.

apiChange.description: Added validation to ensure that if `service.kubernetes.io/topology-aware-hints` and `service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode` annotations are both set, they are set to the same value.Also Added deprecation warning if `service.kubernetes.io/topology-aware-hints` annotation is used.
apiChange.author: robscott
apiChange.userFacingChange:
- Added validation to ensure that if `service.kubernetes.io/topology-aware-hints` and `service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode` annotations are both set, they are set to the same value.
- Added deprecation warning if `service.kubernetes.io/topology-aware-hints` annotation is used.

enrichment.problem: When both `service.kubernetes.io/topology-aware-hints` and `service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode` annotations were set on a Service, they could have conflicting values, leading to ambiguous topology handling. Additionally, the `topology-aware-hints` annotation is deprecated but no warning was emitted, so users were unaware of the upcoming removal.
enrichment.affected: Any Service object that sets `service.kubernetes.io/topology-aware-hints` and/or `service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode`. Clusters that used the deprecated `topology-aware-hints` annotation will see a warning.
enrichment.fix: Added server‑side validation that requires the two annotations to have identical values when both are present, rejecting the Service object otherwise. Added a deprecation warning that is logged whenever the `service.kubernetes.io/topology-aware-hints` annotation is used.
enrichment.impact: Prevents misconfiguration of Services that rely on topology‑aware routing, ensuring consistent behavior. Users are now informed that `topology-aware-hints` is deprecated, giving them time to migrate to the newer `topology-mode` annotation, reducing future upgrade pain.

apiChange.description: Adds feature gate `NodeLogQuery` which provides cluster administrators with a streaming view of logs using kubectl without them having to implement a client side reader or logging into the node.
apiChange.author: LorbusChris

enrichment.problem: Cluster administrators could not stream logs directly with kubectl and had to implement custom client‑side readers or SSH into nodes to view logs, making log access cumbersome and less observable.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and operators who need to view live node logs; also developers using kubectl for debugging workloads on both Linux and Windows nodes.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the `NodeLogQuery` feature gate. When enabled, it adds a server‑side endpoint that streams node logs via the Kubernetes API, allowing `kubectl logs` to retrieve live logs without extra client code or node login.
enrichment.impact: Simplifies log collection and troubleshooting, improves observability, and provides a consistent, built‑in way to stream logs across Linux and Windows nodes using standard kubectl commands.

issueContext.title: API doc should use the field name in description
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Currently we have inconsistency in most of the API where the field name should be used in description so the generated docs match the API fields people actually set. 
e.g. 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/367f01f62d1a6ca149c317f97a958dd5c6e74af1/staging/src/k8s.io/api/admission/v1/types.go#L41
`uid` should be used instead of `UID` so it's shown properly in generated docs.


### What did you expect to happen?

Inside https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/api/openapi-spec/swagger.json description, the field name should reflect the real field name people actually set.

The work could be divided based on API group. 

### Steps

1. Modify the godoc in the versioned types.go file(s) for the appropriate API group to use the JSON name when referring to API fields. Create a commit with these changes.
2. Run `make update` to regenerate API documentation files (this will generate updates to proto files, generated go files, and openapi json files) (or open a PR with just the types.go changes and update the generated files using the instructions at https://www.kubernetes.dev/blog/2022/03/15/k8s-triage-bot-helper-ci-job/#using-the-short-term-solution). Create a second commit with these changes.

### API groups

- admissionregistration.k8s.io | v1 - @bhavyastar
- apiextensions.k8s.io | v1 - @ShivamTyagi12345 (located within staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apis/apiextensions/v*/types*.go)
