other.description:
The `wait.Poll*` and `wait.ExponentialBackoff*` functions have been deprecated and will be removed in a future release.  Callers should switch to using `wait.PollUntilContextCancel`, `wait.PollUntilContextTimeout`, or `wait.ExponentialBackoffWithContext` as appropriate.

`PollWithContext(Cancel|Deadline)` will no longer return `ErrWaitTimeout` - use the `Interrupted(error) bool` helper to replace checks for `err == ErrWaitTimeout`, or compare specifically to context errors as needed. A future release will make the `ErrWaitTimeout` error private and callers must use `Interrupted()` instead. If you are returning `ErrWaitTimeout` from your own methods, switch to creating a location specific `cause err` and pass it to the new method `wait.ErrorInterrupted(cause) error` which will ensure `Interrupted()` returns true for your loop. 

The `wait.NewExponentialBackoffManager` and `wait.NewJitteringBackoffManager` functions have been marked as deprecated.  Callers should switch to using the `Backoff{...}.DelayWithReset(clock, resetInterval)` method and must set the `Steps` field when using `Factor`. As a short term change, callers may use the `Timer()` method on the `BackoffManager` until the backoff managers are deprecated and removed. Please see the godoc of the deprecated functions for examples of how to replace usage of this function.
other.author: smarterclayton
other.userFacingChange:
The `wait.Poll*` and `wait.ExponentialBackoff*` functions have been deprecated and will be removed in a future release.  Callers should switch to using `wait.PollUntilContextCancel`, `wait.PollUntilContextTimeout`, or `wait.ExponentialBackoffWithContext` as appropriate.

`PollWithContext(Cancel|Deadline)` will no longer return `ErrWaitTimeout` - use the `Interrupted(error) bool` helper to replace checks for `err == ErrWaitTimeout`, or compare specifically to context errors as needed. A future release will make the `ErrWaitTimeout` error private and callers must use `Interrupted()` instead. If you are returning `ErrWaitTimeout` from your own methods, switch to creating a location specific `cause err` and pass it to the new method `wait.ErrorInterrupted(cause) error` which will ensure `Interrupted()` returns true for your loop. 

The `wait.NewExponentialBackoffManager` and `wait.NewJitteringBackoffManager` functions have been marked as deprecated.  Callers should switch to using the `Backoff{...}.DelayWithReset(clock, resetInterval)` method and must set the `Steps` field when using `Factor`. As a short term change, callers may use the `Timer()` method on the `BackoffManager` until the backoff managers are deprecated and removed. Please see the godoc of the deprecated functions for examples of how to replace usage of this function.

enrichment.problem: The utility functions wait.Poll*, wait.ExponentialBackoff* and the backoff manager constructors have been deprecated. New context‑aware PollUntil* and ExponentialBackoffWithContext functions change error handling (ErrWaitTimeout is no longer returned) and require callers to use the Interrupted helper or create error causes with wait.ErrorInterrupted. Existing code that relies on the old APIs will fail to compile or mis‑interpret errors after they are removed.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes component or external code that uses the wait.Poll*, wait.ExponentialBackoff* functions or the NewExponentialBackoffManager / NewJitteringBackoffManager constructors, including core components (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet), command‑line tools, and test suites.
enrichment.fix: Switch code to use wait.PollUntilContextCancel, wait.PollUntilContextTimeout, or wait.ExponentialBackoffWithContext. Replace checks for ErrWaitTimeout with the Interrupted(err) helper or compare against context errors. For custom timeout errors, wrap the cause with wait.ErrorInterrupted. Replace wait.NewExponentialBackoffManager / wait.NewJitteringBackoffManager with Backoff{...}.DelayWithReset(clock, resetInterval) (setting Steps when using Factor) or temporarily use the BackoffManager Timer() method.
enrichment.impact: Ensures loops respect Go context cancellation and timeout semantics, provides a consistent way to detect interrupted retries, and prevents future breakage when the deprecated functions are removed. Developers must update their code now to avoid compilation errors and correct error handling in upcoming releases.

other.description: Fixed a regression that the scheduler always goes through all Filter plugins.
other.author: Huang-Wei
other.userFacingChange: Fix a 1.24 regression that the scheduler always goes through all Filter plugins.

issueContext.title: kube-scheduler: Bring back the ability to stop at the first failed filter
issueContext.body:
#108829 changed the default behavior of scheduler framework's `RunFilterPlugins` - from stopping at the first failed filter to always running all filters. This change breaks Cluster Autoscaler at scale. Cluster Autoscaler imports the scheduler framework to simulate filters on artificial nodes. In a (pretty common) one-pod-per-node scenario, the number of `RunFilterPlugins` calls is ~quadratic wrt. the number of nodes needed for unschedulable pods - it can be a lot of calls. Before #108829, in such scenario the vast majority of `RunFilterPlugins` calls would stop at failing Fit or NodeAffinity filters, and not run the rest of them (e.g. PV-related filters). After the change, every call to `RunFilterPlugins` runs all filters, which completely breaks Cluster Autoscaler at scale (an example scenario of 300 1-pod-per-node pods and 200 node groups takes >10min in 1.24, and ~50s in <1.22).

Can we get the old behavior back? Or re-introduce the config option so that Cluster Autoscaler can set it accordingly? Ideally, we'd also like to get this backported as far as possible (the change was introduced in 1.24).

enrichment.problem: In v1.24 the scheduler framework was changed to always run all Filter plugins instead of stopping at the first failure, causing a regression that dramatically increased scheduling latency and broke Cluster Autoscaler performance at scale.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the scheduler, especially those running Cluster Autoscaler or large numbers of pods with per‑node placement, experienced degraded performance and possible autoscaling failures.
enrichment.fix: Restored the original behavior: the scheduler now stops evaluating Filter plugins after the first failure, re‑enabling the fast‑path used by Cluster Autoscaler and other workloads.
enrichment.impact: Scheduling cycles are much faster again, preventing massive slow‑downs for large clusters and allowing Cluster Autoscaler to function correctly without excessive delays.

other.author: andrewsykim

issueContext.title: kube-apiserver using unregistered and unusual label
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

The code at
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/86f3fa94f1b75da275a8040e4155840a7b473dc1/pkg/controlplane/instance.go#L126 specifies a ~annotation~ label that API servers set on Leases (each API server registers its own lease).

https://k8s.io/docs/concepts/architecture/leases/#api-server-identity is likely to document this once v1.26 is released; the alpha for API server identity didn't get documented.

Here's the problems:
- as a project, we use `kubernetes.io` as the domain for labels and annotations - see https://k8s.io/docs/reference/labels-annotations-taints/
  - there are a couple of exceptions in https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/labels-annotations-taints/audit-annotations/, FWIW
- if we document and register this `k8s.io/component` label, people may well confuse it with https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/labels-annotations-taints/#app-kubernetes-io-component and use the wrong thing

### What did you expect to happen?

I guess ideally we'd have proposed and then been able to review docs for this when it went alpha, and in that alternative history the discrepancy would have been much more obvious, and it could have been fixed earlier.

I think we should fix it so that we follow the convention of nearly every other annotation used in Kubernetes code.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Look at the source code. Any text editor would work.

### Anything else we need to know?

/sig api-machinery

### Kubernetes version

1.25
1.26 (unreleased)

### Cloud provider

n/a

### OS version

n/a

### Install tools

n/a

### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)

n/a

### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

n/a

enrichment.impact: Ensures label consistency across the project, prevents user confusion when interpreting API server identity leases, and aligns the implementation with upcoming documentation and registration processes.

other.author: mgoltzsche
other.userFacingChange: upgrade go-jose to v2.6.0

issueContext.title: Update go-jose version
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

The go-jose dependency version should be updated from v2.2.2 to v2.6.0.

### Why is this needed?

This is to make the kubernetes code compatible with newer go-jose v2 versions that have a small breaking change: `jwt.NewNumericDate()` returns a pointer in newer versions which breaks the kubernetes code [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.0-alpha.2/pkg/serviceaccount/claims.go#L93):
```
/go/pkg/mod/github.com/k3s-io/kubernetes@v1.26.0-k3s1/pkg/serviceaccount/claims.go:93:29: cannot use jwt.NewNumericDate(now.Add(time.Duration(warnafter) * time.Second)) (value of type *jwt.NumericDate) as type jwt.NumericDate in assignment
```
For instance this prevents using the kubernetes apiserver and [ory/fosite](https://github.com/ory/fosite/tree/v0.44.0) together within the same Go codebase.

enrichment.problem: Updating go-jose to v2.6.0 introduced a breaking change where jwt.NewNumericDate now returns a *jwt.NumericDate instead of a value. Kubernetes code in pkg/serviceaccount/claims.go expected a value type, causing compilation errors for projects that compile Kubernetes with the newer go-jose version (e.g., when using the apiserver together with ory/fosite).
enrichment.affected: Projects compiling the Kubernetes API server or other components that use the serviceaccount JWT code, especially when combined with libraries like ory/fosite that depend on newer go-jose versions.
enrichment.fix: The Kubernetes repository upgrades its go-jose dependency to v2.6.0 and updates the affected code to handle the pointer return type, restoring compatibility and allowing successful compilation with the newer library.
enrichment.impact: Developers can now build and run the Kubernetes API server (and any components that rely on serviceaccount JWT handling) with go-jose v2.6.0, eliminating the compile‑time break and enabling integration with other libraries such as ory/fosite.

issueContext.title: dynamic resource allocation: rename PodScheduling
issueContext.body:
The name is not ideal. This already came up during the initial API review and again in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3063#issuecomment-1336225191:

@sftim wrote:
> Pretty much everything that has a kind in Kubernetes looks broadly idiomatic if you put a definite or indefinite article in front of it. However, PodScheduling is a bit weird.
> 
> (Fictional) examples:
> 
>  -   “the driver watches for a PodScheduling that matches this driver's resource type”
>  -    “you can use the kubectl tool to manually delete the PodScheduling”
>  -    “the PodScheduling has an ownerReference to the Pod and is therefore a dependent object of that Pod”

My own proposal was `PodSchedulingState`.

@sftim had some more:

- PodSchedulingHint
- PodSchedulingReservation
- ProvisionalPodBinding

issueContext.title: KeyEncipherment usage should not be required for non-RSA kubelet client/serving CSRs
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

https://github.com/golang/go/issues/36499 describes why the KeyEncipherment extended key usage does not make sense (and in some cases, is not allowed) for ECDSA keys.

The Kubernetes `kubernetes.io/kubelet-serving` and `kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client-kubelet` signer names require a `key encipherment` usage.

If the kubelet is not using an RSA key (which it does not [by default](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.23.0/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/util/certificate/certificate_manager.go#L640-L642)), it should not need to specify this key usage.

Since relaxing this to make the `key encipherment` usage optional for those two signerNames may involve an API validation change, this may need rollout over 2 releases. The places we'll need to make sure work properly are:

1. API validation of CSR create and update requests
2. Controller tolerating CSR objects with/without that usage
3. Kubelets requesting CSRs properly without that usage if given a non-RSA key

issueContext.title: Kube-proxy does not validate `healthz` state when answering to HC for eTP:Local
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

KEP https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3837 outlined the fact that Kube-proxy today doesn't perform any validation of its `healthz` state when answering to load balancer HCs for eTP:Local services.

This is a potential problem, because if Kube-proxy is unhealthy then it might also not be writing the rules needed to forward traffic to the endpoint on the node. This means that it might indicate to a load balancer that it should forward traffic to the node, simply because the endpoint is scheduled there



### What did you expect to happen?

Kube-proxy should perform the same validation it currently does for eTP:Local services (i.e: validate that the service has an endpoint scheduled and ready on the node) but AND it with its `healthz` state. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a service of `type: LoadBalancer` + `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`
2. Trigger an issue with Kube-proxy which causes it to fail when writing its rules on the node 
3. Spin up a pod for this service
4. Validate that Kube-proxy continues to indicate to the load balancer that it should send the node traffic, even though it hasn't been able to write the rules required as a consequence of 3. due to 2.

issueContext.title: kubelet event about unattached volumes is incorrect
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

1. Create Pod with unattachable volume A and B and make A unable to mount
2. The Pod will be in `ContainerCreating` state
3. Wait for several minutes, then show the pod events by `kubectl describe pod`
4. The events information includes error msg like
    ```shell
     Warning  FailedMount  3m48s (x2 over 6m2s)  kubelet            Unable to attach or mount volumes: unmounted volumes=[A], unattached volumes=[A, B]: timed out waiting for the condition
    ```
5. The error msg is confusing since it indicates that A and B are unattached

### What did you expect to happen?

The events show correct information about unmounted volumes and unattached volumes.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Use following yaml and do the test as posted above:

```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: myapp
  labels:
    name: myapp
spec:
  containers:
  - name: myapp
    image: nginx
    resources:
      limits:
        memory: "128Mi"
        cpu: "500m"
    volumeMounts:
      - name: test-cm1
        mountPath: /test-cm1
      - name: test-cm2
        mountPath: /test-cm2
      - name: test-ebs
        mountPath: /test-ebs
  volumes:
    - name: test-cm1  # unattachable, succeed to mount
      configMap:
        name: test-cm1
    - name: test-cm2  # unattachable, fail to mount
      configMap:
        name: noexist
    - name: test-ebs   # attachable, fail to attach and mount
      awsElasticBlockStore:
        volumeID: "test"
        fsType: ext4
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: test-cm1
data:
  key: value
```
The event will be like:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/44308864/192127331-ace9ed02-dc5d-41f1-8420-0a6bf06c20cf.png)


### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
# paste output here
```

</details>


### Cloud provider

enrichment.problem: When a pod is force deleted, if the container runtime returns an error while terminating the pod, the kubelet may not finish the pod removal until it is restarted, leaving mirror and runtime pods lingering (orphaned). This was especially observed with static pods that use fixed UIDs.
enrichment.affected: Force‑deleted pods, static pods (especially those with fixed UIDs), and any workloads that rely on rapid pod configuration updates. Cluster operators monitoring pod health are also affected.
enrichment.fix: Added stronger runtime‑failure testing and a more rigorous reconciliation loop in the kubelet so that static pods are reliably restarted even after termination errors. The reconciliation latency for static‑pod restarts was reduced (≈2 s vs 4 s). Also introduced an alpha metric `kubelet_known_pods` to expose pod counts in internal states, helping operators detect orphaned pods.
enrichment.impact: Pods are now cleaned up promptly without requiring a kubelet restart, preventing resource leaks and improving the speed of static‑pod updates. Operators gain visibility into pod‑state anomalies via the new metric.

issueContext.title: PVC recreation needed when Stateful set Pod stuck in pending
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

- User cordons a node with a pvc bound to a local persistent volume
- User deletes a stateful set pod from that node
- The pod is in pending because the pvc is still bound to a local pv on the cordoned node (expected)
- The node dies and the pvc is deleted
- The pod is still stuck in pending because the pvc is missing (bug)

The pod now needs to be manually deleted so that the pod+pvc can be recreated

### What did you expect to happen?

After the pvc was deleted, the statefulset controller should have recreated it and bound it to a new node's local pv so that the pending pod could be scheduled. Currently the only way to get the pod out of pending is to manually delete it so that it recreates itself and its pvc

We used https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/sig-storage-local-static-provisioner for the local PVs, but the problem is not limited to this particular provisioner

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- create a stateful set with a pvc that is bound to a local PV
- use `kubectl cordon` to cordon a node with a local pv
- delete a statefulset pod from that node
- delete the pvc from that node

the pod is now stuck in pending due to a missing pvc

### Anything else we need to know?

There was a related issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/74374 but this only fixed the issue when the order of operations was delete pvc -> delete pod. but in this case, it is delete pod -> delete pvc

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"25", GitVersion:"v1.25.2", GitCommit:"5835544ca568b757a8ecae5c153f317e5736700e", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2022-09-21T14:25:45Z", GoVersion:"go1.19.1", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/arm64"}
Kustomize Version: v4.5.7
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"21+", GitVersion:"v1.21.9-dd.1", GitCommit:"d9705166e190927de148edae148bf46471c7f8d5", GitTreeState:"c

enrichment.problem: When a StatefulSet pod is deleted while its PVC is bound to a local PV on a cordoned node, and the node later dies causing the PVC to be deleted, the pod remains in Pending because the missing PVC is not automatically recreated. This forces users to manually delete the pod to trigger PVC recreation.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running StatefulSets with PersistentVolumeClaims, especially those using local PVs, where pods can become stuck in Pending due to missing PVCs.
enrichment.fix: The controller now automatically recreates missing PVCs for Pods that are in Pending state. If a PVC disappears, the pod’s PVC will be reissued and bound to a suitable volume, allowing the pod to be scheduled without manual intervention.
enrichment.impact: StatefulSet workloads that rely on local or other PVs will recover automatically from node failures or PVC deletions, reducing downtime and operational overhead. Pods no longer get stuck in Pending, improving reliability of stateful applications.

issueContext.title: informers: provide a way to know when a resource handler has "synced"
issueContext.body:
Currently, informers expose a `HasSynced` method.
This asserts that one full List has been synced to the informers *store*.

However, this does not give any guarantees about *handlers* being called.

It is fairly common to need to know that the handlers have been called for the initial state.
However, there is currently no way to access this.

Slack context: https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C0EG7JC6T/p1591115369066700

## Sync state

A common question is "What happens if an object is created during the initial sync? Why would we care about the initial state specifically?"

The issue is one of eventually consistency. If I apply, say, a NetworkPolicy, it may not be actuated for some time - its perfectly reasonable for a controller to not process it for O(seconds). However, if I apply a NetworkPolicy 1 year ago, then restart my controller, it *must* be applied; a small blip in policy enforcement is a CVE. A correct controller implementation needs to ensure the initial state is fully synced before operating.

## Current solutions


* The naive option is to just use `informer.HasSynced`. This works if controllers are operating under Listers (or similar) only, rather than event handlers, as the `HasSynced` applies to the underlying store. This is *close enough* that many controllers probably do this while relying on event handlers, improperly, and don't notice that in rare cases the event handlers lag behind.

  Example (broken) implementation:

  <details>

  ```go
  func TestInformerRace(t *testing.T) {
    kc := fake.NewSimpleClientset(pods...)
    informers := informers.NewSharedInformerFactory(kc, 0)
    handled := &atomic.Int32{}
    podInformer := informers.Core().V1().Pods().Informer()
    podInformer.AddEventHandler(cache.ResourceEventHandlerFuncs{
      AddFunc: func(obj any) {
        handled.Add(1)
      },
    })

    stop := make(chan struct{})
    informers.Start(stop)
    WaitForInformerFactorySync(stop, informer

enrichment.problem: Shared informers' HasSynced only indicated that the store had performed an initial List, but provided no guarantee that event handlers had been called for those items, making it impossible for controllers to know when their handler logic had processed the initial state.
enrichment.affected: Controllers that rely on informer event handlers for initial state (e.g., network policy, auth, workload controllers) may have previously missed initial events.
enrichment.fix: The shared informer now propagates its sync state to each individual informer, exposing a new HasSynced method for handlers. Additionally, a new AsyncTracker utility is added to help controllers track completion of work for items received during the initial list.
enrichment.impact: Controllers can reliably wait until their event handlers have processed the initial object list before acting, preventing missed processing of existing resources and reducing gaps in policy enforcement or other controller logic, improving correctness and security.

issueContext.title: windows cpu maximum incorrect with more than one processor group
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

When submitting a windows pod using resource limits on a node with more than one processor group, the specified `CpuMaximum` count is incorrect due to the usage of `runtime.NumCPU()` which does not take processor groups into account.

For example:
- node with 96 cores
- cpu limit 94
- `runtime.NumCPU()` returns `48`

This results in a CPU maximum of 10000 since the range is from [1, 10000]:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_container_windows.go#L82..L91

```go
	limit := int64(94 * 1000)
	numCPU := 48
	fmt.Println(((10000 * limit) / int64(numCPU) / 1000))

// Output:
// 19583
```

Our initial goal for this was to limit a process to not use all available CPU and therefore render the node uncontrollable. 

### What did you expect to happen?

A CPU maximum of `9791` instead of `10000` for that specific case. For the calculation, it should use the CPU count for all available processor groups instead of just the current one. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Launch a node with a lot of CPUs, for example [a Azure Standard_D96a_v4](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/dav4-dasv4-series) and schedule the following pod on it:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: debug-windows
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - args:
    - ping /t 127.0.0.1
    command:
    - cmd
    - /c
    image: mcr.microsoft.com/windows/nanoserver:1809
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    name: main
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: "94"
        memory: 300Gi
      requests:
        cpu: "90"
        memory: 200Gi
  nodeSelector:
    kubernetes.io/os: windows
```

Then SSH into the node and inspect the running container using `crictl.exe inspect <id>`. The `cpu_maximum` value will be set to 10000. 

### Anything else we need to know?

[tklauser/numcpus](https://github.com/tklause

enrichment.problem: On Windows nodes with more than 64 logical processors (multiple processor groups), kubelet calculated CPU limits using runtime.NumCPU(), which only reports CPUs in the current group. This caused the CpuMaximum value to be incorrect (often defaulting to 10000), allowing pods to exceed intended CPU limits.
enrichment.affected: Windows nodes with >64 logical processors and any pod that specifies a CPU limit on those nodes.
enrichment.fix: The CPU limit calculation now uses the total number of logical processors across all processor groups on the node instead of runtime.NumCPU(), ensuring the correct CpuMaximum is computed for Windows pods.
enrichment.impact: CPU limits are now correctly enforced on high‑core Windows nodes, preventing pods from over‑consuming CPU and potentially destabilizing the node.

issueContext.title: Data race when creating isomorphic Events with an "k8s.io/client-go/tools/events".EventRecorder
issueContext.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

I wrote a test creating multiple isomorphic Events with an "k8s.io/client-go/tools/events".[EventRecorder](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/tools/events/interfaces.go#L26) and stumbled upon a data race.

The data race happens in the [recordToSink](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.18.2/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go#L153) function. It seems that the Event Series field can be read and written at the same time by two different goroutines. [Read](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.18.2/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go#L178) [Write](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.18.2/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go#L168-L171).

This seems to happen in only one scenario:
- (1) a singleton Event is created
- (2) an isomorphic Event is created
- (1) lock addition to cache
- (2) wait for the lock to be released
- (1) unlock
- (2) lock + [create](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.18.2/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go#L168-L171) the Series
- (1) [read](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/v0.18.2/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go#L209) the freshly created Series
- (1) singleton Event is now considered as a series

That being said, this seems to lead to some data inconsistencies as the singleton Event would be created with an unexpected Series.

<details>
<summary>Data race</summary>
|==================
WARNING: DATA RACE
Write at 0x00c0001237a0 by goroutine 23:
  k8s.io/client-go/tools/events.(*eventBroadcasterImpl).recordToSink.func1.1()
      /home/damien/go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/client-go@v0.25.0/tools/events/event_broadcaster.go:183 +0x536
  k8s.io/client-go/tools/events.(*event

enrichment.problem: A data race occurred in the client-go event recorder when multiple isomorphic (similar) Events were emitted consecutively, leading to concurrent reads and writes of the Event Series field.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes component or custom controller that records Events via `k8s.io/client-go/tools/events.EventRecorder`, such as kubelet, scheduler, controller-manager, and user‑written controllers.
enrichment.fix: The race condition in the `recordToSink` path was eliminated by synchronizing access to the Event Series field, ensuring safe concurrent handling of successive similar Events.
enrichment.impact: Event recording is now reliable for all components that use the `EventRecorder` (e.g., controllers, kubelet, scheduler). This prevents possible panics or inconsistent event series, improving observability and debugging.

issueContext.title: Static pods stopped first when priority is not explicitly set
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

etcd / kube-apiserver stops before most containers, despite using `shutdownGracePeriodByPodPriority`.
On a single node server, with multus (and likely other CNI talking to the API), this spam the logs and make the shutdown slower

### What did you expect to happen?

`shutdownGracePeriodByPodPriority` should stop one group at a time

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

On a single node cluster, have a slow to shutdown pod (sleep inf), look at the logs to see in which order they are killed

### Anything else we need to know?

```
shutdownGracePeriodByPodPriority:
  - priority: 2000000001
    shutdownGracePeriodSeconds: 10
  - priority: 2000000000
    shutdownGracePeriodSeconds: 10
  - priority: 0
    shutdownGracePeriodSeconds: 60
```

Reading the kep https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/2712-pod-priority-based-graceful-node-shutdown, the summary says `Kubelet graceful shutdown should take the pod priority values into account to determine the order in which the pods are stopped.` so I would expect all pods with priority between 0 and 2000000000 to be stopped first, then coredns (2000000000), then the rest.

This is definitely not what's happening:
```
Nov 15 21:02:02 atsc2 kubelet[9573]: I1115 21:02:02.083004    9573 nodeshutdown_manager_linux.go:134] "Creating node shutdown manager" shutdownGracePeriodRequested="0s" shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods="0s" shutdownGracePeriodByPodPriority=[{Priority:0 ShutdownGracePeriodSeconds:60} {Priority:2000000000 ShutdownGracePeriodSeconds:10} {Priority:2000000001 ShutdownGracePeriodSeconds:10}]
...
Nov 15 21:06:09 atsc2 kubelet[9573]: I1115 21:06:09.372579    9573 kuberuntime_container.go:722] "Killing container with a grace period" pod="kube-system/kube-scheduler-atemeappliance" podUID=81872379106beaec249553e0efae9ec6 containerName="kube-scheduler" containerID="containerd://282605472eed19f2d131d9805b6616682c677af2ab281be0763d55

enrichment.problem: Static control plane pods (e.g., etcd, kube-apiserver) were stopped before other workloads during node shutdown because their manifests lacked an explicit numeric priority, even though they used `priorityClassName: system-node-critical`. This broke the expected graceful shutdown order defined by `shutdownGracePeriodByPodPriority`.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using static control‑plane pods (created by kubeadm) that rely on `system-node-critical` priority, especially during node termination or reboot.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now writes an explicit `priority` field into static pod manifests that use `priorityClassName: system-node-critical`. This ensures kubelet can correctly sort pods by priority during shutdown.
enrichment.impact: Node shutdown becomes orderly: critical control‑plane pods stay alive longer, reducing API downtime, log spam, and overall shutdown time. Improves reliability for single‑node clusters and any environment relying on graceful shutdown.

issueContext.title: e2e conformance pod sending total tests back as zero for conformance image 1.25.x
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Our team uses sonobuoy to run the conformormance tests on a cluster and displays the results to the users.
We have been using conformance image 1.21.x until now and it sends back progress data to sonobuoy pod and our service reads it from the sonobuoy pod.
The progress data included the total number of tests to be run and the completed tests. For 1.21 conformance we were receiving this data properly but when switching to 1.25.x conformance we are getting the total tests as zero. This is causing issues in our UI.
Not sure what version of conformance image introduced this but we were using 1.21 and started seeing this issue after moving to 1.25.x. The conformance image versions in between 1.21 -1.25 are not CVE free so we cannot use them.

### What did you expect to happen?

Total number of tests should be non-zero for conformance image 1.25.x. Ideally i think it should come back as 360.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- provision a 1.25 kubernetes kind (or anything else) cluster
- Install sonobuoy 
- Run conformance scan on the cluster
- Check the annotation on the sonobuoy pod ` sonobuoy.hept.io/status` . This is set by sonobuoy based on the data it gets back from the e2e conformance pod.
- The total tests comes as zero

### Anything else we need to know?

I just found it on 1.25.x conformance. Not really sure when this was introduced. Need to make sure back dated versiosn also have this fix in case they have this issue.

### Kubernetes version

<details>
1.25 cluster with 1.25.x conformance with any sonobuoy version
```console
$ kubectl version
# paste output here
```

</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>
ANY
</details>


### OS version

<details>

```console
# On Linux:
$ cat /etc/os-release
# paste output here
$ uname -a
# paste output here

# On Windows:
C:\> wmic os get Caption, Version, BuildNumber, OSArchitecture
# paste output here
```

</details>


### Install

enrichment.problem: When running the conformance test image for Kubernetes 1.25, the test pod reports the total number of tests as zero, causing UI progress displays (e.g., Sonobuoy) to show incorrect progress information.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running the 1.25 (or later) conformance image, and any CI/CD or monitoring pipelines that consume Sonobuoy progress annotations.
enrichment.fix: The total test specification is now provided via `ProgressReporter` and emitted before the test suite starts, ensuring the correct non‑zero total test count is reported to consumers.
enrichment.impact: Users of Sonobuoy or any tooling that relies on test progress data can now see accurate total test counts, restoring correct progress UI and enabling reliable monitoring of conformance test runs.

bugOrRegression.description: kubeadm: fixed the bug where `kubeadm` always does CRI detection even if it is not required by a phase subcommand
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: kubeadm: fix the bug that kubeadm always do CRI detection even if it is not required by a phase subcommand

enrichment.problem: kubeadm performed Container Runtime Interface (CRI) detection for every phase subcommand, even when the subcommand did not require a CRI, leading to unnecessary processing and potential failures when a CRI binary was absent.
enrichment.affected: Users invoking kubeadm phase subcommands (e.g., `kubeadm init phase …`) in clusters where a CRI is not needed or not installed.
enrichment.fix: Added logic to skip CRI detection unless the invoked phase subcommand explicitly requires it, restoring the original behavior of phase commands.
enrichment.impact: Phase subcommands run faster and no longer fail in environments without a CRI, improving usability of kubeadm's advanced init phases.

bugOrRegression.author: alexzielenski
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Fixes a 1.26 regression in the alpha Aggregated Discovery feature that can cause a stuck apiserver if an aggregated apiservice returned 304 Not Modified for aggregated discovery information

The problem caused a race condition where application gets intermittent permission denied error when reading files that were just updated, before the correct permissions were applied.
bugOrRegression.author: tsaarni
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Fixed file permission issues that happened during update of Secret/ConfigMap/projected volume when fsGroup is used. The problem caused a race condition where application gets intermittent permission denied error when reading files that were just updated, before the correct permissions were applied.

issueContext.title: Reading from secret volume occasionally fails with `permission denied`
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Reading files from secret volume fails with `permission denied` because files incorrectly have group owner GID 0 instead of given `fsGroup`.  The failure is associated to a change/update of the files in the secret. Failure happens only occasionally and if checking the volume manually after the error, the problem has disappeared and the files can be read successfully. The ownership is wrong only for a very short while. 

The problem started after applying file permissions `defaultMode: 0440` to the secret volume and the security context with `fsGroup: 10000`. The process that reads the files is NOT running with UID 0 or GID 0.

The problem may be seen as intermittent failure of the application since secrets likely have mandatory data for the application to function normally, such as TLS credentials. Applications are not likely prepared to retry opening the files several times since permission issues are not usually intermittent. 

### What did you expect to happen?

The files on secret volume mount should be readable by the process because:
* Non-root process has privileges to read files owned by group ID 10000 - setting `fsGroup: 10000` adds 10000 to supplementary group IDs of the process
* Files on secret volume should be owned by GID 10000 because `fsGroup: 10000` was set
* The files should have group read permissions set because `defaultMode: 0440` was set

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a small test application that does following

1. Watch the secret volume with inotify
2. Wait for inotify event `IN_MOVED_TO` (which indicates that secret has been updated and atomic rename has executed to replace the files with new ones)
3. Attempt to read files the on the volume
4. Print error to stdout if opening the file fails

Create manifest for the application with following properties

* Run the process as non-root and with GID not equal to 0
* Set `fsGroup` to non-zero e.g. `fsG

enrichment.problem: When a Secret, ConfigMap, or projected volume is updated and the pod uses an fsGroup, the kubelet temporarily sets file group ownership to GID 0. This creates a race condition where the application reads the updated files before the correct group permissions are applied, resulting in intermittent "permission denied" errors.
enrichment.affected: Pods that mount Secret, ConfigMap, or projected volumes with a non‑root user and a defined fsGroup can be affected by intermittent read failures during volume updates.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now correctly applies the specified fsGroup permissions to updated volume files before they become visible to the container, eliminating the race condition.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on Secret/ConfigMap/projected volumes with non‑root users and an fsGroup will no longer experience transient permission errors, improving application stability especially for workloads that need timely access to credentials such as TLS certificates.

bugOrRegression.description:
Added warnings to the Services API. Kubernetes now warns for Services in the case of:
- IPv4 addresses with leading zeros
- IPv6 address in non-canonical format (RFC 5952)
bugOrRegression.author: aojea
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange:
Add warnings to the Services API. Kubernetes now warns for Services in the case of:
- IPv4 addresses with leading zeros
- IPv6 address in non-canonical format (RFC 5952)

enrichment.problem: Service objects could be created with IPv4 addresses that include leading zeros or IPv6 addresses that are not in the canonical RFC 5952 format, leading to confusing or non‑standard IP representations.
enrichment.affected: Users defining Service resources (e.g., externalIPs, loadBalancerIP, clusterIP) with improperly formatted IP addresses.
enrichment.fix: The Services API now validates these address formats and emits warnings when an IPv4 address contains leading zeros or an IPv6 address is not in canonical form.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators receive immediate feedback about non‑standard IP formats, reducing misconfigurations and aligning service IPs with networking standards.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed an issue where failed pods associated with a job with `parallelism = 1` are recreated by the job controller honoring exponential backoff delay again. However, for jobs with `parallelism > 1`, pods might be created without exponential backoff delay.
bugOrRegression.author: nikhita
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Fix regression in 1.25 default configurations so failed pods associated with a job with `parallelism = 1` are recreated by the job controller honoring exponential backoff delay again. However, for jobs with `parallelism > 1`, pods might be created without exponential backoff delay.

enrichment.problem: The job controller stopped honoring the exponential backoff delay when recreating failed pods for Jobs with `parallelism = 1`, causing immediate restarts after failures.
enrichment.affected: Users running batch Jobs with `parallelism = 1` that expect exponential backoff on pod failures. The change also clarifies behavior for Jobs with higher parallelism.
enrichment.fix: Restores the original behavior for Jobs with `parallelism = 1` so that failed pods are recreated after the configured exponential backoff period. No change for Jobs with `parallelism > 1`.
enrichment.impact: Prevents rapid, uncontrolled restarts of single‑parallelism Jobs, reducing cluster churn and resource pressure, and improving reliability of batch workloads that depend on backoff semantics.

enrichment.problem: Kubelet could panic with a fatal error "concurrent map iteration and map write" when generating device topology hints in the device manager, causing the kubelet process to crash.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running kubelet with the device manager topology hints feature enabled (typically when using device plugins that expose topology information). Pods that request such devices were at risk of causing a kubelet crash.
enrichment.fix: Added proper synchronization (locking) around the map used in generateDeviceTopologyHints to prevent concurrent iteration and writes, eliminating the race condition that triggered the panic.
enrichment.impact: Stops kubelet crashes on nodes that use the device manager topology hints (e.g., GPUs or other devices exposing NUMA topology). Nodes remain healthy and pods continue to run, avoiding node outages and pod evictions.

bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Hide .metadata.managedFields when describing CRs

enrichment.problem: The `kubectl describe` output for Custom Resources included the `.metadata.managedFields` section, which is verbose and often unnecessary for users, cluttering the command output.
enrichment.affected: Anyone who uses `kubectl describe` on Custom Resources (CRs) in any cluster.
enrichment.fix: `kubectl describe` now suppresses the `.metadata.managedFields` field when displaying Custom Resources, hiding this information by default.
enrichment.impact: Users get cleaner, more readable output when describing CRs, making it easier to focus on relevant resource details. The hidden data can still be accessed via other commands if needed.

bugOrRegression.description: The list-type of the alpha `resourceClaims` field introduced to `Pods` in `1.26.0` was modified from `set` to `map`, resolving an incompatibility with use of this schema in `CustomResourceDefinitions` and with server-side apply.
bugOrRegression.author: JoelSpeed
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Fixes a 1.26 regression in the published openapi of Pod types caused by an incorrect list-type of the alpha resourceClaims field. This fix modifies that field list type from "set" to "map", resolving an incompatibility with use of this schema in CustomResourceDefinitions and with server-side apply.

enrichment.problem: The alpha `resourceClaims` field in Pod spec was defined as a list of type "set" in the OpenAPI schema, which is incompatible with usage in CustomResourceDefinitions and with server-side apply, causing errors for users extending Pods via CRDs or using SSA.
enrichment.affected: Users creating or modifying Pods via CustomResourceDefinitions or server-side apply that include the alpha `resourceClaims` field.
enrichment.fix: The OpenAPI schema for the `resourceClaims` field was corrected to use list type "map" instead of "set", restoring compatibility with CRDs and server-side apply.
enrichment.impact: Users can now define CRDs that embed Pod specs with `resourceClaims` and apply Pods using server-side apply without schema validation failures, ensuring smooth operation of workloads that rely on this alpha field.

issueContext.title: Pod terminating stuck because of trying to umount not actual mounted dir
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

A status of Pod mounted NFS PV remain as terminating when a node shutdown and restart.

### What did you expect to happen?

A Pod is completely terminated.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

### Summary

- Deploy a Pod mounted NFS PV
- Shutdown the node where the Pod is running
- Wait for 5 min and the Pod status become `Terminating`
- Restart the node
- The Pod status is still `Terminating` and the Pod is never terminated completely

<details>

### Reproduce

Prepare a NFS Server.(I used `nfs-kernel-server`)  

Deploy a Pod mounted NFS PV like this.  
`nfs-pv-test-pod.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  labels:
    run: nfs-pv-test-pod
  name: nfs-pv-test-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - image: ubuntu
    name: nfs-pv-test-pod
    command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "while :; do sleep 10; done"]
    volumeMounts:
      - name: nfs-test-volume
        mountPath: "/srv"
  volumes:
    - name: nfs-test-volume
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: nfs-test-pvc
  nodeSelector:
    kubernetes.io/hostname: node02

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: nfs-test-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Mi

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: nfs-test-pv
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 1Mi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  nfs:
    server: <NFS Server IP Address>
    path: <NFS Server Dir Path>
```

```

enrichment.problem: When a node is shut down and later restarted, pods that are terminating and have an NFS (or other) volume try to unmount a directory that is not actually mounted, causing the pod to remain stuck in the Terminating state indefinitely.
enrichment.affected: Pods with NFS (or other) persistent volumes that were terminating when the node went down and came back up. The issue mainly impacts clusters where node reboots can occur while pods are terminating.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now checks whether the target mount point is actually present before attempting the unmount during pod termination, preventing the erroneous unmount call and allowing the pod to complete termination.
enrichment.impact: Pods that use NFS (or similar) volumes will no longer remain stuck in Terminating after a node reboot, freeing resources and avoiding manual cleanup. This improves reliability of workload shutdown and node lifecycle operations.

Additionally, the reserved TEST-NET-2 IPv4 range (198.51.100.0/24) could be mistakenly used for Service ClusterIP or loadBalancerIP, colliding with the address kube-proxy uses for health‑probing.
enrichment.affected: Users running kube-proxy with --proxy-mode=ipvs on nodes with kernels built without module support, and any workloads that define Service IPs from the TEST-NET-2 range.
enrichment.fix: kube-proxy now correctly detects kernels compiled without module support by falling back to checking the kernel config in /boot, allowing ipvs mode to work on statically linked kernels. enrichment.impact: Clusters that run ipvs proxy on statically linked kernels (e.g., certain arm64 or custom builds) can now enable ipvs mode without errors. Service IP allocation is safer, avoiding unexpected probe failures and connectivity issues caused by using the reserved TEST-NET-2 range.

issueContext.title: Add the new kernel scheduler load balance algorithm to ipvs-scheduler option on kube-proxy ipvs-mode
issueContext.body:
The ipvs mode `ipvs-scheduler` limit the scheduler algorithm to :
```
              rr - Round Robin: distributes jobs equally amongst the available real servers.

              wrr - Weighted Round Robin: assigns jobs to real servers  proportionally  to  there
              real  servers'  weight.  Servers with higher weights receive new jobs first and get
              more jobs than servers with lower weights. Servers with equal weights get an  equal
              distribution of new jobs.

              lc - Least-Connection: assigns more jobs to real servers with fewer active jobs.

              wlc  -  Weighted Least-Connection: assigns more jobs to servers with fewer jobs and
              relative to the real servers' weight (Ci/Wi). This is the default.

              lblc - Locality-Based Least-Connection: assigns  jobs  destined  for  the  same  IP
              address to the same server if the server is not overloaded and available; otherwise
              assign jobs to servers with fewer jobs, and keep it for future assignment.

              lblcr - Locality-Based Least-Connection with Replication: assigns jobs destined for
              the  same  IP  address  to  the  least-connection node in the server set for the IP
              address. If all the node in the server set are over loaded, it picks up a node with
              fewer  jobs  in  the  cluster  and  adds it in the sever set for the target. If the
              server set has not been modified for the specified time, the most  loaded  node  is
              removed from the server set, in order to avoid high degree of replication.

              dh  -  Destination Hashing: assigns jobs to servers through looking up a statically
              assigned hash table by their destination IP addresses.

              sh - Source Hashing: assigns jobs  to  servers  through  looking  up  a  statically
              assigned  hash  table  by their source IP addresse

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy in IPVS mode only accepted a fixed set of scheduler algorithms. Configuring an unsupported or newly added kernel scheduler caused kube-proxy to restart with unclear log messages, making it hard for users to adopt new algorithms.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using kube-proxy in IPVS mode that set the ipvs-scheduler flag; especially those wanting to use custom or newer kernel schedulers.
enrichment.fix: kube-proxy now allows any ipvs-scheduler name to be set. If the specified scheduler is not usable, kube-proxy restarts and emits clear log entries indicating the problem (different from previous log printouts).
enrichment.impact: Enables users to configure and test new kernel IPVS scheduling algorithms without code changes, improving flexibility and reducing operational confusion when misconfigurations occur.

bugOrRegression.description: messages of `DisruptionTarget` condition now excludes preemptor pod metadata
bugOrRegression.author: mimowo
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Fix a regression in default 1.26 configurations with the PodDisruptionConditions feature enabled where preemptor pod metadata can be included in the message of DisruptionTarget condition

enrichment.problem: When the PodDisruptionConditions feature is enabled (default in 1.26), the DisruptionTarget condition message incorrectly included metadata from the preemptor pod, leaking internal details and causing confusing status messages.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running Kubernetes 1.26 with the PodDisruptionConditions feature enabled, particularly workloads that experience pod preemption via the scheduler.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now omits preemptor pod metadata from the DisruptionTarget condition message, restoring the intended concise and privacy‑preserving output.
enrichment.impact: Users relying on PodDisruptionBudget status see accurate, less noisy condition messages, avoiding confusion and inadvertent exposure of pod metadata during preemption events.

bugOrRegression.description: Applied configurations can be generated for types with `non-builtin` map fields
bugOrRegression.author: astefanutti
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Apply configurations can be generated for types with non-builtin map fields

enrichment.problem: Apply configuration code generation failed for API types that contain map fields whose value type is not a built‑in type, preventing users from using server‑side apply with those types.
enrichment.affected: Users generating apply configuration types (e.g., client-go code generation) for API types that include non‑builtin map fields.
enrichment.fix: The code generator now supports map fields with non‑builtin element types, allowing apply configuration structs to be generated for such API types.
enrichment.impact: Developers can now generate and use apply configuration objects for a broader set of API types, including CRDs with complex map fields, improving the ergonomics of server‑side apply.

bugOrRegression.description: Excluded preemptor pod metadata in the event message
bugOrRegression.author: mimowo
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Fix regression in 1.23: Do not include preemptor pod metadata in the event message

enrichment.problem: Kube-scheduler regression in v1.23 added preemptor pod metadata to preemption event messages, causing noisy or overly detailed event output.
enrichment.affected: Users who rely on event logs for preemption diagnostics saw extra pod metadata; the regression affected all clusters that enable pod preemption.

issueContext.body:
### What happened?

It "connects" to dockershim
```
DEBU[0000] Connected successfully using endpoint: unix:///var/run/dockershim.sock 
DEBU[0000] VersionRequest: &VersionRequest{Version:v1,} 
E1213 20:22:57.677536   53350 remote_runtime.go:145] "Version from runtime service failed" err="rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = \"transport: Error while dialing dial unix /var/run/dockershim.sock: connect: no such file or directory\""

### What did you expect to happen?

There is no dockershim.sock
```
ERRO[0000] validate service connection: CRI v1 runtime API is not available for endpoint "unix:///var/run/dockershim.sock": rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing dial unix /var/run/dockershim.sock: connect: no such file or directory" 
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run crictl v1.26.0, without setting up /etc/crictl.yaml (or using -r)

* https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cri-tools/issues/1041

### Anything else we need to know?

Worked in crictl v1.25.0, that still had CRI v1alpha2

This patch fixed the issue, to make the fallbacks work:

```diff
--- a/vendor/k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/kubelet/cri/remote/remote_runtime.go
+++ b/vendor/k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/kubelet/cri/remote/remote_runtime.go
@@ -122,6 +122,8 @@ func (r *remoteRuntimeService) validateServiceConnection(ctx context.Context, co
 
        } else if status.Code(err) == codes.Unimplemented {
                return fmt.Errorf("CRI v1 runtime API is not implemented for endpoint %q: %w", endpoint, err)
+       } else if status.Code(err) == codes.Unavailable {
+               return fmt.Errorf("CRI v1 runtime API is not available for endpoint %q: %w", endpoint, err)
        }
 
        return nil
```

### Kubernetes version

<details>
v1.26.0
</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>
Lima
</details>

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed the regression that introduced 34s timeout for DELETECOLLECTION calls
bugOrRegression.author: tkashem
bugOrRegression.userFacingChange: Fix the 1.21 regression that introduced 34s timeout for DELETECOLLECTION calls

issueContext.title: Deletecollection failing after 34 seconds
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

In a cluster with large enough numbers of objects, it seems to be impossible to clean them up with `deletecollection`.  Because the deletecollection is failing while listing the objects from etcd.  The failure happens after exactly 34 seconds, due to the 34-second max timeout introduced in PR #96901 (cc @tkashem for insight on that PR).



### What did you expect to happen?

The deletecollection should be able to run for longer, and succeed.

I recognise that there are still risks of the API server using too much RAM, if deleting a very large collection due to issue #90743.  But, until _that_ issue is fixed, it seems like allowing `deletecollection` to run for longer might be a good idea.  As far as I can tell, the 34 second timeout does not apply to normal LIST calls, so on that basis I feel it should not apply to the giant unchunked LIST call that happens inside `deletecollection`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a few hundred thousand objects of some particular type.  (Argo workflowtaskresults happen to be the type I'm looking at while I write this)
2. Call deletecollection. (Optionally passing some kind of fieldSelector, but I don't think that's essential)
3. Observe that a 504 failure code is logged in kube-audit logs, and that a log entry similar to this is logged by the API Server `"List etcd3" key:<some key>,...,limit:0 ... (total time: 34000ms)`  (In practice, the total time may be a little over 34000 ms).
4. As far as I can tell, the delete collection really has failed at this point.  I notice that PR #96901 says that, in general, "The go-routine can keep running, while the timeout logic will return a timeout to the client" but I don't _think_ that's what's happening here.  I think that, because the 34 sec timeout is used in the context of the etcd call, the etcd list call really does fail, and so the code never proceeds to actually deleting anything.



### Anything else we nee

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced a hard 34‑second timeout for DELETECOLLECTION requests in the API server. When deleting very large collections, the request timed out during the internal unchunked LIST from etcd, returning a 504 error.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that relies on DELETECOLLECTION to remove large numbers of objects, such as batch jobs, controllers, or custom cleanup scripts, especially in clusters with high object counts.
enrichment.fix: The API server timeout for DELETECOLLECTION is restored to its pre‑regression behavior, allowing the operation to run longer and complete successfully for large collections.
enrichment.impact: Users can now clean up large numbers of resources (e.g., hundreds of thousands of objects) with `kubectl delete --all` or programmatic DELETECOLLECTION calls without hitting a 34‑second timeout, reducing failed clean‑up jobs and audit‑log errors.

issueContext.title: When expanding volume during mount make sure that node_stage is always set
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

When a pod is quickly deleted and re-created on a node, it may not be necessary to unstage the volume and in which case only node-publish is called for the volume.

When this happens - stage_path won't be set for `NodeExpandVolume` RPC call because volume was *not* staged even though, volume does have `NODE_STAGE_UNSTAGE` capability. 

We should try and fix this behaviour so that - node_stage_path is always set in `NodeExpandVolume` RPC call. 

### What did you expect to happen?

We should try and fix this behaviour so that - node_stage_path is always set in `NodeExpandVolume` RPC call.

Quickly delete and recreate a pod

issueContext.title: structured-merge-diff supports only  'set' type for associative list
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

kube-apiserver has has this kind of entries in log
```
E0126 00:39:45.253562       1 fieldmanager.go:210] "[SHOULD NOT HAPPEN] failed to update managedFields" err="failed to convert new object (default/test-inline-claim; /v1, Kind=Pod) to smd typed: .spec.containers[name=\"with-resource\"].resources.claims: element 0: associative list without keys has an element that's a map type" VersionKind="/, Kind=" namespace="default" name="test-inline-claim"
E0126 00:39:46.700727       1 fieldmanager.go:210] "[SHOULD NOT HAPPEN] failed to update managedFields" err="failed to convert new object (default/test-inline-claim-resource; resource.k8s.io/v1alpha1, Kind=ResourceClaim) to smd typed: .status.reservedFor: element 0: associative list without keys has an element that's a map type" VersionKind="/, Kind=" namespace="default" name="test-inline-claim-resource"
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected those lines not to appear in kube-apiserver logs, and structured-merge-diff to support map types, like the comment says at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/vendor/sigs.k8s.io/structured-merge-diff/v4/typed/helpers.go#L233

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I ran into it during Dynamic Resource Allocation usage. It requires a either a CRI-O v1.23, or containerd 1.7+ (has to be built from git at the moment); the cluster has to be initialized "DynamicResourceAllocation" feature-gate and alpha apis enabled, for instance with this config for kubeadm :
<details>

```YAML
apiVersion: kubeadm.k8s.io/v1beta3
kind: ClusterConfiguration
kubernetesVersion: v1.26.0
imageRepository: registry.local
apiServer:
  extraArgs:
    feature-gates: "DynamicResourceAllocation=true"
    runtime-config: "api/alpha=true"
controllerManager:
  extraArgs:
    feature-gates: "DynamicResourceAllocation=true"
scheduler:
  extraArgs:
    "feature-gates": "DynamicResourceAllocation=true"
---
apiVersion: kube

enrichment.problem: When using the v1alpha1 ResourceClaim API (e.g., with Dynamic Resource Allocation), the apiserver logged confusing errors like ".status.reservedFor: element 0: associative list without keys has an element that's a map type" because validation allowed the same UID to be reused in multiple reservedFor entries, which StructuredMergeDiff cannot handle.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that enable the DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate and use the v1alpha1 ResourceClaim API (e.g., pods with inline resource claims) saw unnecessary error logs in kube-apiserver.
enrichment.fix: Added stricter validation to the ResourceClaim API that rejects duplicate UID usage across reservedFor entries, preventing the malformed associative list and eliminating the spurious apiserver log messages.
enrichment.impact: Reduces noisy, misleading log entries in kube-apiserver, making debugging easier and ensuring proper validation of ResourceClaim objects. No functional behavior change for workloads, but improves observability for users of Dynamic Resource Allocation.

issueContext.title: Cannot create ingress with ingressClass annotation and IngressClassName both set
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

An ingress resource with both `kubernetes.io/ingress.class` annotation and `spec.ingressClassName` set cannot be **created**. Ingress resources can be updated to include both the annotation and the `ingressClassName` without issue.

Kubernetes response:

> The Ingress "example-ingress" is invalid: annotations.kubernetes.io/ingress.class: Invalid value: "nginx": can not be set when the class field is also set



### What did you expect to happen?

The ingress should be deployed with both annotation and `spec.ingressClassName` set, as it is supported by updating an existing ingress.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Apply this resource:

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: example-ingress
  annotations:
    ingress.kubernetes.io/rewrite-target: /
    kubernetes.io/ingress.class: "nginx"
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
  - host: test.foo.bar
    http:
      paths:
        - path: /
          pathType: Prefix
          backend:
            service:
              name: dummy-service
              port:
                number: 1234

```

### Anything else we need to know?

The code causing this issue is here:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f166a525737e700d12da56833388af72585d4239/pkg/apis/networking/validation/validation.go#L279

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
# Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"25", GitVersion:"v1.25.0", GitCommit:"a866cbe2e5bbaa01cfd5e969aa3e033f3282a8a2", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2022-08-23T17:36:43Z", GoVersion:"go1.19", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/arm64"}
# Kustomize Version: v4.5.7
# Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"21+", GitVersion:"v1.21.14-eks-fb459a0", GitCommit:"b07006b2e59857b13fe5057a956e86225f0e82b7", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2022-10-24T20:32:54Z", GoVersion:"go1.16.15", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
`

enrichment.problem: Ingress resources could not be created when both the `kubernetes.io/ingress.class` annotation and `spec.ingressClassName` were set, resulting in a validation error.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where users define Ingress objects with both the legacy `kubernetes.io/ingress.class` annotation and the `spec.ingressClassName` field (e.g., during migration or multi‑controller setups).
enrichment.fix: The API validation logic was updated to allow creation of Ingress objects that specify both the annotation and the `ingressClassName` field.

issueContext.title: CSI migration race condition can cause unexpected detach and data loss
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

After the cluster was updated to enable PD CSI Driver, there was a race condition where AD Controller (kube-controller-manager) started to [populate the desired state of world](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dc2898b20c6bd9602ae1c3b51333e2e4640ed249/pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/attach_detach_controller.go#L438-L447) BEFORE the PD CSI Driver was up, thus AD Controller gave us the error 

```
Error creating spec for volume "elasticsearch", pod "XXX"/"elasticsearch-0": error performing CSI migration checks and translation for PVC "dXX"/"elasticsearch-elasticsearch-0": in-tree plugin kubernetes.io/gce-pd is migrated on node gke-stage-XXXXX but driver pd.csi.storage.gke.io is not installed.
```

Then AD Controller triggered the disk detach because the disk/volume was not populated in the desired state of world.

Unfortunately the disk was in use during this detach and got corrupted.

### What did you expect to happen?

Since cluster upgrades can cause the controller manager and CSI drivers to start at different times, the AD controller needs to be more conservative when detaching

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

We have not been able to reproduce this, it came up from a customer.

### Anything else we need to know?

/sig storage
/assign @mattcary

<details>
k8s 1.23, CSI migration enabled
</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>
GKE
</details>


### OS version

<details>

```console
# On Linux:
$ cat /etc/os-release
# paste output here
$ uname -a
# paste output here

# On Windows:
C:\> wmic os get Caption, Version, BuildNumber, OSArchitecture
# paste output here
```

</details>

</details>


### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)

<details>

</details>


### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

<details>

</details>

enrichment.problem: When CSI migration is enabled, the attach‑detach controller could populate the Desired State of World before the CSI driver was running on the node. This caused the controller to think the volume was unavailable and prematurely detached the in‑use migrated volume, leading to possible data corruption.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use CSI‑migrated volumes (e.g., GCE PD) on nodes where the CSI driver is not yet running, especially during upgrades with CSI migration enabled.
enrichment.fix: The attach‑detach controller now adds CSI‑migrated volumes to the Desired State of World even if the CSI driver is not yet up and ready on the node, preventing premature detach until the driver becomes available.
enrichment.impact: Prevents unexpected volume detachments and possible data loss during cluster upgrades or node restarts where the CSI driver starts after the controller manager. Improves reliability for workloads that rely on CSI‑migrated storage (e.g., GCE PD).

issueContext.title: Pod terminating stuck because of trying to umount not actual mounted dir
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

A status of Pod mounted NFS PV remain as terminating when a node shutdown and restart.

### What did you expect to happen?

A Pod is completely terminated.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

### Summary

- Deploy a Pod mounted NFS PV
- Shutdown the node where the Pod is running
- Wait for 5 min and the Pod status become `Terminating`
- Restart the node
- The Pod status is still `Terminating` and the Pod is never terminated completely

<details>

### Reproduce

Prepare a NFS Server.(I used `nfs-kernel-server`)  

Deploy a Pod mounted NFS PV like this.  
`nfs-pv-test-pod.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  labels:
    run: nfs-pv-test-pod
  name: nfs-pv-test-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - image: ubuntu
    name: nfs-pv-test-pod
    command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "while :; do sleep 10; done"]
    volumeMounts:
      - name: nfs-test-volume
        mountPath: "/srv"
  volumes:
    - name: nfs-test-volume
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: nfs-test-pvc
  nodeSelector:
    kubernetes.io/hostname: node02

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: nfs-test-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Mi

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: nfs-test-pv
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 1Mi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  nfs:
    server: <NFS Server IP Address>
    path: <NFS Server Dir Path>
```

Shutdown the node where the Pod is running.(In this case `node02`)
```console
root@node02:~# shutdown now
```

And the status of node02 becomes `NotReady`.
```console
$ k get no
NAME     STATUS     ROLES           AGE    VERSION
cp01     Ready      control-plane   126d   v1.25.0
node01   Ready      <none>          126d   v1.25.0
node02   NotReady   <none>          126d   v1.25.0
```

After 5 min later(by default), the Pod status becomes

enrichment.problem: When a node that hosts a pod with an NFS persistent volume is shut down and later restarted, the kubelet attempts to unmount a directory that was never actually mounted. This causes the pod to remain in a Terminating state indefinitely.
enrichment.affected: Pods that mount NFS (or other network) persistent volumes on a node that experiences a shutdown/reboot were unable to terminate, leaving them stuck in the Terminating phase.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet's volume unmount logic was updated to verify that the target path is an actual mount point before attempting to unmount it, preventing futile unmount attempts on non‑existent mounts.
enrichment.impact: Pods using NFS (or similar) volumes will now complete termination correctly after node shutdown or restart, eliminating stuck Terminating pods and freeing associated resources.

issueContext.title: windows kube-proxy: "externalTrafficPolicy: Local" results in no clusterIP entry in windows node
issueContext.body:
I am tracking a changed behavior in networking with kubernetes 1.26. If I create a service of type externalTrafficPolicy: Local, and there are no local endpoints in a node, kube-proxy does not create hns loadbalancers for the clusterIP of that service. 

With kubernetes 1.25, it creates a loadbalancer for clusterIP (but not externalIP). 

This is the relevant log message:
```
"Skipped creating Hns LoadBalancer for cluster ip resources. Reason : all endpoints are terminating" clusterIP="10.114.142.98" nodeport=31336 allEndpointsTerminating=true 
```

Looks like this comes with a result from a new function isAllEndpointsTerminating introduced in kubernetes 1.26.

In Linux, we can still access clusterIP even if there are no local endpoints for the service. Thoughts?

The end result is that in Windows, clients cannot access the clusterIP of such a service with there are no local endpoints.

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.26 the Windows kube-proxy (Winkernel Proxier) stopped creating HNS LoadBalancers for the ClusterIP of a Service when `externalTrafficPolicy` is set to `Local` and all endpoints are remote, causing the ClusterIP to be unreachable on Windows nodes.
enrichment.affected: Windows nodes running kube-proxy (Winkernel Proxier) with Services that have `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` and no local endpoints.
enrichment.fix: The proxy logic was updated to no longer treat a set of only remote endpoints as “all terminating”. It now creates the necessary HNS LoadBalancer for the ClusterIP even when no local endpoints exist, restoring the previous 1.25 behavior.
enrichment.impact: Windows nodes can again reach services via their ClusterIP when using `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`, preventing service disruption for workloads that rely on this configuration.

issueContext.title: PVs with annotations are not being dynamically provisioned on k8s 1.26.1
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

We observed that when deplying manifests to a cluster running 1.26.1-gke.200, the StorageClass and PVC get created successfully. However, the PVC is stuck in a Pending state and no PV is provisioned.

The workaround is to add storageClassName to one of the pending PVCs on cluster, and it did go from Pending to properly provisioned a PV and reaching Bound state. 

We looked at the logs and found that according to the doc: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes/#class,

```
In the past, the annotation volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-class 
was used instead of the storageClassName attribute. This annotation
 is still working; however, it will become fully deprecated in a future 
Kubernetes release.
```

Is this annotation is fully deprecated in the new 1.26.1 release? If yes can we add this detail to documentation or release note?






### What did you expect to happen?

the PVC should not stuck in a Pending state and PV is provisioned in 1.26.1

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a 1.26.1-gke.200 cluster in GKE
2. Create via yaml

```
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: sunnytest-sc
parameters:
  type: pd-ssd
provisioner: kubernetes.io/gce-pd
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: storage-class-issue-test
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: storage-class-issue-test
  serviceName: storage-class-issue-test
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: storage-class-issue-test
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: writer
        image: busybox
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: 100m
            memory: 100Mi
          requests:
            cpu: 10m
            memory: 80Mi
        command:
          - "/bin/sh"
          - "-c"
          - touch

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes incorrectly applied a default StorageClass to a PersistentVolumeClaim even when the deprecated annotation `volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-class` was set, causing PVCs to remain pending and preventing dynamic provisioning.

enrichment.impact: PVCs that rely on the legacy annotation now bind correctly without requiring a manual `storageClassName` addition, restoring expected provisioning behavior for workloads using older manifests.

issueContext.title: Cacher may not send events if it reinitializes at the time of watch initialization
issueContext.body:
Found when reviewing https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116024

I'm still not 100% convinced it's true, but I believe this is a faulty scenario:
1. new watch is being established `Watch()` method
2. `c.ready` is still initialized so we successfully pass the c.ready.wait() check
3. `ListAndWatch` in `startCaching` fails (for whatever reason)
4. `c.ready.set(false)` is called (from defer in `startCaching`)
5. `startCaching` is called again and we call `terminateAllWatchers()`
6. the Watch call (started in point 1 above) only now continues to be processed and is established (and added to watchers) - init events are being send in the meantime
7. `ListAndWatch` is being called from `startCaching` which reinitializes watchCache to a new (higher RV)
8. if some events missed in the meantime, they will not be delivered to this newly established watch

/kind bug
/priority critical-urgent
/sig api-machinery

enrichment.problem: A race condition in kube-apiserver could cause watch API requests to miss events when the server reinitializes its internal watch cache at the same time the watch is being created.
enrichment.affected: Clients that rely on the watch API (e.g., controllers, operators) could miss events, leading to inconsistent view of resources.
enrichment.fix: Added proper synchronization around watch cache reinitialization and watch establishment so that the watch is fully registered before the cache is reset, guaranteeing that no events are dropped during the transition.
enrichment.impact: Watch‑based clients—including controllers, operators, and custom applications—receive a complete event stream, preventing stale state and improving overall cluster reliability.
