issueContext.title: API-initiated eviction does not work on first try in certain scenarios, but does work on second try
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Scenarios that require setting resourceVersion either

- explicitly to the eviction request
- or when the eviction API needs to make sure that the pod has not become ready when deleting unready pods https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/core/pod/storage/eviction.go#L232

fails to evict a pod. This is caused by a conflict with PodDisruptionConditions feature, which adds a condition to a pod, and the delete itself fails. The second eviction works correctly and results in a pod deletion.

### What did you expect to happen?

eviction should succeed on a first try 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. create a simple pod

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: nginx
spec:
  containers:
    - name:  nginx
      image: registry.k8s.io/nginx-slim:0.8
```

```
$ kubectl apply -f nginx.yaml
```

2. obtain its resource version

```
$ kubectl get pod nginx -oyaml | grep resourceVersion
> resourceVersion: "313"
```

3. try to evict it

$ kubectl create -f - <<EOF --raw /api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/nginx/eviction
{"apiVersion": "policy/v1", "kind": "Eviction", "metadata": {"name": "nginx"}, "deleteOptions": {"preconditions": {"resourceVersion": "313"}}}
EOF
$ Error from server (Conflict): Operation cannot be fulfilled on Pod "nginx": the ResourceVersion in the precondition (313) does not match the ResourceVersion in record (425). The object might have been modified

>    status: "False"
>    type: DisruptionTarget
```

4. second eviction with updated resouce version succeeds


```
$ kubectl create -f - <<EO

enrichment.problem: The PodDisruptionConditions feature introduced two regressions: eviction API calls returned spurious precondition (Conflict) errors, requiring a second eviction request to succeed, and dry-run eviction calls incorrectly persisted a DisruptionTarget condition onto the pod being evicted.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that relies on the eviction API (e.g., kubectl evict, controllers performing pod disruption) experienced failures or extra API calls; dry‑run evictions also left incorrect pod conditions.
enrichment.fix: The regressions have been fixed so that eviction requests succeed on the first attempt without false precondition errors, and dry-run evictions no longer add a DisruptionTarget condition to the pod.
enrichment.impact: Users can reliably evict pods (including those with resourceVersion preconditions) with a single API call, and dry‑run evictions no longer leave stray conditions that could interfere with pod status or controllers.

issueContext.title: Mutation of a cached object in kubelet through in place resizing of pods
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/76d351065e504e23b7962158ef0e9067b6bd96ed/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2682

mutates the pod object in place (vs creating a copy first).  That's illegal and can cause data races or potentially panics (the panic is unlikely here but I can't rule it out).

This line should be:

```
pod = updatedPod
...
kl.podManager.UpdatePod(pod)
```

This should be fixed because we might serialize the object in the middle of this from somewhere else and if the object changes midway the protobuf object we create may not be valid, leading to panics in kubelets with this gate turned on.

/sig node
/priority critical-urgent
/kind bug
/assign @vinaykul 

### What did you expect to happen?

No mutation of pod objects from within `Sync*Pod` methods (in fact no mutation of `pod` should occur in most loops).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

N/A

_No response_

enrichment.problem: Kubelet mutated a cached Pod object in place during in‑place pod resizing, violating the expectation that pod objects are immutable in Sync*Pod loops. This could cause data races or panics if the object is serialized while being modified.
enrichment.affected: All nodes running kubelet, especially clusters using the InPlacePodResize feature gate; any workload that triggers in‑place pod resizing could have been impacted.
enrichment.fix: The code now creates a copy of the updated Pod (assigning `pod = updatedPod`) before calling `kl.podManager.UpdatePod(pod)`, eliminating in‑place mutation of the cached object.
enrichment.impact: Eliminates potential data races and panics in kubelet when the InPlacePodResize feature gate is enabled, improving node stability and reliability of pod resize operations.

enrichment.problem: After a node reboot with graceful kubelet shutdown, DaemonSet pods that finish with a Succeeded/Completed phase are not recreated, causing them to remain in Completed state and never restart (regression introduced in Kubernetes 1.27.0-rc.0).

feature.description:
scheduler volumebinding: leveraged `PreFilterResult` to reduce down to only
eligible node(s) for pod with bound claim(s) to local `PersistentVolume(s)`
feature.author: yibozhuang
feature.userFacingChange: scheduler volumebinding: leverage PreFilterResult to reduce down to only eligible node(s) for pod with bound claim(s) to local PersistentVolume(s)

issueContext.title: scheduler volumebinding: leverage PreFilterResult for Bound local PersistentVolumes
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Similar to #109475

Today, in the scheduler volumebinding plugin, the bound PV node affinity check is done during `Filter` stage which means that all nodes are considered.

For the case of bound **local** PV, the PV node affinity spec looks like

```yaml
nodeAffinity:
    required:
      nodeSelectorTerms:
      - matchExpressions:
        - key: kubernetes.io/hostname
          operator: In
          values:
          - node1
```

Today, if the node which the local PV with affinity tied to is tainted and/or out of cpu/memory, etc. we still run through Filter and consider all possible nodes which for a large cluster of n nodes, (n-1)/n nodes are irrelevant.

So, under such case, we see something along the lines of
```
  Type     Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----     ------            ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  3s    default-scheduler  0/100 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {key-fake-0: value-fake-0}, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {key-fake-10: value-fake-10}, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {key-fake-11: value-fake-11}, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {key-fake-12: value-fake-12}, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {key-fake-13: value-fake-13}, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {key-fake-14: value-fake-14}, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {key-fake-15: value-fake-15}, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {key-fake-16: value-fake-16}, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {key-fake-17: value-fake-17}, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {key-fake-18: value-fake-18}, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {key-fake-19: value-fake-19}, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {key-fake-1: value-fake-1}, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {key-fake-20: value-fake-20}, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {key-fake-21: value-fake-21}, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {key-fake-22: value-fake-22}, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {key-fake-23: value-fake-23}, 1 nod ...
```

enrichment.problem: The volumebinding scheduler plugin performed node affinity checks for bound local PersistentVolumes during the Filter stage, causing the scheduler to evaluate every node in the cluster even when only a specific node matches the PV's nodeAffinity, leading to unnecessary computation and noisy scheduling failure messages.
enrichment.affected: Pods that reference bound local PersistentVolumes; clusters with many nodes where such PVs are used.
enrichment.fix: The plugin now uses PreFilterResult to evaluate the PV node affinity earlier and restrict the candidate node set to only those eligible for the bound local PV, so only relevant nodes are considered in the Filter stage.
enrichment.impact: Reduces scheduler latency and CPU usage on large clusters, eliminates irrelevant failure reasons, and improves overall scheduling efficiency for pods that use bound local PersistentVolumes.

feature.description: node `ipam` controller now exposes metrics `cidrset_cidrs_max_total` and `multicidrset_cidrs_max_total` with information about the max number of CIDRs that can be allocated.
feature.author: aryan9600

issueContext.title: Improve ClusterCIDR metrics
issueContext.body:
Opening issue for tracking purpose based on feedback from sig instrumentation

> It might be clearer for admins to expose one metric containing the CIDRs limit and one containing the current number of allocated CIDRs. Otherwise, they will only know that the percentage is high but they won't really know how many allocations they can still make, they would have to look at the configuration in order to get that information.

_Originally posted by @dgrisonnet in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/109090#discussion_r934612254_

enrichment.problem: Cluster administrators could only see the percentage of allocated CIDRs from the node IPAM controller, but had no metric exposing the absolute maximum number of CIDRs that can be allocated, making capacity planning difficult.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and monitoring systems that track IP address usage; any workloads that rely on node IPAM for pod IP allocation.
enrichment.fix: The node IPAM controller now emits two new Prometheus metrics—`cidrset_cidrs_max_total` and `multicidrset_cidrs_max_total`—that report the configured maximum CIDR count for each CIDR set type.
enrichment.impact: Admins can now monitor both current allocation and total capacity, quickly detect when CIDR pools are near exhaustion, and make informed decisions about expanding ClusterCIDR ranges or adjusting configurations.

feature.description: Added scheduler preemption support for pods using `ReadWriteOncePod` PVCs
feature.author: chrishenzie
feature.userFacingChange: Adds scheduler preemption support for pods using `ReadWriteOncePod` PVCs

issueContext.title: Enforce ReadWriteOncePod PVC access mode during scheduling
issueContext.body:
See [KEP-2485](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-storage/2485-read-write-once-pod-pv-access-mode) for more context.

#### What would you like to be added:

The `ReadWriteOncePod` PVC access mode guarantees only a single pod can access the provided PVC as a volume. This is enforced during volume mount (in kubelet), and should be additionally enforced during scheduling.

#### Why is this needed:

Because without it the scheduler will assign pods to nodes and they will fail to start (due to failed volume attachment / mount).

#### Implementation details:

- The `NodeInfo` type will be extended to store a mapping of PVC names to the number of pods on the node consuming that PVC
- The `VolumeRestrictions` scheduler plugin is extended to have a lister for PVC and for `NodeInfo`
- During PreFilter, the plugin enumerates each `NodeInfo` checking the reference count for each PVC in the pod to be scheduled
- If the pod to be scheduled's PVC is using the `ReadWriteOncePod` access mode and that PVC is found with a reference count > 0, mark the pod `UnschedulableAndUnresolvable` (alpha)
  - For beta, we will mark the pod `Unschedulable` and implement preemption logic

enrichment.problem: The scheduler did not enforce the ReadWriteOncePod PVC access mode, allowing multiple pods to be scheduled on the same node with the same PVC. This caused pods that require exclusive volume access to fail at start‑up due to volume mount conflicts.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use the ReadWriteOncePod access mode and any other pods sharing the same node that might be preempted.
enrichment.fix: Extended the scheduler to track PVC reference counts per node and added preemption logic. When a pod with a ReadWriteOncePod PVC is being scheduled, the scheduler now marks the pod unschedulable if the PVC is already in use on a node, and can preempt other pods to honor the exclusive access guarantee.
enrichment.impact: Pods that require exclusive volume access are now correctly scheduled, preventing start‑up failures and reducing unnecessary pod restarts. Cluster operators get more reliable scheduling for stateful workloads using ReadWriteOncePod PVCs.

feature.description:
Scheduler no longer runs the plugin's `Filter` method when its `PreFilter` method returned a Skip status.
In other words, your `PreFilter`/`Filter` plugin can return a Skip status in `PreFilter` if the plugin does nothing in Filter for that Pod.
Scheduler skips `NodeAffinity` Filter plugin when `NodeAffinity` Filter plugin has nothing to do with a Pod.
It may affect some metrics values related to the `NodeAffinity` Filter plugin.
feature.author: sanposhiho
feature.userFacingChange:
Scheduler doesn't run plugin's Filter method when its PreFilter method returned a Skip status.
In other words, your PreFilter/Filter plugin can return a Skip status in PreFilter if the plugin does nothing in Filter for that Pod.
Scheduler skips NodeAffinity Filter plugin when NodeAffinity Filter plugin has nothing to do with a Pod.
It may affect some metrics values related to the NodeAffinity Filter plugin.

enrichment.problem: The scheduler always invoked a plugin's Filter method even when its PreFilter returned a Skip status, causing unnecessary work and skewing metrics for plugins such as NodeAffinity.
enrichment.affected: All workloads scheduled by kube‑scheduler that use plugins with a PreFilter/Filter pair, especially those using the NodeAffinity Filter plugin.
enrichment.fix: Scheduler now checks the result of PreFilter and skips the corresponding Filter call when the PreFilter returns Skip. NodeAffinity and any other PreFilter/Filter plugins that have nothing to do for a pod will no longer run their Filter phase.
enrichment.impact: Reduces CPU overhead in the scheduling cycle and makes Filter‑related metrics (e.g., execution counts for NodeAffinity) reflect actual work. No change to pod placement decisions.

feature.description: Profiling can now be served on a unix-domain socket by using the `--profiling-path` option (when profiling is enabled) for security purposes.
feature.author: apelisse

enrichment.problem: Profiling endpoints were only exposed over HTTP, which could be accessed over the network and increase attack surface.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes component that runs with the profiling server enabled (e.g., kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet). Users who rely on profiling over the network must switch to the Unix socket or keep the existing behavior.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the `--profiling-path` flag that allows the profiling server to be bound to a Unix domain socket instead of a TCP port when profiling is enabled.
enrichment.impact: Improves security by limiting profiling access to local processes, reducing the risk of remote exploitation while still enabling developers to collect profiling data.

feature.description: Dynamic Resource Allocation framework can be used for network devices
feature.author: bart0sh

issueContext.title: dynamic resource allocation: ensure PrepareResources called before CNI invoked
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Ensure that `PrepareResources()` is called against all DRA `kubelet` plugins for all containers before CNI is invoked.

This can be done by either moving this call earlier in the process of doing pod creation, or moving it into the `PodAdmission` loop (as is done by the existing device plugin framework).

Ideally, we would follow the pattern used by the existing device plugin. This would allow us to integrate seamlessly with the `TopologyManager`, for example, for DRA kubelet plugins that wished to do so.

However, there are unfortunate issues with this approach. The biggest one being that there is no retry loop for transient failures when calling out to external plugins. This means that if a transient failure does occur, the pod fails admission with an `UnexpectedAdmissionError` (even though it could have quickly recovered with a subsequent call out to the plugin, for example. Other resource managers, beyond DRA (especially the device plugin) could also benefit from improving the situation around transient failures, so this approach is worth exploring

The alternate approach, i.e. simply moving the `PrepareResources()` earlier in the process if pod creation is fairly straightforward, and a PR for doing so has already been created:
* https://github.com/pohly/kubernetes/pull/43

However, this doesn't allow us to integrate as nicely with the other resource managers, as moving it to the pod admission loop would.

We will need to consider what the right approach is as we start to work on this.

### Why is this needed?

This link summarizes the reasons behind needing this enhancement well:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111023#discussion_r1005306039

Quoted from that review comment:
> The PrepareResources is called after the CNI is invoked. This is a problem for network devices that want to use DRA framework.
>
> In our case we have complex netdevice with several of other devices that we want to map

enrichment.problem: Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) plugins were not invoked via PrepareResources() before the CNI plugin ran, causing pod admission failures (especially on transient plugin errors) and preventing seamless integration with the TopologyManager.
enrichment.affected: Pods using DRA network device plugins and the kubelet on nodes where those plugins run; any workloads that depend on dynamic network resource allocation.
enrichment.fix: The change moves the PrepareResources() call for all DRA kubelet plugins to run before CNI is invoked (integrated into the pod admission loop), aligning the behavior with the existing device plugin framework and adding handling for transient failures.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on DRA for network devices now admit reliably, can integrate with TopologyManager, and avoid unexpected admission errors caused by temporary plugin issues, improving overall cluster stability and network resource handling.

feature.description: Added new feature gate `ServiceNodePortStaticSubrange`, to enable the new strategy in the `NodePort` Service port allocators, so the node port range is subdivided and dynamic allocated `NodePort` port for Services are allocated preferentially from the upper range.
feature.author: xuzhenglun
feature.userFacingChange: New feature gate, ServiceNodePortStaticSubrange, to enable the new strategy in the NodePort Service port allocators, so the node port range is subdivided and dynamic allocated NodePort port for Services are allocated preferentially from the upper range.

issueContext.title: Reserved an statically port range for nodeport
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

just like [KEP-3070](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-network/3070-reserved-service-ip-range) did, I want to reserve some port for nodeport.  I can try to submit an KEP if it sound good for sig/network.

### Why is this needed?

In our cluster, some applications are NOT deployed in Kubernetes. But they need to connect to `service` in Kubernetes too.

For example, some applications need to connect to the `minio` service but they have no idea what cluster-ip it is. In our situation, those applications just connect to a specific port (30009) of the Kubernetes master node.

This situation works most time, but in something 30009 is allocated by something else. And minio service will be failed to applied.

enrichment.problem: Dynamic NodePort allocation could consume ports that external, non‑Kubernetes applications rely on, causing port conflicts and failures when those apps try to reach services via a known port.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that expose services via NodePort and have external applications depending on fixed ports; administrators who need to reserve specific NodePort numbers.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the ServiceNodePortStaticSubrange feature gate. When enabled, the NodePort range is split into a static lower sub‑range (reserved for manually assigned ports) and a dynamic upper sub‑range. Dynamic allocations are preferentially taken from the upper range, preserving the lower range for static usage.
enrichment.impact: Allows clusters to reserve a predictable set of NodePort numbers for external services, eliminating accidental port collisions and improving interoperability with legacy or non‑K8s workloads that need fixed ports.

feature.description: [E2E] Pods spawned by E2E tests can now pull images from the private registry using the new --e2e-docker-config-file flag
feature.author: Divya063

issueContext.title: [E2E] Support for pulling images from private registry
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Our team is using sonobuoy to run the conformance tests on a cluster. When running Sonobuoy E2E/Conformance tests, deployed pods will go into an ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff state when the image resides in a repository that requires authentication, and credentials are not passed with the request.

The [E2E/Conformance test](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/test/e2e) process spawns pods in separate namespaces to run E2E/Conformance tests. If pods are referencing images from a private registry, the secrets wouldn’t be available in the newly created namespaces and the pod will fail to start.

This is the issue reported by one of the sonobuoy users - https://github.com/vmware-tanzu/sonobuoy/issues/1038

Kubernetes E2E framework provides a `--e2e-docker-config-file`  flag which takes in a file containing the credentials that can be used to pull images from private registries needed for a test.  Using the credentials a secret can be created in the newly created namespace. 
With the Secret created, the default service account (in the new namespace) will be patched with the created secret and can then be referenced by the test pod, and repository authentication should be successful.


### Why is this needed?

As of now, when running the E2E tests, the flag is only being checked in a single test - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/57eb5d631ccd615cd161b6da36afc759af004b93/test/e2e/common/node/runtime.go#L292-L308
so despite passing the credential file, other tests would fail.

enrichment.problem: E2E test pods that run in newly created namespaces cannot pull images from private registries because the necessary image pull secrets are not present, leading to ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff failures.
enrichment.affected: Teams executing Kubernetes E2E or conformance tests that need to pull private images; test pods in temporary namespaces.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the `--e2e-docker-config-file` flag to the E2E test framework. The flag accepts a Docker config file with registry credentials, creates a corresponding secret in each test namespace, and patches the default service account to reference that secret, enabling pods to authenticate to private registries.
enrichment.impact: Allows users running E2E or conformance tests (e.g., via Sonobuoy) to use private container images, eliminating test failures and expanding CI capabilities for clusters that rely on private registries.

issueContext.title: scheduler: distinguish between Unschedulable and UnschedulableAndUnresolvable from PostFilter
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Right now, both status codes are treated the same:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cc704f97784c3359db4690b97201ebfe6b481869/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L769C26-L771

This could be changed so that Unschedulable only means "I couldn't do anything, but keep trying", which might make sense when there are two PostFilter plugins, like the new dynamic resource plugin and preemption.



### Why is this needed?

Better decision on how to proceed when a pod cannot be scheduled, but some action could make it schedulable.

enrichment.problem: When a scheduler plugin returned the UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status during the PostFilter phase, the scheduler continued the scheduling cycle, leading to unnecessary processing and potential repeated preemption attempts.
enrichment.affected: Pods that reach the PostFilter stage and encounter a plugin that determines they are unschedulable and unresolvable.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now terminates the scheduling cycle immediately for the pod as soon as any PostFilter plugin returns an UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status.
enrichment.impact: Reduces wasted scheduling cycles and improves scheduling latency, especially for workloads using PostFilter plugins such as dynamic resource or preemption plugins. It ensures the scheduler stops trying when a pod cannot be made schedulable, conserving cluster resources.

feature.description: The job controller back-off logic is now decoupled from workqueue. In case of parallelism > 1, if there are multiple new failures in a reconciliation cycle, all the failures are taken into account to compute the back-off. Previously, the back-off kicked in for all types of failures; with this change, only pod failures are taken into account. If the back-off limits exceeds, the job is marked as failed immediately; before this change, the job is marked as failed in the next back-off.
feature.author: sathyanarays

issueContext.title: Kubernetes Jobs API rapid-fire scheduling doesnt honor exponential backoff characteristics
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

# Problem

The job controller appears to "rapidly reschedule" several pods at the same time (without backing off) which ultimately appears almost like a batch or gang scheduling workflow.  

... This is the opposite of what the job docs say, bc they clearly state :
```
 The back-off limit is set by default to 6. Failed Pods associated with the Job are recreated by the Job controller with an exponential back-off delay (10s, 20s, 40s ...) capped at six minutes.
```
So, rather then, 

- 10, 20, 40, 80 wait times between trying things we are seeing
- 0, 3, 3, 3, 3 second wait times before pods are being retried

This is in the 1.25 release, but not sure if it also happens earlier.  You can see this in the latest kind version. 




### What did you expect to happen?

Jobs wouldnt schedule the same pod at rapid fire intervals

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

# Details 

Thanks to Ryan for this reproducer: 
```
apiVersion: batch/v1

kind: Job

metadata:

  name: backoff-exp

spec:

  backoffLimit: 100

  template:

    spec:

      containers:

        - name: die

          image: ubuntu

          command: [ "/bin/false" ]

          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent

      restartPolicy: Never

```

Now once this is running, you can graph the values like so: 

```
kubectl get pods -o wide | awk '

BEGIN {

    a["d"] = 24*(\

    a["h"] = 60*(\

    a["m"] = 60*(\

    a["s"] = 1)));

  }

  {

    print fx($5); # kubernetes time elapsed in seconds

  }

  function fx(ktym,    f,u,n,t,i) {

    n = split(ktym, f, /[dhms]/, u)

    t = 0

    for (i=1; i<n; i++) {

      t += f[i] * a[u[i]]

    }

    return t

  }

'|sort
```

And youl see a table like this, where the integers below are the AGE OF PODS in SECONDS.  We can see that the pod ages are 3 seconds apart as opposed to (10, 20, 40, 80 ...) or some other exponentialll

enrichment.problem: When a Job has parallelism > 1, the job controller treated all failure types (including non‑pod failures) as back‑off triggers. Multiple failures in a single reconciliation cycle bypassed the exponential back‑off, causing rapid‑fire pod recreation and delaying the job from being marked failed until the next back‑off.
enrichment.affected: Users running batch Jobs with parallelism >1 that experience multiple pod failures in a reconciliation loop. The issue manifested as rapid pod rescheduling and delayed job failure.
enrichment.fix: The back‑off logic was decoupled from the generic workqueue. Only pod failures are now considered for exponential back‑off, and the job is marked as failed immediately once the backoffLimit is exceeded.
enrichment.impact: Jobs now respect the documented exponential back‑off semantics, preventing resource spikes and unexpected rapid pod creation. Users relying on backoffLimit for failure handling get deterministic behavior and faster job termination when limits are hit.

feature.userFacingChange:
New "plugin_evaluation_total" is added to the scheduler. 
This metric counts how many times the specific plugin affects the scheduling result. The metric doesn't get incremented when the plugin has nothing to do with an incoming Pod.

enrichment.problem: There was no observable metric to indicate how often individual scheduler plugins actually influence scheduling decisions, making it difficult to monitor, debug, or optimize plugin behavior.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using kube‑scheduler, especially those that deploy custom or built‑in scheduler plugins and rely on metrics for observability.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new Prometheus metric `plugin_evaluation_total` in kube‑scheduler. The counter is incremented each time a specific plugin contributes to the scheduling result and remains unchanged when the plugin is not involved with the incoming pod.
enrichment.impact: Operators and developers can now track plugin impact directly via metrics, enabling better observability, troubleshooting, and performance tuning of scheduling plugins. It also aids in capacity planning and detecting misbehaving plugins.

feature.description: Added `kubelet` Topology Manager metrics to track admission requests processed and occured admission errors.
feature.author: swatisehgal
feature.userFacingChange: Add kubelet Topology Manager metrics to track admission requests processed by it and occured admission errors.

enrichment.problem: Kubelet’s Topology Manager did not expose metrics for how many admission requests it processes or how many admission errors occur, making it difficult for operators to observe and troubleshoot topology-aware scheduling.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the kubelet Topology Manager for pod placement; especially those relying on NUMA‑aware scheduling and needing observability of admission failures.
enrichment.fix: Introduces new kubelet Topology Manager metrics that count admission requests processed and admission errors, exposing them via the kubelet’s /metrics endpoint.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now monitor, alert on, and debug Topology Manager behavior, leading to faster identification of placement issues and improved reliability of NUMA‑aware workloads.

feature.description:
A new feature was enabled to improve the performance of the iptables mode of `kube-proxy` in large clusters. No action was required, however:

1. If you experienced problems with Services not syncing to iptables correctly, you can disable the feature by passing `--feature-gates=MinimizeIPTablesRestore=false` to kube-proxy (and file a bug if this fixes it). (This might also be detected by seeing the value of kube-proxy's `sync_proxy_rules_iptables_partial_restore_failures_total` metric rising.)
2. If you were previously overriding the kube-proxy configuration for performance reasons, this may no longer be necessary. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/networking/virtual-ips/#optimizing-iptables-mode-performance.
feature.author: danwinship
feature.userFacingChange:
A new feature has been enabled to improve the performance of the iptables mode of kube-proxy in large clusters. You do not need to take any action, however:

1. If you experience problems with Services not syncing to iptables correctly, you can disable the feature by passing `--feature-gates=MinimizeIPTablesRestore=false` to kube-proxy (and file a bug if this fixes it). (This might also be detected by seeing the value of kube-proxy's `sync_proxy_rules_iptables_partial_restore_failures_total` metric rising.)
2. If you were previously overriding the kube-proxy configuration for performance reasons, this may no longer be necessary. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/networking/virtual-ips/#optimizing-iptables-mode-performance.

enrichment.problem: In large clusters, the new MinimizeIPTablesRestore feature can cause kube-proxy iptables mode to fail to sync Service rules correctly, leading to partial restore failures.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using kube-proxy in iptables mode, especially large ones or those that have manually overridden kube-proxy performance settings.
enrichment.fix: A performance‑focused feature (MinimizeIPTablesRestore) is enabled by default to speed up iptables restores. If the issue appears, users can disable it with the feature gate `--feature-gates=MinimizeIPTablesRestore=false` and report a bug. Existing custom kube-proxy performance tweaks may no longer be needed.
enrichment.impact: Improves iptables restore throughput for kube-proxy, reducing CPU and latency in large clusters, while providing a reversible option for clusters experiencing sync errors.

feature.description:
`kube-proxy` now accepts the `ContextualLogging`, `LoggingAlphaOptions`,
`LoggingBetaOptions`
feature.author: pohly
feature.userFacingChange: kube-proxy accepts the ContextualLogging, LoggingAlphaOptions, LoggingBetaOptions feature gates.

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy could not be started with the ContextualLogging, LoggingAlphaOptions, or LoggingBetaOptions feature gates, preventing users from enabling those logging capabilities for proxy operations.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using kube-proxy that wish to enable contextual or advanced logging options were unable to do so; now they can.
enrichment.fix: kube-proxy now recognizes and accepts the ContextualLogging, LoggingAlphaOptions, and LoggingBetaOptions feature gates, allowing the corresponding logging features to be enabled at runtime.
enrichment.impact: Enables richer, contextual logging for kube-proxy, improving observability and debugging of network traffic handling. Users can now opt‑in to alpha and beta logging options without errors.

feature.description: API validation relaxed allowing Indexed Jobs to be scaled up/down by changing parallelism and completions in tandem, such that parallelism == completions.
feature.author: danielvegamyhre

enrichment.problem: Indexed Jobs could not be scaled up or down because API validation rejected changes to .spec.parallelism and .spec.completions when they were modified together, even when they were equal.
enrichment.affected: Owners of Indexed Jobs (Jobs with completionMode=Indexed) who need to change parallelism/completions for scaling.
enrichment.fix: The API validation logic was relaxed to allow updating both parallelism and completions simultaneously for Indexed Jobs, as long as parallelism equals completions. This permits scaling indexed jobs by adjusting these fields together.
enrichment.impact: Users can now dynamically scale indexed jobs without deleting and recreating them, simplifying workload management and testing scenarios that rely on indexed job scaling.

feature.description: Added `NewVolumeManagerReconstruction` feature gate and enabled it by default to enable updated discovery of mounted volumes during kubelet startup. Please watch for kubelet getting stuck at startup and / or not unmounting volumes from deleted Pods and report any issues in this area.
feature.author: jsafrane
feature.userFacingChange: Added NewVolumeManagerReconstruction feature gate and enable it by default to enable updated discovery of mounted volumes during kubelet startup. Please watch for kubelet getting stuck at startup and / or not unmounting volumes from deleted Pods and report any issues in this area.

enrichment.problem: The kubelet’s previous volume manager reconstruction did not reliably discover all mounted volumes during startup, leading to possible leftover mounts and situations where the kubelet could get stuck or fail to unmount volumes from deleted Pods.
enrichment.affected: All nodes running the kubelet, especially those with Pods that use persistent volumes (CSI, in‑tree drivers, etc.).
enrichment.fix: Introduced the NewVolumeManagerReconstruction feature gate, enabled by default, which adds updated discovery of mounted volumes during kubelet startup, ensuring proper reconstruction of the volume manager state.
enrichment.impact: Improves kubelet reliability and volume cleanup on node startup, reducing the risk of orphaned mounts and startup hangs for workloads that use volumes. Users should monitor for any regressions where the kubelet might still get stuck or fail to unmount volumes.

feature.description: Performance improvements in `klog`
feature.author: pohly
feature.userFacingChange: performance improvements in klog

enrichment.problem: klog logging library incurred non‑trivial overhead, especially when verbose logging was enabled, leading to slower execution of components that emit many log statements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components that use the klog library (e.g., kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, and other core components) benefit from the reduced logging overhead.
enrichment.fix: Optimized the klog implementation to reduce CPU work and memory allocations during log formatting and output, improving overall runtime performance.
enrichment.impact: Reduces latency and CPU usage across the Kubernetes control plane and node components, leading to smoother operation for clusters of any size, particularly under heavy logging or debug scenarios.

feature.description:
Give terminal phase correctly to all pods that will not be restarted. 

In particular, assign Failed phase to pods which are deleted while pending. Also, assign a terminal 
phase (Succeeded or Failed, depending on the exit statuses of the pod containers) to pods which
are deleted while running.

This fixes the issue for jobs using pod failure policy (with JobPodFailurePolicy and PodDisruptionConditions 
feature gates enabled) that their pods could get stuck in the pending phase when deleted.

Users who maintain controllers which relied on the fact that pods with RestartPolicy=Always
never enter the Succeeded phase may need to adapt their controllers. This is because as a consequence of 
the change pods which use RestartPolicy=Always may end up in the Succeeded phase in two scenarios: pod 
deletion and graceful node shutdown.
feature.author: mimowo
feature.userFacingChange:
Give terminal phase correctly to all pods that will not be restarted. 

In particular, assign Failed phase to pods which are deleted while pending. Also, assign a terminal 
phase (Succeeded or Failed, depending on the exit statuses of the pod containers) to pods which
are deleted while running.

This fixes the issue for jobs using pod failure policy (with JobPodFailurePolicy and PodDisruptionConditions 
feature gates enabled) that their pods could get stuck in the pending phase when deleted.

ACTION REQUIRED: Users who maintain controllers which relied on the fact that pods with RestartPolicy=Always
never enter the Succeeded phase may need to adapt their controllers. This is because as a consequence of 
the change pods which use RestartPolicy=Always may end up in the Succeeded phase in two scenarios: pod 
deletion and graceful node shutdown.

enrichment.problem: Pods could remain in the Pending phase after being deleted, especially for Jobs using the PodFailurePolicy with the JobPodFailurePolicy and PodDisruptionConditions feature gates enabled. Additionally, pods with RestartPolicy=Always could incorrectly transition to the Succeeded phase on deletion or graceful node shutdown, breaking assumptions of some controllers.
enrichment.affected: Jobs using PodFailurePolicy and any controllers that depended on RestartPolicy=Always pods never becoming Succeeded; also any workloads that could see pods stuck in Pending after deletion.
enrichment.fix: When a pod is deleted and will not be restarted, the system now assigns a proper terminal phase: Failed for pods deleted while pending, and either Succeeded or Failed (based on container exit codes) for pods deleted while running. This ensures pods reach a terminal state correctly.
enrichment.impact: Jobs that rely on pod failure handling will no longer get stuck in Pending, improving reliability of job completion. Controllers that assumed RestartPolicy=Always pods never reach Succeeded may need to be updated, preventing logic errors.

feature.description: kubelet allows pods to use the `net.ipv4.ip_local_reserved_ports` sysctl by default and the minimal kernel version is 3.16; Pod Security admission allows this sysctl in v1.27+ versions of the baseline and restricted policies.
feature.author: pacoxu

issueContext.title: Mark net.ipv4.ip_local_reserved_ports as a safe sysctl
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

The `net.ipv4.ip_local_reserved_ports` sysctl is namespaced so should be safe to permit. It is an often necessary counterpart to `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` sysctl which is currently in the default safe list. It would therefore be helpful to include it in the default safe list as well.

### Why is this needed?

If you have a pod with multiple containers which both sets the `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` to a large range such as the commonly used '1025 65535' in order to maximise the number of available ports *and* binds to local ports in that range then it is possible for a container doing a bind to deadlock repeatedly failing to start if the another container has already used the local port as an ephemeral port. If the ports needed by the bind can be added to the reserved ports list then this issue can be avoided without having to unnecessarily shrink the local port range or add coupling to ensure containers start in the correct order to prevent the deadlock.

enrichment.problem: Pods could not use the net.ipv4.ip_local_reserved_ports sysctl, leading to port allocation deadlocks when multiple containers set a wide net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range and bind to specific local ports. The sysctl was not in the safe list, causing failures or requiring work‑arounds such as shrinking the port range.
enrichment.affected: Pods that need to reserve specific ports, especially multi‑container pods that set a large port range. Cluster administrators using baseline or restricted PSA policies before v1.27 were unable to use this sysctl.
enrichment.fix: kubelet now permits the net.ipv4.ip_local_reserved_ports sysctl by default (kernel >= 3.16). The Pod Security Admission baseline and restricted policies also allow this sysctl starting with v1.27, making it a supported, safe configuration for pods.
enrichment.impact: Users can safely reserve specific ports for pod containers without risking binding deadlocks or having to reduce the port range. This simplifies network configuration and improves reliability for multi‑container pods that need reserved ports.

feature.description: The go version defined in `.go-version` is now fetched when invoking test, build, and code generation targets if the current go version does not match it. Set $FORCE_HOST_GO=y while testing or building to skip this behavior, or set $GO_VERSION to override the selected go version.
feature.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: When the host Go version differed from the version specified in the repository’s .go-version file, test, build, and code generation make targets used the host Go, leading to inconsistent builds or failures.
enrichment.affected: Developers invoking make test, make build, or code generation targets in the Kubernetes source tree with a Go version mismatch.
enrichment.fix: The make targets now automatically fetch and use the Go version defined in .go-version if the current Go version does not match. Users can skip this behavior with FORCE_HOST_GO=y or override the selected version via GO_VERSION.
enrichment.impact: Developers no longer need to manually ensure the correct Go version when running tests, building binaries, or generating code, reducing build errors and improving reproducibility. Overrides remain possible for custom workflows.

feature.description: The mount-utils mounter now provides an option to limit the number of concurrent format operations.
feature.author: artemvmin

enrichment.problem: Kubelet’s mount-utils mounter had no mechanism to restrict how many volume format operations could run at the same time, leading to potential resource contention when many volumes are provisioned concurrently.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that perform many volume format operations (e.g., during bulk provisioning, CSI drivers, or node initialization) may see smoother node performance.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new option in mount-utils that lets callers limit the number of concurrent format calls, allowing operators to throttle formatting and avoid overload.
enrichment.impact: Improves stability of large‑scale provisioning and reduces spikes in CPU/disk I/O on nodes, especially in clusters that create many volumes at once.

feature.description: apiserver_storage_transformation_operations_total metric has been updated to include labels transformer_prefix and status.
feature.author: ritazh

issueContext.title: [kmsv2] Add metrics
issueContext.body:
Beta: 

- [ ] - Envelop encrypt/decrypt latency - `apiserver_storage_transformation_duration_seconds`, Histogram, Labels: transformation_type This already exists, need to add transformer_prefix="k8s:enc:kms:v2:" and document it
- [ ]  - Envelop encrypt/decrypt total - `apiserver_storage_transformation_operations_total`, counter, Labels: transformer_prefix="k8s:enc:kms:v2:", transformation_type, status. This already exists, need to add test and document it.
- [ ] - `key_id` used - `apiserver_envelope_encryption_keyid_total`, counter, Labels: transformation_type, key_id

After beta:
- reload of encryptionConfig - `apiserver_server_encryptionconfig_reload_total`, counter, Labels: status

enrichment.problem: The apiserver_storage_transformation_operations_total metric did not expose the transformer_prefix and status labels, limiting users' ability to differentiate KMS v2 envelope encryption operations and their outcomes.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using KMS v2 envelope encryption rely on this metric for monitoring; lack of labels previously made it difficult to filter and aggregate operation counts by transformer or status.
enrichment.fix: The metric is updated to include the new transformer_prefix and status labels, enabling granular counting of encryption/decryption operations per transformer and status.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now monitor and troubleshoot KMS v2 envelope encryption more precisely, improving observability of security-related API server activity and aiding performance analysis.

feature.description: Added e2e test to node expand volume with secret
feature.author: zhucan
feature.userFacingChange: add e2e test to node expand volume with secret

enrichment.problem: There was no end‑to‑end test covering the scenario where a node expands a volume using a secret, leaving that functionality unverified.
enrichment.affected: Storage developers, CSI driver maintainers, and users who rely on volume expansion that uses secrets.
enrichment.fix: Added an e2e test that exercises node volume expansion when the operation requires a secret, ensuring the code path is exercised in CI.
enrichment.impact: Improves test coverage for CSI volume expansion with secret credentials, helping catch regressions early and increasing confidence for users of secret‑based volume expansion.

feature.description: Added `--output plaintext-openapiv2` argument to kubectl explain to use old openapiv2 `explain` implementation.
feature.author: alexzielenski
feature.userFacingChange: Adds --output plaintext-openapiv2 argument to kubectl explain to use old openapiv2 `explain` implementation.

enrichment.problem: kubectl explain only used the new openapiv3 implementation, removing the previous openapiv2 behavior that some users relied on.
enrichment.affected: Any user or automation that runs `kubectl explain` and expects the old openapiv2 output format.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new output flag `--output plaintext-openapiv2` that forces kubectl explain to use the original openapiv2 explain implementation.
enrichment.impact: Restores compatibility for scripts and users that depend on the legacy openapiv2 output format, preventing breakage after the default switch to openapiv3.

feature.description: Added kubelet Topology Manager metric to measure topology manager admission latency.
feature.author: swatisehgal
feature.userFacingChange: Add kubelet Topology Manager metric to measure topology manager admission latency.

enrichment.problem: Kubelet’s Topology Manager had no observable metric for admission latency, making it difficult for operators to detect performance regressions or diagnose pod placement delays.
enrichment.affected: Cluster operators and any workloads relying on the Topology Manager for NUMA‑aware pod placement could not previously measure admission latency.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new kubelet Topology Manager metric that records the admission latency for each pod, exposing the data via the kubelet’s metrics endpoint.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now monitor and alert on Topology Manager latency, helping to identify bottlenecks, improve troubleshooting, and ensure NUMA‑aware pod placement performs as expected.

feature.description: Pods which have an invalid negative `spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds` value will now be treated as having a `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` of `1`
feature.author: wzshiming
feature.userFacingChange: Pods which have an invalid negative `spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds` value will be treated as having terminationGracePeriodSeconds of 1

enrichment.problem: Pods that were created with a negative spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds value were considered invalid, leading to unexpected behavior or failures when terminating the pod.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that specifies a negative terminationGracePeriodSeconds value; clusters where such pods are created.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now treats any pod with a negative terminationGracePeriodSeconds as if it had a terminationGracePeriodSeconds of 1 second, allowing the pod to terminate gracefully.
enrichment.impact: Prevents pod termination failures for workloads that inadvertently specify a negative grace period, improving cluster stability and reducing the need for manual remediation.

feature.description: `kubeadm`: now shows a warning message when detecting that the sandbox image of the container runtime is inconsistent with that used by kubeadm
feature.author: SataQiu
feature.userFacingChange: kubeadm: show a warning message when detecting that the sandbox image of the container runtime is inconsistent with that used by kubeadm

enrichment.problem: When the container runtime’s default sandbox image differs from the image that kubeadm expects, kubeadm previously did not alert the user, leading to potential pod creation failures or hard‑to‑debug runtime errors.
enrichment.affected: Users running kubeadm to bootstrap clusters with a container runtime (e.g., containerd, Docker) whose default sandbox image differs from kubeadm’s expected image.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now detects a mismatch between the runtime’s sandbox image and the one configured for kubeadm and prints a warning message during cluster initialization or node join.
enrichment.impact: Operators are warned early about an image inconsistency, allowing them to correct the runtime configuration before workloads are affected, improving cluster reliability and troubleshooting.

feature.description: Graduated the `CSINodeExpandSecret` feature to Beta. This feature facilitates passing secrets to CSI driver as part of Node Expansion CSI operation.
feature.author: humblec
feature.userFacingChange: Graduates the CSINodeExpandSecret feature to Beta. This feature facilitates passing secrets to CSI driver as part of Node Expansion CSI operation.

enrichment.problem: CSI drivers that require credentials could not receive secrets during the Node Expansion CSI operation, limiting the ability to use secure storage drivers that need authentication for volume expansion.
enrichment.affected: Users of CSI drivers that need secrets for node expansion, and administrators managing storage that relies on such drivers.
enrichment.fix: Graduates the CSINodeExpandSecret feature to Beta, enabling the API and node expansion workflow to pass secret objects to CSI drivers as part of the NodeExpand RPC.
enrichment.impact: Cluster admins and storage teams can now use CSI drivers that need secrets for node‑level volume expansion without custom workarounds, improving reliability and security of storage operations.

feature.description: Changed metrics for aggregated discovery to publish new time series (alpha).
feature.author: Jefftree

enrichment.problem: The aggregated discovery endpoint did not expose dedicated Prometheus metrics, making it hard for operators to monitor discovery latency and request patterns.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running the API server with aggregated discovery enabled; operators looking to monitor discovery activity.
enrichment.fix: Introduced new alpha metrics for aggregated discovery, publishing additional time series that capture request counts, latencies, and error rates.
enrichment.impact: Provides better observability for API servers using aggregated discovery, enabling alerting and performance analysis of discovery traffic.

feature.description: Added apiserver_envelope_encryption_kms_operations_latency_seconds metric to measure the KMSv2 grpc calls latency.
feature.author: aramase

enrichment.problem: There was no built‑in metric to observe the latency of KMS v2 gRPC calls used for envelope encryption, making it hard for operators to monitor performance or troubleshoot slow encryption operations.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using KMS v2 envelope encryption for secret encryption; API server performance monitoring and troubleshooting are directly impacted.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the apiserver_envelope_encryption_kms_operations_latency_seconds metric, which records the latency of each KMS v2 gRPC request performed by the API server during envelope‑encryption operations.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now monitor, alert on, and troubleshoot KMS v2 latency issues, improving the reliability and observability of envelope‑encryption workflows.

feature.description: The Scheduler did not run the plugin Score method when its PreScore method returned a Skip status. In other words, the PreScore/Score plugin could return a Skip status in PreScore if the plugin did nothing in Score for that Pod.
feature.author: AxeZhan
feature.userFacingChange: Scheduler doesn't run plugin's Score method when its PreScore method returned a Skip status. In other words, your PreScore/Score plugin can return a Skip status in PreScore if the plugin does nothing in Score for that Pod.

issueContext.title: Allow PreScore to return `Skip` status to skip running the corresponding Score extension
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

In some scheduler plugins, PreScore is implemented to pre-process state before running Score for each node. In some cases, PreScore can decide that Score shouldn't run at all (e.g., no relevant PodTopologySpread constraints), and so it will be useful to have an explicit way to communicate that.

### Why is this needed?

To potentially improve performance (likely negligible), but this also offer a better API (vs having each plugin communicate a special value internally)

/sig scheduling

enrichment.problem: Scheduler always executed a plugin's Score method even when the plugin's PreScore returned a Skip status, causing unnecessary processing.
enrichment.affected: Scheduler plugins that implement PreScore/Score. Clusters using custom plugins may see reduced scheduling latency.
enrichment.fix: Scheduler now respects a Skip status returned from a plugin's PreScore method and skips invoking the corresponding Score method for that pod.
enrichment.impact: Improves scheduling performance and provides a cleaner API for plugin developers, allowing them to efficiently skip scoring when it is not needed.

feature.description: Added "netadmin" debugging profiles for kubectl debug.
feature.author: wedaly

enrichment.problem: kubectl debug did not include a predefined debugging profile for network administration tasks, requiring users to manually configure containers for packet tracing, firewall manipulation, etc.
enrichment.affected: Users of kubectl debug who need to perform network‑admin level troubleshooting (cluster operators, developers, SREs).
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new "netadmin" debugging profile that can be specified with kubectl debug, automatically provisioning a pod with the appropriate capabilities and tools for network administration debugging.
enrichment.impact: Makes network‑related troubleshooting faster and less error‑prone by providing a ready‑to‑use profile, reducing the need for custom pod specifications and helping cluster admins and developers debug networking issues more efficiently.
