issueContext.title: Switch image in gRPC probe tests to agnhost
issueContext.body:
- Tests in `test/e2e/common/node/container_probe.go` are using `etcd` image for gRPC probe tests:
  - should not be restarted with a GRPC liveness probe
  - should be restarted with a GRPC liveness probe

We should use `agnhost` image for these tests as it is much smaller size.

/sig node
/kind cleanup
/priority important-soon
/area tests
/help-wanted
/good-first-issue

KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2727

enrichment.problem: The e2e node tests for gRPC probes used the large etcd image, causing unnecessarily large test image size and longer download/execution times.
enrichment.affected: Developers and CI systems running the node e2e test suite were affected by slower test runs due to the large etcd image.
enrichment.fix: Updated the tests in `test/e2e/common/node/container_probe.go` to use the lightweight `agnhost` image instead of `etcd` for gRPC probe scenarios.
enrichment.impact: Reduces the size of test images, speeds up test setup and execution, and lowers resource consumption for developers and CI pipelines running these node e2e tests.

feature.description: The Pod API field `.spec.schedulingGates[*].name` now requires qualified names (like `example.com/mygate`), matching validation for names of `.spec.readinessGates[*].name`. Any uses of the alpha scheduling gate feature prior to 1.27 that do not match that validation must be renamed or deleted before upgrading to 1.27.
feature.author: lianghao208

enrichment.problem: Prior to v1.27 the `.spec.schedulingGates[*].name` field accepted any string, including unqualified names. Starting in v1.27 the field requires a fully qualified name (e.g., `example.com/mygate`), matching the validation used for readiness gates. Pods that use the alpha scheduling gate feature with non‑qualified names will be rejected by the API server on upgrade.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that use the alpha scheduling gates feature with non‑qualified gate names. Cluster administrators performing an upgrade to v1.27 are directly impacted.
enrichment.fix: The API server now validates `schedulingGates` names and rejects unqualified values. Users must rename existing scheduling gates to qualified names or remove the gates before upgrading to v1.27.
enrichment.impact: Upgrading a cluster to v1.27 will fail pod creation or update for any workloads that define scheduling gates with unqualified names. Administrators need to audit and adjust manifests, preventing unexpected deployment failures after upgrade.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.20.1
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were being built with an older Go version, which could lack recent security fixes, language improvements, and support for newer platforms.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components and users building or running Kubernetes binaries are affected, as the new Go version changes the build artifacts across the project.
enrichment.fix: The build system was updated to compile all Kubernetes components with Go 1.20.1.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes binaries (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) benefit from the latest Go compiler improvements, security patches, and compatibility with newer toolchains.

feature.description: Added apiserver_envelope_encryption_invalid_key_id_from_status_total to measure number of times an invalid keyID is returned by the Status RPC call.
feature.author: ritazh

issueContext.title: [kmsv2] metrics to capture when plugin returns invalid keyID
issueContext.body:
it's hard to imagine life being better for a cluster admin if we make the cluster start failing reads ... I wouldn't do that.

failing no-op writes doesn't seem useful to me either... it pushes errors to users unlikely to be able to do anything about them

I think I would expect to coast, and for an error here to increment a metric to make it clear something is not working as expected (either transiently or persistently)

_Originally posted by @liggitt in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114544#discussion_r1080592400_

enrichment.problem: There was no metric to indicate when the KMS v2 encryption provider returned an invalid key ID via the Status RPC, making it difficult for administrators to detect and troubleshoot misbehaving encryption plugins.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using API server envelope encryption with KMS v2 providers that may return invalid key IDs.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the `apiserver_envelope_encryption_invalid_key_id_from_status_total` counter metric, which increments each time the Status RPC returns an invalid key ID, providing visibility into such errors.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators can now monitor this metric to quickly identify and address issues with KMS plugins, improving observability and reducing silent encryption failures.

feature.description: When an unsupported PodDisruptionBudget configuration is found, an event and log will be emitted to inform users of the misconfiguration.
feature.author: JayKayy

enrichment.problem: When a PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) is configured with unsupported fields, the system did not provide any clear indication, making it hard for users to detect the misconfiguration.
enrichment.affected: Users who configure PodDisruptionBudgets with unsupported options; workloads that rely on PDBs (e.g., Deployments, StatefulSets).
enrichment.fix: The controller now detects unsupported PDB configurations and generates a warning event as well as a log entry, alerting users to the problem.
enrichment.impact: Operators can quickly identify and correct invalid PDB settings, preventing unexpected disruption behavior and reducing troubleshooting time.

feature.description: Pod template `schedulingGates` are now mutable for Jobs that are suspended and have never been started
feature.author: ahg-g

enrichment.problem: Previously, the `schedulingGates` field in a Job's pod template was immutable, so users could not modify scheduling directives for Jobs that were suspended and had never started, forcing deletion and recreation of the Job to change them.
enrichment.affected: Jobs that are suspended and have not yet started any Pods. Users who need to adjust scheduling gates on such Jobs.
enrichment.fix: The change makes the `schedulingGates` field mutable when the Job is in a suspended state and has not yet started any Pods, allowing in‑place updates of scheduling directives.
enrichment.impact: Administrators can adjust scheduling constraints (e.g., add or remove scheduling gates) for pending Jobs without recreating them, improving operational flexibility and reducing downtime for workloads that need scheduling tweaks before launch.

feature.description: Added metrics for volume reconstruction during kubelet startup.
feature.author: jsafrane

enrichment.problem: Operators had no dedicated metrics to monitor the volume reconstruction process that occurs during kubelet startup, making it difficult to detect delays or failures in restoring volumes on node restart.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and storage operators who need to monitor node startup and volume reconstruction performance.
enrichment.fix: Introduced new Prometheus metrics emitted by the kubelet that track volume reconstruction progress and timing during node startup.
enrichment.impact: Provides observability into volume reconstruction, enabling alerting and troubleshooting of node startup issues related to storage, which improves cluster reliability and reduces mean-time-to-resolution for storage‑related problems.

feature.description: Graduated CRI Events driven Pod LifeCycle Event Generator (Evented PLEG) to Beta
feature.author: harche
feature.userFacingChange: Graduate CRI Events driven Pod LifeCycle Event Generator (Evented PLEG) to Beta

enrichment.problem: Kubelet relied on a polling‑based Pod Lifecycle Event Generator (PLEG), which incurred higher CPU usage and added latency to pod start/stop detection. The event‑driven (CRI events) PLEG was only in Alpha, so it was not considered stable for production use.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet nodes that run a CRI implementation supporting events. Users who want lower CPU overhead and quicker pod state updates are directly impacted.
enrichment.fix: Graduated the CRI‑events‑driven Evented PLEG to Beta. The feature gate can now be enabled in production clusters, providing a stable, event‑driven implementation of the PLEG.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can enable the Evented PLEG to reduce kubelet CPU load and get faster, more reliable pod lifecycle event handling, improving scalability and overall node performance.

feature.description: HPA controller starts to expose metrics from the kube-controller-manager.\n- `reconciliations_total`: Number of reconciliation of HPA controller. \n- `reconciliation_duration_seconds`: The time(seconds) that the HPA controller takes to reconcile once.
feature.author: sanposhiho
feature.userFacingChange:
HPA controller starts to expose metrics from the kube-controller-manager.
- `reconciliations_total`: Number of reconciliation of HPA controller. 
- `reconciliation_duration_seconds`: The time(seconds) that the HPA controller takes to reconcile once.

enrichment.problem: The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) controller did not expose any internal metrics, making it difficult for operators to monitor its reconciliation activity and performance.
enrichment.affected: Users running the HPA controller and monitoring/alerting systems that rely on metrics from kube-controller-manager.
enrichment.fix: The HPA controller now registers two new Prometheus metrics in kube-controller-manager: `reconciliations_total` (counts each reconciliation loop) and `reconciliation_duration_seconds` (measures the duration of each reconciliation).
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators can now observe how often the HPA controller reconciles and how long each cycle takes, enabling better debugging, capacity planning, and alerting for autoscaling behavior.

feature.description: Promote aggregated discovery endpoint to beta and it will be enabled by default
feature.author: Jefftree

enrichment.problem: The aggregated discovery endpoint was only available as an alpha feature and required a feature gate, limiting its use and visibility for clients that need to discover aggregated APIs.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes users and operators who rely on API discovery, especially those using aggregated API servers and clients such as kubectl or custom controllers.
enrichment.fix: Promoted the aggregated discovery endpoint to beta and enabled it by default, removing the need for a feature gate and making the endpoint generally available.
enrichment.impact: Clients and controllers can now reliably discover aggregated APIs without extra configuration, improving usability and encouraging broader adoption of aggregated API servers.

feature.description: The `JobMutableNodeSchedulingDirectives` feature gate has graduated to GA.
feature.author: ahg-g

issueContext.title: Make scheduling directives mutable for Jobs
issueContext.body:
#### What would you like to be added:

Make node affinity and tolerations mutable for Jobs. 

#### Why is this needed:

In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/97170 we added a new flag to allow suspending jobs to control when the Pods of a Job get created by controller-manager. We proposed this as a primitive that higher-level controllers can use to support job queuing,

Allowing to mutate node affinity and tolerations allows a higher-level queue controller to influence job placement by injecting node affinity or tolerations before un-suspending a job.

The implementation is basically relaxing the validation on job updates to allow for mutating the node affinity and tolerations of the pod template for jobs.

/sig scheduling
/sig apps
/kind feature

enrichment.problem: Job pod templates had immutable node affinity and tolerations, preventing updates to scheduling directives after a Job was created. This limited use cases such as queue controllers that need to modify placement constraints before unsuspending a Job.
enrichment.affected: Batch Jobs (and any controllers that manage Jobs) that need to modify node affinity or tolerations after creation.
enrichment.fix: Graduated the JobMutableNodeSchedulingDirectives feature to GA. The API validation for Job updates now permits changes to node affinity and tolerations in the pod template, and the feature gate is always enabled.
enrichment.impact: Higher‑level controllers can now adjust a Job's node affinity or tolerations on‑the‑fly, enabling dynamic job placement, better resource utilization, and support for job queuing patterns without recreating Jobs.

feature.description: The scheduler's metric `plugin_execution_duration_seconds` now records `PreEnqueue` plugins execution seconds.
feature.author: sanposhiho
feature.userFacingChange: The scheduler's metric "plugin_execution_duration_seconds" now records PreEnqueue plugins execution seconds.

issueContext.title: `plugin_execution_duration_seconds` in PreEnqueue
issueContext.body:
/kind feature
/sig scheduling

We don't support [`plugin_execution_duration_seconds`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/eabb70833a5649e10ab81f04423ce5cb16aba1b7/pkg/scheduler/metrics/metrics.go#L146) in PreEnqueue. It's worth implementing in PreEnqueue as well because the performance of PreEnqueue is critical for the whole scheduler's throughput.

/assign

enrichment.problem: The scheduler's `plugin_execution_duration_seconds` metric did not record execution time for PreEnqueue plugins, leaving a blind spot in performance monitoring of the critical PreEnqueue phase.
enrichment.affected: Users of scheduler observability (e.g., cluster operators, SREs) who rely on `plugin_execution_duration_seconds` to analyze scheduling latency.
enrichment.fix: The metric implementation was updated to include timing data for PreEnqueue plugins, so their execution seconds are now emitted alongside other plugin phases.
enrichment.impact: Operators and developers can now observe and troubleshoot the latency of PreEnqueue plugins via Prometheus, enabling better performance tuning and capacity planning for the scheduler.

feature.description: Since Kubernetes v1.5, `kubectl apply` has had an alpha-stage `--prune` flag to support deleting previously applied objects that have been removed from the input manifest. This feature has remained in alpha ever since due to performance and correctness issues inherent in its design. This PR exposes a second, independent pruning alpha powered by a new standard named `ApplySets`. An `ApplySet` is a server-side object (by default, a Secret; ConfigMaps are also allowed) that kubectl can use to accurately and efficiently track set membership across `apply` operations. The format used for `ApplySet` is set out in  [KEP 3659](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3659) as a low-level specification.  Other tools in the ecosystem can also build on this specification for improved interoperability.  To try the ApplySet-based pruning alpha, set `KUBECTL_APPLYSET=true` and use the flags `--prune --applyset=secret-name` with `kubectl apply`.
feature.author: justinsb
feature.userFacingChange: Since Kubernetes v1.5, `kubectl apply` has had an alpha-stage `--prune` flag to support deleting previously applied objects that have been removed from the input manifest. This feature has remained in alpha ever since due to performance and correctness issues inherent in its design. This PR exposes a second, independent pruning alpha powered by a new standard named ApplySets. An ApplySet is a server-side object (by default, a Secret; ConfigMaps are also allowed) that kubectl can use to accurately and efficiently track set membership across `apply` operations. The format used for ApplySet is set out in  [KEP 3659](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3659) as a low-level specification.  Other tools in the ecosystem can also build on this specification for improved interoperability.  To try the ApplySet-based pruning alpha, set `KUBECTL_APPLYSET=true` and use the flags `--prune --applyset=secret-name` with `kubectl apply`.

enrichment.problem: The existing `kubectl apply --prune` feature, present since v1.5, suffers from performance and correctness problems, making it unreliable for deleting resources that were removed from manifests.
enrichment.affected: Users who rely on `kubectl apply --prune` to remove resources no longer defined in their manifests, including CI pipelines and GitOps workflows.
enrichment.fix: Introduces an alpha‑stage ApplySet‑based pruning mechanism. An ApplySet is a server‑side object (Secret by default, ConfigMap also supported) that kubectl uses to track set membership across apply operations, enabling accurate and efficient pruning. Enabled with `KUBECTL_APPLYSET=true` and the flags `--prune --applyset=secret-name`.
enrichment.impact: Provides a more reliable and performant way to prune resources, reducing the risk of orphaned objects and improving CI/CD workflows that rely on `kubectl apply --prune`. The specification also allows other tools to interoperate via the ApplySet format.

feature.description: Promoted `OpenAPIV3` to GA
feature.author: Jefftree

enrichment.problem: OpenAPIV3 support was only in beta, lacking guaranteed stability for production workloads.
enrichment.affected: All clusters and tools that consume the Kubernetes OpenAPI v3 schema, such as client generators and API documentation systems.
enrichment.fix: Promoted OpenAPIV3 to GA status in the API machinery, stabilizing the spec generation and guaranteeing backward compatibility.
enrichment.impact: Users and tooling that rely on the OpenAPI v3 spec (e.g., client libraries, API explorers) can now safely use it in production, improving reliability and ecosystem integration.

feature.description: Graduated `matchLabelKeys` in `podTopologySpread` to Beta
feature.author: denkensk

enrichment.problem: The `matchLabelKeys` field for pod topology spread constraints was only available as an alpha feature, limiting its use in production environments.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that use pod topology spread constraints and want to match pods based on specific label keys. Cluster operators can now enable this capability without the risk associated with alpha features.
enrichment.fix: The field has been promoted to beta, making it a stable, supported part of the PodSpec and enabling the scheduler to consider label-key matching when spreading pods across topology domains.
enrichment.impact: Users can now rely on `matchLabelKeys` for more precise pod placement across zones, nodes, or other topologies, improving workload distribution and resilience in production clusters.

feature.description: Enable external plugins can be used as subcommands for kubectl create command if subcommand does not exist as builtin only when KUBECTL_ENABLE_CMD_SHADOW environment variable is exported.
feature.author: ardaguclu

enrichment.problem: External kubectl plugins could not be invoked as subcommands of `kubectl create` because the command was not permitted to shadow built‑in subcommands, making it impossible to extend `create` with custom functionality.
enrichment.affected: kubectl users who want to run external plugins as `kubectl create <plugin>` commands.
enrichment.fix: The change introduces support for external plugins to be used as subcommands of `kubectl create` when the requested subcommand does not already exist as a built‑in command, gated by the `KUBECTL_ENABLE_CMD_SHADOW` environment variable.
enrichment.impact: Users can now add custom create‑related operations via plugins without modifying the core binary, improving extensibility and workflow automation. The behavior is opt‑in via an environment variable, preserving backward compatibility.

feature.description:
By enabling the alpha `CloudNodeIPs` feature gate in kubelet and the cloud
provider, you can now specify a dual-stack `--node-ip` value (when using an
external cloud provider that supports that functionality).
feature.author: danwinship
feature.userFacingChange:
By enabling the alpha `CloudNodeIPs` feature gate in kubelet and the cloud
provider, you can now specify a dual-stack `--node-ip` value (when using an
external cloud provider that supports that functionality).

enrichment.problem: Kubelet only allowed a single-stack --node-ip, preventing users from configuring nodes with both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses when using external cloud providers that support dual‑stack.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using an external cloud provider that supports dual‑stack node IPs and that enable the CloudNodeIPs feature gate.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the alpha CloudNodeIPs feature gate in kubelet and the cloud provider, allowing a dual‑stack value to be supplied to the --node-ip flag for supported external cloud providers.
enrichment.impact: Enables dual‑stack node IP configuration, simplifying network setup for clusters that require both IPv4 and IPv6, and expands flexibility for cloud‑provider integrations.

feature.description:
HPA controller exposes the following metrics from the kube-controller-manager.
- `metric_computation_duration_seconds`: Number of metric computations. 
- `metric_computation_total`: The time(seconds) that the HPA controller takes to calculate one metric.
feature.author: sanposhiho
feature.userFacingChange:
HPA controller exposes the following metrics from the kube-controller-manager.
- `metric_computation_duration_seconds`: Number of metric computations. 
- `metric_computation_total`: The time(seconds) that the HPA controller takes to calculate one metric.

enrichment.problem: The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) controller did not expose any metrics about its metric computation latency or count, making it difficult for cluster operators to monitor, debug, or tune HPA performance.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, particularly operators who need visibility into HPA performance.
enrichment.fix: Added two new Prometheus metrics to the kube‑controller‑manager: `metric_computation_duration_seconds` (the number of metric computations performed) and `metric_computation_total` (the time in seconds taken to calculate a single metric).
enrichment.impact: Operators can now observe and alert on HPA metric‑computation performance, identify bottlenecks, and improve autoscaling reliability and tuning. Improves overall cluster observability.

feature.description:
Unlocked the `CSIMigrationvSphere` feature gate.
The change allow users to continue using the in-tree vSphere driver,pending a vSphere
CSI driver release that has with GA support for Windows, XFS, and raw block access.
feature.author: msau42
feature.userFacingChange:
Unlocked the `CSIMigrationvSphere` feature gate.
The change allow users to continue using the in-tree vSphere driver,pending a vSphere
CSI driver release that has with GA support for Windows, XFS, and raw block access.

enrichment.problem: The vSphere CSI driver does not yet have GA support for Windows, XFS, and raw block access, and the CSIMigrationvSphere feature gate was disabled, risking loss of functionality for users relying on the in‑tree vSphere driver.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters that use the in‑tree vSphere volume driver, particularly workloads on Windows nodes or those requiring XFS or raw block storage.
enrichment.fix: The CSIMigrationvSphere feature gate is unlocked, allowing clusters to continue using the in‑tree vSphere driver until a fully GA vSphere CSI driver with the missing capabilities is released.
enrichment.impact: Enables vSphere storage users—especially those on Windows, using XFS or raw block volumes—to keep their workloads running without interruption and provides a smoother migration path to the CSI driver.

feature.description: [alpha: kubectl apply --prune --applyset] Enabled certain custom resources (CRs) to be used as `ApplySet` parent objects. To enable this for a given CR, apply the label `applyset.kubernetes.io/is-parent-type: true` to the CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) that defines it.
feature.author: KnVerey
feature.userFacingChange: [alpha: kubectl apply --prune --applyset] Enables certain custom resources (CRs) to be used as ApplySet parent objects. To enable this for a given CR, apply the label `applyset.kubernetes.io/is-parent-type: true` to the CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) that defines it .

enrichment.problem: kubectl apply --prune --applyset could only use built‑in resources as ApplySet parent objects, preventing users from organizing custom resources into ApplySets.
enrichment.affected: Users of kubectl who need to prune/apply sets of resources and want to use a custom resource as the parent object.
enrichment.fix: Introduces an alpha feature where a CustomResourceDefinition can be labeled with `applyset.kubernetes.io/is-parent-type: true`. Such CRDs can then serve as ApplySet parent objects for `kubectl apply --prune --applyset`.
enrichment.impact: Allows operators to use their own custom resources as logical parents for ApplySet operations, simplifying bulk apply/prune workflows and improving consistency for workloads that rely on custom APIs.

feature.description: By enabling the `UserNamespacesStatelessPodsSupport` feature gate in kubelet, you can now run a stateless pod in a separate user namespace
feature.author: giuseppe

enrichment.problem: Stateless pods could not be run in separate user namespaces, preventing workloads from taking advantage of user namespace isolation for security and multi‑tenant scenarios.
enrichment.affected: Users who want to run stateless pods with user namespace isolation (e.g., security‑focused or multi‑tenant workloads).
enrichment.fix: Introduced the UserNamespacesStatelessPodsSupport feature gate in kubelet. When enabled, kubelet configures the pod's runtime to create and use a distinct user namespace for the pod, allowing stateless pods to run with user namespace isolation.
enrichment.impact: Enables finer‑grained security isolation for stateless workloads, expands the set of workloads that can leverage user namespaces, and supports use‑cases such as unprivileged multi‑tenant clusters without sacrificing pod functionality.

feature.description: Switched kubectl explain to use OpenAPIV3 information published by the server. OpenAPIV2 backend can  still be used with the `--output plaintext-openapiv2` argument
feature.author: alexzielenski

enrichment.problem: kubectl explain was based on the OpenAPIV2 (Swagger) schema served by the API server, which lacked support for newer OpenAPI v3 features and could provide incomplete or outdated resource documentation.
enrichment.affected: All users of the `kubectl explain` command, especially those relying on up‑to‑date field information for resource definitions.
enrichment.fix: The implementation of kubectl explain now defaults to consuming the OpenAPIV3 schema published by the server. Users can still request the legacy OpenAPIV2 output with the `--output plaintext-openapiv2` flag.
enrichment.impact: Users get more accurate and complete documentation for Kubernetes resources, including new fields introduced via OpenAPI v3. This improves developer experience and reduces confusion when exploring API objects.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.20.2
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes was previously built with an older Go toolchain, which could lack recent language improvements, security patches, and performance fixes.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) built from source.
enrichment.fix: The build system has been updated to compile all Kubernetes components with Go 1.20.2.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes binaries benefit from Go 1.20.2's bug fixes, security updates, and performance enhancements, reducing potential build‑time issues for downstream users and improving overall reliability.

feature.description: Updated `kube-apiserver` SLO/SLI latency metrics to exclude priority & fairness queue wait times
feature.author: andrewsykim
feature.userFacingChange: Update kube-apiserver SLO/SLI latency metrics to exclude priority & fairness queue wait times

enrichment.problem: kube-apiserver SLO/SLI latency metrics historically included the time a request spent waiting in the priority and fairness queue, inflating the measured latency and giving operators a misleading view of actual request processing time.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that monitor kube-apiserver latency SLO/SLI metrics; any tooling or dashboards that consume those metrics.
enrichment.fix: The metrics collection logic in kube-apiserver was updated to subtract the queue wait time, so the reported latency reflects only the time spent processing the request after it leaves the priority‑and‑fairness queue.
enrichment.impact: Operators get more accurate latency numbers for SLO/SLI tracking, enabling better alerting and capacity planning. Dashboard and alert thresholds based on these metrics will now correspond to true request handling latency.

feature.description:
Updated distroless iptables to use released image `registry.k8s.io/build-image/distroless-iptables:v0.2.2`
- Updated setcap to use released image `registry.k8s.io/build-image/setcap:bullseye-v1.4.2`

feature.description: Promoted `whoami` kubectl command.
feature.author: nabokihms
feature.userFacingChange: Promote `whoami` kubectl command.

enrichment.affected: All users of kubectl, especially those who work with multiple authentication contexts or service accounts.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the `kubectl whoami` command, which prints the currently configured user (and optionally the associated context) directly to standard output.
enrichment.impact: Simplifies workflow for developers and administrators who switch between multiple clusters or service accounts, reducing errors caused by operating under the wrong identity.

feature.description: Migrated the main kube-controller-manager binary to use [contextual logging](https://k8s.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/system-logs/#contextual-logging).
feature.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: kube-controller-manager logs were plain text without structured context, making it difficult for operators to correlate log entries and diagnose issues.

enrichment.fix: The kube-controller-manager binary is migrated to use the new contextual logging framework, emitting logs with structured fields (e.g., component, level, request IDs) per KEP 3077.
enrichment.impact: Operators and tooling gain richer, machine‑parseable logs from the controller manager, improving debugging, alerting, and overall observability without affecting cluster functionality.

feature.description: Added e2e tests for kubectl `--subresource` for beta graduation
feature.author: MadhavJivrajani
feature.userFacingChange: Adding e2e tests for kubectl --subresource for beta graduation

enrichment.problem: The kubectl `--subresource` feature was graduating to beta without dedicated end‑to‑end tests, risking unnoticed regressions or broken behavior in future releases.

feature.description: Changed kubectl `--subresource` flag to beta
feature.author: MadhavJivrajani
feature.userFacingChange: Change kubectl --subresource flag to beta

enrichment.problem: The kubectl `--subresource` flag was only available as an alpha feature, meaning it was hidden by default, less stable, and required explicit enabling, limiting its usability for users who need to work with subresources.

enrichment.fix: Promoted the `--subresource` flag to beta status, making it enabled by default and indicating a higher stability guarantee while retaining the same functionality.
enrichment.impact: Users can now rely on the `--subresource` flag in production environments without extra opt‑in steps, improving the ergonomics and reliability of subresource operations in kubectl.

feature.description:
Upgrades functionality of `kubectl kustomize` as described at
https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/releases/tag/kustomize%2Fv5.0.0 and https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/releases/tag/kustomize%2Fv5.0.1. 

This is a new major release of kustomize, so there are a few backwards-incompatible changes, most of which are rare use cases, bug fixes with side effects, or things that have been deprecated for multiple releases already:

- https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/pull/4911: Drop support for a very old, legacy style of patches. patches used to be allowed to be used as an alias for patchesStrategicMerge in kustomize v3. You now have to use patchesStrategicMerge explicitly, or update to the new syntax supported by patches. See examples in the PR description of https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/pull/4911.
- https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/issues/4731: Remove a potential build-time side-effect in ConfigMapGenerator and SecretGenerator, which loaded values from the local environment under some circumstances, breaking kustomize build's side-effect-free promise. While this behavior was never intended, we deprecated it and are announcing it as a breaking change since it existed for a long time. See also the Eschewed Features documentation.
- https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/pull/4985: If you previously included .git in an AWS or Azure URL, we will no longer automatically remove that suffix. You may need to add an extra / to replace the .git for the URL to properly resolve.
- https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/pull/4954: Drop support for using gh: as a host (e.g. gh:kubernetes-sigs/kustomize). We were unable to find any usage of or basis for this and believe it may have been targeting a custom gitconfig shorthand syntax.
feature.author: natasha41575
feature.userFacingChange:
Upgrades functionality of `kubectl kustomize` as described at
https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/releases/tag/kustomize%2Fv5.0.0 and https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/releases/tag/kustomize%2Fv5.0.1. 

This is a new major release of kustomize, so there are a few backwards-incompatible changes, most of which are rare use cases, bug fixes with side effects, or things that have been deprecated for multiple releases already:

- https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/pull/4911: Drop support for a very old, legacy style of patches. patches used to be allowed to be used as an alias for patchesStrategicMerge in kustomize v3. You now have to use patchesStrategicMerge explicitly, or update to the new syntax supported by patches. See examples in the PR description of https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/pull/4911.
- https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/issues/4731: Remove a potential build-time side-effect in ConfigMapGenerator and SecretGenerator, which loaded values from the local environment under some circumstances, breaking kustomize build's side-effect-free promise. While this behavior was never intended, we deprecated it and are announcing it as a breaking change since it existed for a long time. See also the Eschewed Features documentation.
- https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/pull/4985: If you previously included .git in an AWS or Azure URL, we will no longer automatically remove that suffix. You may need to add an extra / to replace the .git for the URL to properly resolve.
- https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/pull/4954: Drop support for using gh: as a host (e.g. gh:kubernetes-sigs/kustomize). We were unable to find any usage of or basis for this and believe it may have been targeting a custom gitconfig shorthand syntax.

enrichment.problem: kubectl kustomize upgraded to kustomize v5, which drops several legacy features: the old `patches` alias for `patchesStrategicMerge`, automatic loading of environment variables in ConfigMapGenerator/SecretGenerator, automatic stripping of a `.git` suffix in AWS/Azure URLs, and the `gh:` host shorthand. Users relying on these behaviors will see build failures or incorrect resource references.
enrichment.affected: Any workflow that uses `kubectl kustomize` with the removed legacy patch syntax, environment‑driven ConfigMap/Secret generation, AWS/Azure URLs ending with `.git`, or the `gh:` shorthand will be affected.
enrichment.fix: The upgrade removes the deprecated behaviors. Users must update Kustomization files to use `patchesStrategicMerge` explicitly, avoid relying on env-var loading in generators, include a trailing `/` when a `.git` suffix is needed in remote URLs, and stop using the `gh:` shorthand (use full URL instead).
enrichment.impact: Ensures kustomize builds remain side-effect‑free and aligns with the new major version. Users need to adjust configurations, but the changes prevent unexpected environment leakage and ambiguous URL handling.

feature.description: `kube-scheduler`: Optimized implementation of null `labelSelector` in topology spreading.
feature.author: alculquicondor
feature.userFacingChange: kube-scheduler: Optimized implementation of null labelSelector in topology spreading.

enrichment.problem: The scheduler's handling of a null labelSelector in topology spread constraints was inefficient, causing unnecessary computation during scheduling.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with pods that define topologySpreadConstraints with a null labelSelector; workloads that rely on topology-aware pod placement.
enrichment.fix: Implemented an optimized code path for null labelSelector when evaluating topology spreading, reducing overhead.
enrichment.impact: Scheduling latency is reduced for pods that use topologySpreadConstraints without a labelSelector, improving overall cluster throughput, especially in large clusters.

feature.description: Locked `CSIMigrationvSphere` feature gate.
feature.author: xing-yang
feature.userFacingChange: Locks CSIMigrationvSphere feature gate.

enrichment.problem: The CSIMigrationvSphere feature gate could be toggled by users, leading to potential inconsistencies or unsupported configurations during migration from in-tree vSphere volumes to CSI.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the vSphere CSI migration path, particularly those that might have attempted to enable or disable the CSIMigrationvSphere feature gate.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate is now locked, making its setting immutable and preventing users from enabling or disabling CSIMigrationvSphere at runtime.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that rely on vSphere CSI migration can no longer change the gate state, ensuring stable and predictable behavior. Users must upgrade to a version where the gate's default behavior matches their needs.

enrichment.impact: CI pipelines and developers running the test suite now use a vetted, version‑locked image, improving build reproducibility and ensuring any upstream security or bug fixes are included.

deprecation.description: support for the alpha seccomp annotations `seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod` and `container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io` were deprecated since v1.19, now have been completely removed. The seccomp fields are no longer auto-populated when pods with seccomp annotations are created. Pods should use the corresponding pod or container `securityContext.seccompProfile` field instead.
deprecation.author: saschagrunert
deprecation.userFacingChange: Action required: support for the alpha seccomp annotations `seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod` and `container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io`, deprecated since v1.19, has been completely removed. The seccomp fields are no longer auto-populated when pods with seccomp annotations are created. Pods should use the corresponding pod or container `securityContext.seccompProfile` field instead.

issueContext.title: Graduate Seccomp to GA
issueContext.body:
Graduate seccomp to GA, as defined on the respective [KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-node/20190717-seccomp-ga.md). This is an umbrella issue to track all outstanding work.

### Core Items
- [x] API Server changes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/91408 (MERGED)
- [x] Kubelet changes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/91381 (MERGED)
- [x] Mark flag `--seccomp-profile-root` as deprecated https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/91182 (MERGED)
- [x] Update PSP to support seccomp fields https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/92856 (MERGED)
- [x] Document Kubernetes seccomp support https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/21278 (MERGED)

### Nice to Have on 1.19
- [x] Add seccomp least privilege for docker sandbox https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/90948 (MERGED)
- [x] Add seccomp least privilege for kuberuntime https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/90949 (MERGED)
- [x] E2E tests review https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/91442 (LGTM)

### Pushed to 1.22
- [x] Add Warning mechanism for deprecated features usage (based off [KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/1693-warnings))

/area kubelet
/area kubelet-api
/sig node
/area security
/assign

enrichment.problem: The alpha seccomp annotations `seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/pod` and `container.seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io` have been removed. Pods created with these annotations no longer have their seccomp fields auto-populated, causing the intended seccomp profile to be omitted.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads that use the removed alpha seccomp annotations in pod or container definitions.
enrichment.fix: The removal is final; users must update manifests to specify the seccomp profile using the stable `securityContext.seccompProfile` field on pods or containers.
enrichment.impact: Pods that relied on the deprecated annotations will run without the desired seccomp confinement until the manifests are migrated, potentially reducing security posture. Updating manifests restores explicit seccomp profiling.

deprecation.description: The `SecurityContextDeny` admission plugin is going deprecated and will be removed in future versions.
deprecation.author: mtardy
deprecation.userFacingChange: The SecurityContextDeny admission plugin is going deprecated and will be removed in future versions.

enrichment.problem: The SecurityContextDeny admission plugin is deprecated and will be removed in future Kubernetes releases, breaking clusters that rely on it for enforcing pod security policies.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with the SecurityContextDeny admission plugin enabled, and any workloads that depend on its security checks.
enrichment.fix: The plugin is being phased out; users should transition to the newer PodSecurity admission mechanism or other policy enforcement tools before the plugin is removed.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that have SecurityContextDeny enabled will lose that security check after removal, potentially allowing insecure pod specifications unless mitigated by alternative policies.

deprecation.description: Added a [warning](https://k8s.io/blog/2020/09/03/warnings/) response when handling requests that set the deprecated `spec.externalID` field for a Node.
deprecation.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: Requests that include the deprecated `spec.externalID` field on a Node did not provide any indication that the field is deprecated, so users could continue using it unknowingly.
enrichment.affected: Any client, controller, or script that creates or updates Node objects with the `spec.externalID` field.
enrichment.fix: The API server now returns a warning in the response when a request sets the `spec.externalID` field on a Node, informing the client that the field is deprecated.
enrichment.impact: Operators and developers receive immediate feedback about the deprecated field, allowing them to migrate away before the field is removed, reducing upgrade friction and potential failures.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a regression in 1.27.0 that resulted in "missing metadata in converted object" errors when modifying objects for multi-version custom resource definitions with a conversion strategy of `None`.
bugOrRegression.author: ncdc

enrichment.problem: A regression introduced in v1.27.0 caused "missing metadata in converted object" errors when modifying objects of multi-version CustomResourceDefinitions that use the `None` conversion strategy.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that contain custom resources defined by multi‑version CRDs with a `None` conversion strategy; API clients that attempt to update those resources were affected.
enrichment.fix: Restores proper handling of object metadata during conversion for multi‑version CRDs with the `None` strategy, preventing the metadata loss and associated errors.
enrichment.impact: Users with multi‑version CRDs using the `None` conversion strategy can again modify their resources without errors, restoring normal API functionality and preventing operational disruptions.

bugOrRegression.description: Known issue: fixed that the PreEnqueue plugins aren't executed for Pods proceeding to activeQ through backoffQ.
bugOrRegression.author: sanposhiho

enrichment.problem: PreEnqueue scheduler plugins were not executed when Pods moved from the backoff queue to the active queue, causing those Pods to bypass plugin logic such as priority or other pre‑enqueue checks.
enrichment.affected: Pods that experienced a scheduling backoff and were later re‑queued to the active queue; cluster administrators relying on PreEnqueue plugins for policy enforcement.
enrichment.fix: The kube‑scheduler now invokes PreEnqueue plugins for Pods that transition from backoffQ to activeQ, ensuring consistent plugin processing for all Pods.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that all Pods are subject to the intended pre‑enqueue policies, preventing unexpected scheduling decisions and improving fairness and predictability.

bugOrRegression.description: Setting a mirror pod's phase to Succeeded or Failed can prevent the corresponding static pod from restarting due mutation of a Kubelet cache.
bugOrRegression.author: smarterclayton

enrichment.problem: When a mirror pod (the kubelet’s representation of a static pod) had its status.phase set to Succeeded or Failed, the kubelet mutated its cache in a way that prevented the static pod from being restarted.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running static pods on any node, particularly control‑plane components that rely on static pod mirroring.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet logic was updated so that setting the mirror pod phase no longer corrupts the cache, allowing the static pod controller to detect the terminated state and recreate the pod as expected.
enrichment.impact: Static pods such as kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, and kube-proxy on control‑plane nodes will now be correctly restarted after they exit, improving cluster reliability and preventing unintended downtime of critical components.

apiChange.description: Added error handling for seccomp localhost configurations that do not properly set a localhostProfile
apiChange.author: cji

enrichment.problem: When a pod spec used a seccomp profile of type "Localhost" but did not set the required localhostProfile field, the system failed to handle the misconfiguration properly, leading to unclear errors or pod start failures.
enrichment.affected: Pods that specify a seccomp profile of type Localhost without providing a localhostProfile, typically users customizing security profiles on nodes.
enrichment.fix: Added explicit error handling to detect seccomp localhost configurations lacking a localhostProfile and return a clear validation error.
enrichment.impact: Users configuring seccomp via localhost now receive a descriptive error instead of silent failures, improving debugging and cluster stability for workloads that rely on custom seccomp profiles.

apiChange.description: Fixed an issue where kubelet does not set case-insensitive headers for http probes. (#117182, @dddddai)
apiChange.author: dddddai

enrichment.problem: kubelet failed to set HTTP probe headers in a case‑insensitive way, causing readiness/liveness probes to be rejected by servers that expect case‑insensitive header handling.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use HTTP readiness or liveness probes and rely on case‑insensitive header handling.
enrichment.fix: kubelet now normalises and sets probe headers case‑insensitively, ensuring they comply with the HTTP specification.
enrichment.impact: HTTP probes work reliably for all workloads, preventing false‑negative health checks and unnecessary pod restarts.

apiChange.description: Revised the comment about the feature-gate level for PodFailurePolicy from alpha to beta
apiChange.author: kerthcet

enrichment.problem: The comment for the PodFailurePolicy feature gate incorrectly stated its maturity level as alpha, which could mislead users about its stability and readiness.
enrichment.affected: Anyone reading the PodFailurePolicy documentation or relying on the feature-gate description could have been misinformed about its stability.
enrichment.fix: The comment has been updated to correctly indicate that the PodFailurePolicy feature gate is at beta level.
enrichment.impact: Users and developers now have accurate documentation about the feature's maturity, reducing confusion and helping them make informed decisions when using PodFailurePolicy.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.4
feature.author: xmudrii

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes was built with an older Go toolchain, which may lack recent security patches, bug fixes, and language improvements.
enrichment.affected: Anyone building Kubernetes from source—including CI/CD pipelines and custom builds—will now compile with Go 1.20.4. End‑users of official binaries are indirectly affected through the upgraded toolchain.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.20.4 for compiling all Kubernetes components.
enrichment.impact: All binaries (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, etc.) now benefit from Go security updates, performance enhancements, and improved compiler behavior. No functional changes to clusters, but downstream builds and CI pipelines must use Go 1.20.4.

failingTest.description: Allow Azure Disk e2es to use newer topology labels if available from nodes
failingTest.author: gnufied

enrichment.problem: Three critical CVEs (CVE-2023-27561, CVE-2023-25809, CVE-2023-28642) were present in runc v1.1.4, allowing potential container escape or privilege escalation on nodes.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes node that uses the default runc v1.1.4 runtime; all pods and containers running on those nodes are at risk.
enrichment.fix: Update the bundled runc binary from v1.1.4 to v1.1.5, which contains patches that remediate the reported vulnerabilities.
enrichment.impact: Secures the node's container runtime against remote code execution and privilege escalation, protecting workloads and reducing the attack surface for Kubernetes clusters.

bugOrRegression.description: During device plugin allocation, resources requested by the pod can only be allocated if the device plugin has registered itself to kubelet AND healthy devices are present on the node to be allocated. If these conditions are not sattsfied, the pod would fail with `UnexpectedAdmissionError` error.
bugOrRegression.author: swatisehgal

enrichment.problem: Pods that requested devices via a device plugin could fail with an UnexpectedAdmissionError when the plugin was not fully registered or when the node had no healthy devices, even though the pod should have been admitted or scheduled later.
enrichment.affected: Pods that request hardware devices via device plugins on nodes where the plugin registration or device health state was transiently invalid.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet device plugin allocation logic was updated to only reject a pod when the plugin is not registered *and* healthy devices are unavailable. The admission check now correctly allows allocation to proceed when appropriate, preventing spurious pod failures.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability for workloads that depend on GPU, FPGA, or other hardware accelerators. Pods will no longer be rejected unexpectedly, reducing downtime and manual intervention for users of device plugins.

bugOrRegression.description: Fallback from OpenAPI V3 to V2 when the OpenAPI V3 document is invalid or incomplete.
bugOrRegression.author: seans3

enrichment.problem: When the API server's OpenAPI v3 document is invalid or incomplete, kubectl fails to retrieve the schema, causing commands that rely on discovery to error out.
enrichment.affected: kubectl users and any automation that relies on the CLI for API discovery, particularly when the API server serves an invalid OpenAPI v3 definition.
enrichment.fix: kubectl now automatically falls back to using the OpenAPI v2 document if the v3 document cannot be parsed or is missing required information, ensuring commands continue to work.
enrichment.impact: Improves CLI resilience and prevents disruptions for users and automation pipelines that interact with clusters providing broken OpenAPI v3 specs.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix bug where `listOfStrings.join()` in CEL expressions resulted in an unexpected internal error.
bugOrRegression.author: jpbetz

enrichment.problem: CEL expressions that called listOfStrings.join() triggered an unexpected internal error, causing validation or defaulting logic to fail.
enrichment.affected: Any workloads or CRDs that rely on CEL expressions using listOfStrings.join(), such as custom resource validation rules.
enrichment.fix: Implemented proper handling for listOfStrings.join() in the CEL evaluator, eliminating the internal error and returning the correct joined string.
enrichment.impact: Users can now safely use listOfStrings.join() in CEL-based validation, defaulting, and other server-side expression contexts without encountering server errors.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix incorrect calculation for ResourceQuota with PriorityClass as its scope.
bugOrRegression.author: Huang-Wei

enrichment.problem: ResourceQuota objects that used PriorityClass as a scope calculated usage incorrectly, leading to wrong quota enforcement (either over‑consumption or unnecessary rejections).
enrichment.affected: Namespaces with ResourceQuota objects scoped by PriorityClass; workloads that rely on those quotas for admission control.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the quota calculation logic to correctly account for PriorityClass‑scoped resources, ensuring accurate tracking and enforcement of ResourceQuota limits.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators who define ResourceQuota with a PriorityClass scope will now see correct quota behavior, preventing unexpected pod admission failures or resource over‑use.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix performance regression in scheduler caused by frequent metric lookup on critical code path.
bugOrRegression.author: tosi3k

enrichment.problem: The kube-scheduler experienced a performance regression because it performed frequent metric lookups on a critical code path, causing increased scheduling latency.
enrichment.affected: All clusters using the default kube-scheduler; pods experienced delayed scheduling.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler code was changed to reduce the frequency of metric lookups and cache metric values where appropriate, eliminating the unnecessary overhead on the hot path.
enrichment.impact: Scheduling latency returns to normal, improving pod startup times and overall cluster responsiveness, especially in large clusters or workloads with high scheduling rates.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix: the volume is not detached after the pod and PVC objects are deleted
bugOrRegression.author: cvvz

enrichment.problem: When a Pod and its PersistentVolumeClaim are deleted, the associated storage volume is sometimes not detached, leaving the volume attached to the node.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using CSI volumes that delete Pods and PVCs; workloads that rely on dynamic volume provisioning and teardown.
enrichment.fix: Implemented proper cleanup in the attach‑detach controller so that volume detach logic is triggered when both the Pod and PVC objects are removed.
enrichment.impact: Prevents leaked volume attachments that could block subsequent volume deletion or reuse, reducing storage resource leakage and avoiding potential data‑access issues.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a memory leak in the Kubernetes API server that occurs during APIService processing.
bugOrRegression.author: enj

enrichment.problem: The kube-apiserver leaked memory during APIService processing, causing memory usage to continuously increase and potentially leading to OOM crashes.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with registered APIService resources (aggregated API servers) could experience API server memory bloat and restarts.
enrichment.fix: The code handling APIService objects was fixed to correctly release allocated memory, eliminating the leak.
enrichment.impact: Prevents uncontrolled memory growth in the API server, ensuring stable operation for clusters that use aggregated APIs and avoiding possible downtime.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a race condition serving OpenAPI content
bugOrRegression.author: Jefftree

enrichment.problem: A race condition in the API server could cause OpenAPI content to be served incorrectly or result in intermittent errors when clients request the OpenAPI schema.
enrichment.affected: Any component or tool that fetches OpenAPI specifications from the API server (e.g., kubectl, client libraries, CI pipelines) could experience intermittent failures.
enrichment.fix: The code that generates and serves OpenAPI documents was updated to synchronize access, eliminating the race condition and ensuring consistent, reliable delivery of the schema.
enrichment.impact: Clients such as kubectl, custom controllers, and other tooling that rely on the OpenAPI discovery documents will receive correct data consistently, reducing failures and improving overall cluster usability.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a regression in kubectl and client-go discovery when configured with a server URL other than the root of a server.
bugOrRegression.author: ardaguclu

enrichment.problem: kubectl and client-go discovery stopped working when the configured server URL included a non-root path prefix, causing commands that rely on discovery to fail.
enrichment.affected: Users and automation that run kubectl or use client-go with a server URL that includes a path prefix (non‑root) rather than just the root domain.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the discovery logic in kubectl and client-go to correctly handle server URLs that are not at the root, restoring proper discovery and command execution.
enrichment.impact: Restores functionality for clusters accessed via custom base paths (e.g., through proxies or API gateways), preventing broken CLI operations and client library calls.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fixes bug where an incomplete OpenAPI V3 document can cause a nil-pointer crash.
  Ensures fallback to OpenAPI V2 endpoint for errors retrieving OpenAPI V3 document.
bugOrRegression.author: seans3

enrichment.problem: kubectl could panic with a nil-pointer dereference when the API server’s OpenAPI V3 document was incomplete or malformed.
enrichment.affected: kubectl users who rely on API discovery (e.g., command‑completion, help, and dynamic client generation) when the API server provides an incomplete OpenAPI V3 document.
enrichment.fix: kubectl now detects errors while retrieving the OpenAPI V3 spec and automatically falls back to the OpenAPI V2 endpoint, avoiding the crash.
enrichment.impact: Prevents CLI crashes during API discovery, ensuring kubectl commands (including help, completion, and resource introspection) continue to work even against servers that serve an incomplete OpenAPI V3 spec.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix a bug where file copy(backup) could not be executed correctly on Windows platform during upgrade
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: During kubeadm upgrade on Windows nodes, the file copy (backup) step failed, preventing successful upgrades.
enrichment.affected: Users performing kubeadm upgrades on Windows nodes were unable to complete the upgrade due to backup copy failures.
enrichment.fix: Corrected the file copy implementation in kubeadm for Windows, ensuring backups are created and restored properly during upgrades.
enrichment.impact: Windows clusters can now be upgraded with kubeadm without failure, reducing upgrade downtime and avoiding potential data loss.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubelet terminates pods correctly upon restart, fixing an issue where pods may have not been fully terminated if the kubelet was restarted during pod termination.
bugOrRegression.author: bobbypage

enrichment.problem: If the kubelet was restarted while a pod was in the termination phase, the pod could remain in a partially‑terminated state, leaving resources dangling and the pod appearing not fully deleted.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that relied on graceful pod termination could be left in an incomplete state when the node’s kubelet was restarted during termination.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now tracks pods that are shutting down and, after a restart, ensures they are completed and fully removed, guaranteeing correct termination semantics.
enrichment.impact: Clusters no longer end up with orphaned or stuck pods after a kubelet restart, improving reliability of pod cleanup and preventing resource leaks that could affect subsequent scheduling.

bugOrRegression.description: Number of errors reported to the metric `storage_operation_duration_seconds_count` for emptyDir decreased significantly because previously one error was reported for each projected volume created.
bugOrRegression.author: mpatlasov

enrichment.problem: The metric `storage_operation_duration_seconds_count` reported an error for every projected volume created within an emptyDir, causing an abnormally high error count and misleading monitoring data.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using emptyDir with projected volumes saw inflated error counts in the `storage_operation_duration_seconds_count` metric, affecting monitoring and alerting systems.
enrichment.fix: The metric collection logic was updated to count only one error per storage operation rather than per projected volume, dramatically reducing the reported error count for emptyDir.
enrichment.impact: Users get accurate error metrics for emptyDir storage operations, reducing false alarms and improving the reliability of observability dashboards that depend on this metric.

bugOrRegression.description: Resolves a spurious "Unknown discovery response content-type" error in client-go discovery requests by tolerating extra content-type parameters in API responses
bugOrRegression.author: seans3

enrichment.problem: client-go discovery requests sometimes failed with an "Unknown discovery response content-type" error when the API server's Content-Type header included extra parameters.
enrichment.affected: Any software using client-go for discovery (kubectl, controller managers, custom operators) that received API responses with extra Content-Type parameters.
enrichment.fix: The discovery code now tolerates additional content-type parameters in API responses, preventing the spurious error and allowing discovery to succeed.
enrichment.impact: Clients that use the Go client library for API discovery (e.g., kubectl, controllers, operators) will no longer encounter failures due to non‑canonical Content-Type headers, improving reliability of cluster interactions.

bugOrRegression.description: Reverted NewVolumeManagerReconstruction and SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod feature gates to disabled by default to resolve a regression of volume reconstruction on kubelet/node restart
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: Enabling the NewVolumeManagerReconstruction and SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod feature gates caused a regression where volume reconstruction failed after a kubelet or node restart, leading to pods being unable to mount their volumes.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet and any pods using persistent volumes on nodes that were restarted while the feature gates were enabled.
enrichment.fix: The two feature gates have been reverted to disabled by default, restoring the previous stable behavior of volume reconstruction on node restarts.
enrichment.impact: Restores reliability for workloads that depend on persistent volumes after node restarts, preventing pod start failures and reducing downtime.

bugOrRegression.description: Static pods were taking extra time to be restarted after being updated.  Static pods that are waiting to restart were not correctly counted in `kubelet_working_pods`.
bugOrRegression.author: smarterclayton

enrichment.problem: Static pods that needed to be restarted after an update experienced extra delay, and pods waiting to restart were not included in the `kubelet_working_pods` metric.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run static pods (e.g., self‑hosted control‑plane components) saw slower restarts and misleading kubelet metrics.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now correctly counts static pods that are pending restart as working pods, ensuring they are restarted promptly and the metric reflects the true number of active pods.
enrichment.impact: Static pod restarts (including critical control‑plane components when self‑hosted) happen without unnecessary delay, and monitoring/alerting based on `kubelet_working_pods` becomes accurate.

bugOrRegression.description:
[KCCM] service controller: change the cloud controller manager to make `providerID` a predicate when synchronizing nodes. This change allows load balancer integrations to ensure that  the `providerID` is set when configuring
  load balancers and targets.
bugOrRegression.author: alexanderConstantinescu

enrichment.problem: Load balancer integrations could attempt to configure load balancers before a node's providerID was set, leading to failed or incomplete provisioning.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using cloud provider load balancer integrations (Service of type LoadBalancer) where nodes may not have providerID set at sync time.
enrichment.fix: The service controller in the cloud controller manager now treats `providerID` as a predicate during node synchronization, ensuring that providerID is set before any load balancer or target configuration is performed.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability of Service type=LoadBalancer provisioning by preventing errors due to missing providerID, benefiting clusters that rely on cloud provider load balancer integrations.

other.description: A v2-level info log will be added, which will output the details of the pod being preempted, including victim and preemptor
other.author: HirazawaUi

enrichment.problem: Kube-scheduler did not provide detailed logs about preemption events, making it hard for operators to understand which pod was preempted (victim) and which pod caused the preemption (preemptor).
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators and developers troubleshooting pod preemption scenarios.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new v2-level info log in kube-scheduler that prints the victim and preemptor pod details whenever a preemption occurs.
enrichment.impact: Improves observability and debugging of scheduling preemption, helping operators diagnose and tune workloads that involve preemption.

other.description: Structured logging of NamespacedName was inconsistent with klog.KObj. Now both use lower case field names and namespace is optional.
other.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: NamespacedName fields were logged with inconsistent capitalization compared to klog.KObj, causing mismatched log keys and making log parsing harder.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes component or external tool that logs NamespacedName via klog (e.g., API server, controller manager, kubelet, etc.)
enrichment.fix: Aligned structured logging of NamespacedName with klog.KObj by using lower‑case field names for both and making the namespace field optional.
enrichment.impact: Logs are now uniform across components, simplifying log aggregation, search, and debugging for operators and tooling that rely on structured logs.

securityFixes.title: Bypassing enforce mountable secrets policy imposed by the ServiceAccount admission plugin
securityFixes.description:
A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where users may be able to launch containers that bypass the mountable secrets policy enforced by the ServiceAccount admission plugin when using ephemeral containers. The policy ensures pods running with a service account may only reference secrets specified in the service account's secrets field. Kubernetes clusters are only affected if the ServiceAccount admission plugin and the `kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets` annotation are used together with ephemeral containers.

**Note**: This only impacts the cluster if the ServiceAccount admission plugin is used (most cluster should have this on by default as recommended in https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/admission-controllers/#serviceaccount), the `kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets` annotation is used by a service account (this annotation is not added by default), and Pods are using ephemeral containers.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.5
feature.author: puerco

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, which could miss recent language security patches, bug fixes, and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes users who run or build the official binaries, as every component is recompiled with the newer Go toolchain.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to compile all Kubernetes components with Go 1.20.5.
enrichment.impact: Users and operators receive binaries that incorporate the latest Go security and stability updates, reducing potential supply‑chain risks and ensuring better compatibility with future Go releases.

bugOrRegression.description: Add DisruptionTarget condition to the pod preempted by Kubelet to make room for a critical pod
bugOrRegression.author: mimowo

enrichment.problem: When the kubelet evicts (preempts) pods to make room for a critical pod, the affected pod did not have a status condition indicating it was being preempted, making it difficult for users and controllers to understand why the pod was terminated.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that may be preempted on a node when a higher‑priority (critical) pod needs resources; administrators troubleshooting unexpected pod evictions.
enrichment.fix: Introduce a new pod condition named `DisruptionTarget` that is set by the kubelet on pods that are preempted for a critical pod. The condition is visible via the pod status, providing explicit information about the disruption reason.
enrichment.impact: Operators and higher‑level controllers can now detect and react to preemptions more reliably, improving debugging, observability, and automated handling of pod disruptions caused by critical‑pod preemption.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a bug at kube-apiserver start where APIService objects for custom resources could be deleted and recreated.
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: During kube-apiserver startup, APIService objects for custom resources could be unintentionally deleted and recreated, causing temporary loss of those aggregated APIs.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that register custom APIService objects (e.g., aggregated API servers or CRDs) could experience brief API outages at apiserver start.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the kube-apiserver start-up logic to preserve existing APIService objects for custom resources, preventing their deletion and unnecessary recreation.
enrichment.impact: Ensures stability and continuous availability of custom aggregated APIs, avoiding service interruptions for workloads that rely on those APIs.

bugOrRegression.description: If `kubeadm reset` finds no etcd member ID for the peer it removes during the `remove-etcd-member` phase, it continues immediately to other phases, instead of retrying the phase for up to 3 minutes before continuing.
bugOrRegression.author: dlipovetsky

enrichment.problem: During `kubeadm reset`, if the `remove-etcd-member` phase cannot find an etcd member ID for the peer being removed, the phase skips the retry logic and proceeds immediately to subsequent phases, potentially leaving stale etcd membership information.
enrichment.affected: Administrators running `kubeadm reset` on clusters where an etcd member ID may be missing (e.g., after prior failures or manual etcd changes).
enrichment.fix: The reset logic now retries the `remove-etcd-member` phase for up to 3 minutes when no member ID is found before moving on, ensuring the removal is given sufficient time to succeed.
enrichment.impact: Users performing a cluster reset with kubeadm will have a more reliable cleanup of etcd members, preventing leftover membership entries and reducing the chance of reset‑related errors or manual intervention.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix a bug where the static pod changes detection logic is inconsistent with kubelet
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: kubeadm's logic for detecting changes to static pod manifests was inconsistent with the kubelet's detection, causing kubeadm to miss updates to static pods.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using kubeadm‑managed static pods such as etcd, kube-apiserver, kube-controller‑manager, and kube-scheduler could experience missed pod updates.
enrichment.fix: The detection algorithm in kubeadm was updated to match the kubelet's behavior, ensuring that changes to static pod manifests are correctly recognized.
enrichment.impact: Users who rely on kubeadm to manage static pods (e.g., control‑plane components) will now see proper detection and handling of pod updates, preventing missed upgrades or restarts and improving cluster reliability.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix etc version support for Kubernetes v1.27
bugOrRegression.author: SataQiu

enrichment.problem: kubeadm did not recognize or support the required etcd version for Kubernetes v1.27, causing cluster initialization or upgrade failures for users on that version.
enrichment.affected: Anyone using kubeadm to create or upgrade a Kubernetes v1.27 cluster, especially those providing an external etcd endpoint.
enrichment.fix: Updated kubeadm to correctly handle and validate the etcd version compatible with Kubernetes v1.27, allowing successful cluster creation and upgrades.
enrichment.impact: Users can now reliably bootstrap or upgrade clusters to v1.27 with the appropriate etcd version, preventing setup errors and reducing downtime.

feature.description: Fixes the alpha `CloudDualStackNodeIPs` feature.
feature.author: danwinship

enrichment.problem: The alpha CloudDualStackNodeIPs feature was broken, preventing proper handling of dual‑stack (IPv4/IPv6) node IPs in clusters that enabled the feature.
enrichment.affected: Users who enabled the alpha CloudDualStackNodeIPs feature on their clusters, particularly those running dual‑stack workloads on cloud provider nodes.
enrichment.fix: The change restores the functionality of the CloudDualStackNodeIPs feature, ensuring node IP information is correctly populated and used by the node and networking components.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that relied on the alpha dual‑stack node IP capability can now correctly advertise and use both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, avoiding networking misconfigurations and service connectivity issues.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.20.6
feature.author: xmudrii

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes previously built with older Go version, lacking recent security fixes and language improvements.
enrichment.affected: All clusters built from source; all core components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.)
enrichment.fix: Upgrade the Kubernetes build process to use Go 1.20.6 for compiling all binaries.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components benefit from Go security patches, performance enhancements, and bug fixes, improving overall stability and future compatibility.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix component status calling etcd health endpoint over http which exposed kubernetes to the risk of complete watch starvation and is inconsistent with other etcd probing done by kube-apiserver.
bugOrRegression.author: serathius

enrichment.problem: The component status endpoint queried the etcd health endpoint over plain HTTP, exposing the cluster to the risk of complete watch starvation and differing from the secure probing used by the kube-apiserver.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the componentstatus API (kube-apiserver health checks) could experience watch starvation or insecure communication.
enrichment.fix: Component status now probes the etcd health endpoint using the same secure (HTTPS) method as other kube-apiserver health checks, eliminating the insecure HTTP call and aligning probing behavior.
enrichment.impact: Prevents potential watch starvation that could lead to loss of watch streams and API unavailability, and removes an insecure HTTP exposure, improving overall cluster reliability and security.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix cronjob controller handling of complex schedules, like "30 6-16/4 * * 1-5", for example
bugOrRegression.author: kmala

enrichment.problem: The cronjob controller failed to correctly interpret complex Cron schedule expressions such as "30 6-16/4 * * 1-5", causing jobs to be missed or executed at wrong times.
enrichment.affected: Users running CronJob objects with complex cron expressions (e.g., hourly ranges with step values) experienced missed or misfired jobs.
enrichment.fix: Updated the cronjob controller logic in kube-controller-manager to properly parse and handle complex schedule syntax, ensuring correct calculation of next execution times.
enrichment.impact: CronJob resources that rely on advanced schedule expressions now run reliably, preventing unexpected job failures or timing issues for workloads that depend on precise scheduling.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix deletion of non-admissible pods that are deleted during Kubelet restart
bugOrRegression.author: bobbypage

enrichment.problem: When the kubelet restarts, pods that have already been deleted but are still present in the kubelet's pod list (non‑admissible pods) were not cleaned up properly, leading to stale pod objects on the node.
enrichment.affected: Pods that are deleted while a kubelet is restarting, and the nodes running those kubelets.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now correctly detects and removes non‑admissible pods that are deleted during a restart, ensuring the pod lifecycle is properly reconciled after the kubelet comes back up.
enrichment.impact: Prevents orphaned pod entries and resource leakage on nodes after a kubelet restart, improving node stability and pod lifecycle consistency.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed #118052: nodeAffinity on pods can change prior to scheduling gates being removed even when podSpec.affinity is nil in the initial spec, this matches the 1.28 behavior to allow consistent integrators to be written.
bugOrRegression.author: aleskandro
