bugOrRegression.description: Updates google.golang.org/protobuf to v1.33.0 to resolve CVE-2024-24786
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: The protobuf library (google.golang.org/protobuf) used by Kubernetes contained a security vulnerability (CVE-2024-24786) that could be exploited via crafted protobuf data.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components that serialize/deserialize protobuf messages, including the API server, controller manager, scheduler, kubelet, kubectl, and cloud provider components.
enrichment.fix: Update the protobuf dependency to version v1.33.0, which includes patches that remediate the CVE.
enrichment.impact: Removes the attack surface introduced by the vulnerability, protecting clusters from potential exploitation and ensuring secure serialization of API objects.

other.description: Build etcd image v3.5.12
other.author: bzsuni

enrichment.problem: The Kubernetes release needed to update the bundled etcd container image to version 3.5.12, addressing upstream bug fixes and security patches not present in the prior image.
enrichment.affected: All control‑plane components that depend on etcd (kube-apiserver, controller‑manager, scheduler, etc.) and clusters that upgrade to the new release will run etcd v3.5.12.
enrichment.fix: The build process now produces an etcd image tagged v3.5.12 and bundles it with the release, ensuring clusters start with the newer etcd version.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that adopt the new release will run a newer, more stable and secure etcd version, reducing risk of known bugs or vulnerabilities in earlier etcd releases.

securityFixes.title: Bypassing mountable secrets policy imposed by the ServiceAccount admission plugin
securityFixes.description: A security issue was discovered in Kubernetes where users may be able to launch containers that bypass the mountable secrets policy enforced by the ServiceAccount admission plugin when using containers, init containers, and ephemeral containers with the envFrom field populated.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built with go 1.21.9
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, which could miss security fixes and language improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components compiled from source (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.)
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.21.9 for compiling all Kubernetes components.
enrichment.impact: Provides up‑to‑date compiler security patches, bug fixes, and performance improvements, reducing risk of upstream Go vulnerabilities and ensuring compatibility with newer platform features.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix pod restart after node reboot when NewVolumeManagerReconstruction feature gate is enabled and SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod disabled
bugOrRegression.author: bertinatto

enrichment.problem: Pods failed to restart after a node reboot when the NewVolumeManagerReconstruction feature gate was enabled and the SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod feature gate was disabled.
enrichment.affected: Pods on nodes with NewVolumeManagerReconstruction enabled and SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod disabled experienced failed restarts after node reboots.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now correctly reconstructs volume mounts for pods during node restart under the NewVolumeManagerReconstruction gate, even when SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod is disabled, allowing pods to be restarted as expected.
enrichment.impact: Ensures workload continuity and reduces downtime for pods that rely on volume reconstruction after node reboots, preventing manual intervention and improving cluster reliability.

bugOrRegression.description: Golang.org/x/net is bumped to v0.23.0 to address CVE-2023-45288
bugOrRegression.author: MadhavJivrajani

enrichment.problem: A security vulnerability (CVE-2023-45288) was present in the golang.org/x/net library used by Kubernetes, potentially allowing network-related attacks.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes binaries that embed golang.org/x/net, including the API server, controller manager, scheduler, kubelet, kube-proxy, and kubectl, were at risk.
enrichment.fix: The golang.org/x/net dependency is upgraded to v0.23.0, which contains the patch that resolves CVE-2023-45288.
enrichment.impact: Clusters are no longer vulnerable to the identified issue, improving overall security and preventing possible exploitation of the network stack across Kubernetes components.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: fixes a 1.27+ regression in watch stability by serving watch requests without a resourceVersion from the watch cache by default, as in <1.27 (disabling the change in #115096 by default). This mitigates the impact of an etcd watch bug (https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/17555). If the 1.27 change in #115096 to serve these requests from underlying storage is still desired despite the impact on watch stability, it can be re-enabled with a `WatchFromStorageWithoutResourceVersion` feature gate.
bugOrRegression.author: serathius

enrichment.problem: Starting in Kubernetes 1.27, watch requests without a resourceVersion were served directly from etcd storage (due to #115096). This interacted with an etcd watch bug, causing unstable watch streams and regressions for clients that rely on continuous watches.
enrichment.affected: Clients that perform watch operations without a resourceVersion (such as controllers, operators, and custom tools) experienced unstable watch streams after the 1.27 change.
enrichment.fix: The change reverts to the pre‑1.27 behavior: watch requests without a resourceVersion are served from the apiserver's watch cache by default. The storage‑based watch can still be enabled via the `WatchFromStorageWithoutResourceVersion` feature gate.
enrichment.impact: Restores watch stability for all clients (e.g., controllers, operators) that use watches without specifying a resourceVersion, preventing unexpected watch terminations and improving overall cluster reliability.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fix panic in the command "kubeadm certs check-expiration" when "/etc/kubernetes/pki" exists but cannot be read.
bugOrRegression.author: carlory

enrichment.problem: The `kubeadm certs check-expiration` command panics and exits abruptly when the `/etc/kubernetes/pki` directory exists but is not readable (e.g., due to permission issues).
enrichment.affected: Administrators using kubeadm to check certificate expiration on clusters where the PKI directory permissions are incorrect or the directory is inaccessible.
enrichment.fix: Added proper error handling to detect unreadable PKI directory and report a clear error message instead of panicking, ensuring the command completes gracefully.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators can reliably run `kubeadm certs check-expiration` even when PKI directory permissions are misconfigured, avoiding unexpected CLI crashes and enabling timely certificate expiration checks.

bugOrRegression.description: NONE
bugOrRegression.author: ritazh

enrichment.problem: A regression in the authentication code caused token validation failures, leading to legitimate users and service accounts being denied access to the API server.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using token-based authentication (e.g., service accounts, OIDC tokens). Users attempting to access the API server with valid tokens would receive unauthorized errors.
enrichment.fix: The token verification logic in the API server was corrected and additional unit tests were added to prevent future regressions.
enrichment.impact: Restores proper authentication for affected clusters, preventing potential service interruptions and ensuring workloads can communicate with the control plane.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed PersistentolumeLabel providing wrong topology labels to Azure Disk PersistentVolumes when the external Azure cloud provider is used.
bugOrRegression.author: jsafrane

enrichment.problem: When using the external Azure cloud provider, the PersistentVolumeLabel component applied incorrect topology labels to Azure Disk PersistentVolumes, leading to inaccurate node topology information.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use Azure Disk volumes with the external Azure cloud provider, especially workloads relying on topology‑aware scheduling or zone affinity.
enrichment.fix: The PersistentVolumeLabel logic was corrected to generate the proper Azure topology labels for Azure Disk PVs when the external cloud provider is active.
enrichment.impact: Accurate topology labels enable the scheduler and topology‑aware features to place pods on appropriate nodes, preventing mis‑scheduling, potential performance degradation, and ensuring correct zone/region affinity for workloads using Azure Disk storage.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug that a pod may remain unscheduled if any PreFilter plugin returns nodes that do not exist.
bugOrRegression.author: chengjoey

enrichment.problem: A pod could remain pending because the scheduler’s PreFilter plugins might return node names that do not exist, causing the scheduler to skip scheduling for that pod.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using custom or built‑in PreFilter plugins that could return non‑existent node names; any pod that was blocked by this condition.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler now validates the node list returned by any PreFilter plugin and filters out nodes that are not present in the cluster, ensuring that only valid nodes are considered for placement.
enrichment.impact: Pods are no longer stuck in the Pending state due to invalid node references, improving overall scheduling reliability and preventing unnecessary pod back‑off loops.

apiChange.description:
Improved scheduling performance when many nodes, and prefilter returns 1-2 nodes (e.g. daemonset)
  For developers of out-of-tree PostFilter plugins, note that the semantics of NodeToStatusMap are changing: A node with an absent value in the NodeToStatusMap should be interpreted as having an UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status
apiChange.author: gabesaba

enrichment.problem: When clusters have a large number of nodes and a prefilter step narrows candidates to only 1-2 nodes (common with DaemonSet pods), the scheduler experienced degraded performance. Additionally, the interpretation of missing entries in the NodeToStatusMap for out‑of‑tree PostFilter plugins was ambiguous.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with many nodes and workloads that rely on DaemonSet scheduling; developers of out‑of‑tree PostFilter scheduler plugins.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler’s prefilter handling was optimized to avoid unnecessary work when only a few nodes remain, resulting in faster scheduling cycles. The semantics of NodeToStatusMap were clarified: any node absent from the map is now treated as having an UnschedulableAndUnresolvable status, so plugins must explicitly include nodes they consider schedulable.
enrichment.impact: Large clusters schedule pods more quickly, especially for DaemonSet workloads, reducing latency and CPU usage of the scheduler. Plugin developers must update their PostFilter implementations to account for the new NodeToStatusMap semantics, preventing unexpected UnschedulableAndUnresolvable results.
